eugeniosegala/mako.name: MAKO Decky v5.0.0
eugeniosegala/mako.body: > Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v5.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v5.0.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v5.0.0 ### Release codename: Phoenix > _“Where the phoenix lit the drowned stones, the mako found a way through.”_ > > **Mira Valen, _Charts of the Ember Tide_** --- Phoenix brings bundled MAKO FG to MAKO Decky through the matching Renderer: open-weight Frame Generation for SteamOS and Linux. At 3×, shared motion work can turn 30 FPS into 90 FPS when the game and GPU sustain it; 2×, 4× and other output schedules are also supported. Free for non-commercial use, with no Lossless Scaling required. See the [model card](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/mako-fg/MODEL_CARD.md) for design, benchmarks and limitations, or download the model and runtime from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/eugeniosegala/MAKO-FG). - **MAKO FG:** V1.24 supports Fixed and Adaptive Frame Generation, SDR, HDR and Flow Scale, including self-contained AppImages. It is the default for profiles without a saved model, including profiles from earlier releases. Developed by Eugenio Segala. See the [setup guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/MAKO-FG.md). - **Pick a Frame Generation model:** Choose **MAKO FG**, **LSFG Quality** or **LSFG Performance** per profile and power mode. Switching between MAKO FG and LSFG needs a restart; LSFG Quality and Performance switch live. LSFG and LS1 still require your own Lossless Scaling installation. - **Clearer model availability:** Unavailable Lossless Scaling choices are grayed out; MAKO FG and MAKO Scaler stay usable. Failed LSFG starts fall back to MAKO FG without changing the saved choice. A missing DLL keeps that choice with a warning; the editor changes it only when a present DLL fails validation. Live Status shows the running model. - **MAKO FG performance controls:** Flow Scale trades motion detail for GPU cost. Ultra Performance uses 60% Flow Scale and MAKO Scaler when Scaling is on. Supports frames up to 8,294,400 pixels (the area of 3840×2160) and 8192 pixels per side; the analysis grid may be capped at higher resolutions. - **MAKO FG Mode:** Quality, Balanced, Performance and Extra Performance switch live and control how often motion is fully estimated at 2× and 3×. Balanced and Performance correct motion between full estimates; Extra Performance uses cheaper reuse when frames arrive evenly and correction otherwise. Start with Balanced; try Quality for artifacts in fast motion. At 4× and above, every pair gets a full estimate. Ultra Performance uses at least Performance. - **MAKO Scaler by default:** Profiles without a saved scaling method use MAKO Scaler; existing choices stay. The Renderer improves eligible scaling and HDR bridge paths. - **Capture frames for comparison:** Arm burst or rolling capture, then press L3 + R3 to save real frames locally. Rolling mode buffers recent frames until saved; burst pauses Frame Generation. The game also receives the button press. See [recording setup and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/MAKO-FG.md#record-test-frames). - **Mailbox Presentation:** Optional compatibility setting for FIFO hangs or failures, off by default. Requires a restart. Where supported, newer frames replace queued ones, which may reduce smoothness. - **MangoHud real FPS:** **Count Real Frames Only** excludes generated frames from MangoHud's FPS counter. Requires a restart and host-installed MangoHud; cannot run alongside MAKO Shaders. - **Adaptive and bridge pacing:** Skips recovery probes that cannot succeed, handles Gamescope timing drift, and restores normal Adaptive pacing within seconds when a game's clock outpaces the display at the chosen multiplier. - **OpenGL games through Zink:** Fixes swapchain failures and uneven pacing after loading screens. With Base FPS Cap off and a known Gamescope refresh, Fixed mode paces eligible Zink games at refresh divided by the multiplier; Dynamic Cadence Recovery keeps that cap off. Workarounds also address colour speckles and tearing. See [compatibility settings and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#compatibility-and-external-tools). - **Even pacing on the desktop:** Outside Gamescope, generated frames are spaced evenly when total output is below display refresh, helping capped games and low-FPS video at some added latency. Game Mode is unchanged. - **Non-Steam games and AppImages:** Fixes Frame Generation under Steam's older Vulkan loader and shader pre-caching layer, plus related X11 window crashes. - **Proton 8 and 9 offscreen windows:** Applies Wine's workaround on the first enabled launch, fixing offscreen Frame Generation in games such as Half-Life 2. If video or UI displays incorrectly, add `WINE_DISABLE_VK_CHILD_WINDOW_RENDERING_HACK=0` before `mako-run`. Other Proton versions may use different paths; see [setup and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#proton-offscreen-windows). - **MAKO FG in games with large per-thread data:** Fixes MAKO FG startup in games with large thread-local allocations, including some native ports. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. Compare Fixed, Adaptive, and scaling-only modes one at a time. If a feature does not work, try Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed. For Scaling, test in-game resolutions and check that Live Status shows Input smaller than Display. - **Adaptive target:** Adaptive aims for an average frame rate; it cannot lower a game’s native rate or exceed available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and latency. Smooth Cadence may trade responsiveness for steadier motion. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Only the optional Lossless Scaling frame generation model and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. MAKO FG, the open MAKO Scaler, and bundled shaders do not require it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v5.0.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 5.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v5.0.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use a Lossless Scaling frame generation model or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `5.0.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v5.0.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v5.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v5.0.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v5.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v5.0.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

Synthetic results; game FPS and Steam Deck gains were not measured. Buffer memory excludes model weights, shared images, driver memory and game VRAM._ - **GPU Headroom:** Under **Performance**, choose a 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% GPU reserve and adjust it live during Frame Generation. The matching Renderer gradually reduces real FPS using supported AMD utilization readings. Adaptive can add generated frames within its ceiling; Fixed can lower output FPS. Off by default, saved per profile and power mode, and mutually exclusive with Dynamic Cadence Recovery. Brief spikes can still reach 100%, and unavailable telemetry leaves normal pacing active. - **Faster Frame Generation:** The matching Renderer reduces CPU and GPU overhead in Fixed and Adaptive with FP16 or FP32. The chart above compares Quality and Lighter throughput and GPU time with v4.5.0. In-game gains depend on the game, hardware and settings. - **More efficient FP16 Quality:** The matching Renderer automatically uses a leaner compute path for supported native FP16 Quality models on AMD’s RADV driver, preserving model weights, precision and Flow Scale without adding image buffers. It applies to Fixed and Adaptive, bridge and non-bridge, with VRR on or off. Enable **Allow FP16** and leave **Lighter FG Model** and **Ultra Performance** off. Steam Deck and other AMD/RADV handhelds can use this path; their performance gains have not yet been measured. - **Lower overhead for Quality and Lighter:** The matching Renderer spends less CPU time submitting GPU work in Fixed 2× and Adaptive steps that produce one generated frame. This applies automatically with either model, FP16 or FP32, and bridge or non-bridge modes, preserving image quality and Flow Scale. - **Lower FG working-buffer memory:** Generated outputs share temporary image storage, reducing private buffer allocations at higher multipliers. The chart includes unchanged 800p 2× controls and measures FG working buffers rather than total MAKO or game VRAM. - **Less CPU work for Scaling and Shaders:** The matching Renderer reuses scaling preparation, and the bundled shader system reduces temporary allocations during frame presentation. Your scaling method, sharpness, shader effects and effect order are preserved. - **Adaptive and FIFO stability:** The matching Renderer preserves proven Adaptive workloads after brief image-availability misses and retains qualified Smooth Cadence pacing through short cadence dips. Sustained slowdowns and unsuccessful higher-multiplier trials still trigger the existing safeguards. - **More reliable multiplier checks:** Adaptive checks the real-frame cost after pacing settles and refreshes older comparisons when needed. Brief bursts of queued frames no longer repeatedly restart these checks. When both workloads reach the target, MAKO prefers the lower multiplier. - **Better use of frame-cap waits:** Eligible capped Fixed and Adaptive paths coordinate frame preparation with output timing, including supported Scaling and bridge paths, avoiding consecutive pacing waits while preserving your configured cap. - **Gamescope timing compatibility:** The matching Renderer improves bridge feedback handling, VRR timing interpretation and presentation deadlines. Newer Gamescope reports and optional Vulkan timing on non-bridge surfaces are used when supported, with existing pacing retained otherwise. This does not require replacing SteamOS’s Gamescope. - **Customize shaders per game:** Select **Customize shaders** to adjust selected bundled and compatible custom effects with sliders, toggles, choices and colour controls. **Reset shader to defaults** restores the selected effect. - **Live shader adjustments:** Changes save with the selected profile and are shared across its AC and battery modes. They apply live when Shaders was enabled at game launch; rebuilding an effect may cause a brief hitch. The editor opens beside the game, and **Hide controls** collapses it while comparing results. - **Clearer shader controls:** Palettes such as Nostalgia’s **Custom palette** use colour swatches, sliders and exact-value fields. Sliders follow the author’s step size with consistent controller increments. Numeric fields hide floating-point display noise without changing stored values or saving untouched fields. - **Smoother controller navigation:** Focused controls stay visible when entering settings tabs or leaving the effects list. Collapsing the list reveals the next focused action without restoring stale scroll positions. Unavailable actions are skipped, and closing the shader editor returns to the selected MAKO section in Decky’s Quick Access panel. - **Shared MangoHud layouts:** Profiles with MangoHud enabled can use an optional `~/.config/mako-render/mangohud.conf`, shared with the standalone Renderer launcher. Creating or removing it takes effect on the next game launch without resaving profiles. Keep the usual `mako-run %command%` launch option. Requires host-installed MangoHud; Flatpak games and simultaneous Shaders remain unsupported. - **Native FPS above the Adaptive target:** With **Fractional Adaptive** and **Automatic** Real Frame Priority, sustained native FPS can exceed **Target FPS** without generation when **Base FPS Cap** is off or at least the target. Manual caps remain enforced. - **More complete translations:** Performance, HDR, scaling and Remote Play controls have more consistent translated labels and explanations across MAKO Decky and the configuration app. Thanks to [Tak-attack](https://github.com/Tak-attack) for the Japanese improvements in [PR #91](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/91). - **Better support reports:** With diagnostics enabled, MAKO Decky retains ten launch sessions instead of five. Reports preserve Wayland errors and multi-line failure details in Steam’s timestamped logs, identify failed presentation waits and available timing capabilities, and keep MAKO Wiz’s guide links usable from GitHub issue comments. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. By morning, the storm had drawn a course around us.”_ > > **Mira Valen, _Charts of the Last Fleet_** --- Maelstrom adds experimental HDR, AC/battery settings, display-aware Adaptive targets, custom shaders and native Steam Remote Play, with new Steam Overlay controls and broader Flatpak support. - **Experimental HDR:** HDR10/PQ and linear scRGB now work with Scaling, Frame Generation and Shaders through Gamescope, on external HDR displays. **HDR Quality** offers Quality, Balanced and Performance (default), trading precision and motion detail for speed while preserving output resolution. See [HDR setup](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#hdr). - **Window-mode stability:** Scaling, Frame Generation and HDR share swapchain retirement and resize recovery. Returning from native display resolution retains a proven output size, and HDR Quality updates the internal HDR resize live with Scaling off. - **AC and battery settings:** Enable separate Handheld and Docked settings for each profile, then edit either set or Base settings. The matching Renderer follows battery or AC power automatically while playing, even with the panel closed. Switching sets preserves shared shader edits and keeps native settings separate; normal restart requirements still apply. - **Match Display Refresh Rate:** Let Adaptive follow Gamescope's current refresh rate instead of a fixed target. Your manual target is kept as the fallback; turn matching off to edit it. Live Status shows the effective target. The option can differ between AC and battery settings. - **Custom shaders:** Add compatible ReShade `.fx` files, then select and order them alongside bundled effects. Selection, ordering and deletion apply live while Shaders is active; **Refresh** reloads edited files and dependencies. Failed edits keep the previous chain running. The picker has more reliable paging, scrolling and controller focus. Flatpak games need access to the original files and dependencies. - **Lossless Scaling is optional:** MAKO Scaler and Shaders work through the installed Renderer without it. All profile controls remain editable; only Frame Generation and LS1 require Lossless Scaling. - **Clearer FP16 controls:** Allow FP16 applies to LSFG and MAKO Scaler across profiles and presets; LS1 always stays FP32, and shader effects keep their own precision behavior. Model warnings explain unavailable native FP16. Restart the game after changing precision. - **Native Steam Remote Play:** Stream on the receiving native x86_64 Linux Steam client using your selected profile and optional AC/battery settings. Create a named copy during a stream; normal live/restart rules apply. Qt and Decky share client restoration and current shader selections. Requires system Python 3.11 or newer; standalone Steam Link, Flatpak Steam and browser streaming are unsupported. Stream quality and latency still need qualification. Thanks to [Hugo Uchôas Borges](https://github.com/hugouchoasborges) for the contribution. - **Disable Steam Overlay (Restart):** New per-profile Performance control, enabled by default. May reduce stutter; disables Steam's in-game overlay and FPS counter and may affect Steam Input. Gaming Mode menus and performance overlay remain available. - **Better profile capture:** Launcher and helper processes cannot stand in for the game or select another game's profile through old aliases. Ubisoft Connect, CD Projekt RED, Rockstar helpers and EA app windows remain excluded while their games stay eligible. - **Non-Steam menu handling:** Steam and Quick Access menus pause generated frames on supported non-Steam launches, including Heroic/UMU shortcuts. Works across Fixed and Adaptive modes, with or without Scaling. - **Flatpak support:** Flatpak Setup now includes Freedesktop 26.08 extensions alongside 23.08–25.08. Automatic host discovery applies VRR On/Off requests to the game's verified Gamescope session during Frame Generation. Requires a VRR-capable display; Follow Steam and manual Steam changes retain their existing priority. - **Adaptive stability:** Steam menu returns preserve multiplier retry cooldowns. Failed Smooth Cadence reductions keep their retry delay across stalls and menu returns. Higher-multiplier pacing is rechecked against its real-frame cost. Brief native-only recovery samples restore the automatic base cap and generated workload before checking recovery. - **Frame pacing and recovery:** The matching Renderer improves capped Fractional spacing, completion pacing and recovery from retired Gamescope scaling swapchains, while keeping native fallback responsive. Scaling and HDR preserve games’ presentation-wait support while adapting output timing to compositor feedback. - **Shader overhead:** The bundled vkBasalt reduces per-frame CPU work and preserves ReShade effect settings. Effect GPU cost still increases with the Frame Generation multiplier. - **Clearer guides and reports:** Setup, configuration, Remote Play, Flatpak and troubleshooting guides are shorter. Diagnostic instructions now request 5,000 lines; reports retain startup, state and process/GPU health context. - **German interface:** MAKO Decky now follows Steam's German interface language with a complete translated catalog. Thanks to [Hu2ki3](https://github.com/Hu2ki3) for contributing German support to the Renderer configuration app in [PR #77](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/77). - **Russian interface:** MAKO Decky now follows Steam’s Russian language setting. Thanks to [rosakodu](https://github.com/rosakodu) and the Decky Loader Russia community for [PR #83](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/83). - **Japanese translations:** Clearer shader controls, installation messages, and explanations. Thanks to [Tak-attack](https://github.com/Tak-attack) for [PR #71](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/71). ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. Compare Fixed, Adaptive, and scaling-only modes one at a time. If a feature does not work, try Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed. eugeniosegala/mako.body: > Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v4.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v4.0.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v4.0.0 ### Release codename: Inferno > _“The flames painted the sea in colors no sailor had a name for.”_ > > **Captain Matteo Veyr, _Chronicles of the Last Fleet_** --- MAKO Decky 4.0 adds per-game shaders and ordered effect stacks through MAKO's managed vkBasalt fork. Install MAKO Renderer from the plugin to get the matching layer; a separate vkBasalt installation is unnecessary. - **Shaders and effects:** Profiles offer sharpening, anti-aliasing, 20% default DLS denoise, and curated colour, contrast, cinematic, and retro effects, including new Clarity and Levels Plus shaders. Combine effects in your chosen order; each extra pass can increase GPU cost. Native 64-bit and 32-bit games and prepared Flatpak apps are supported. - **Live controls and custom chains:** Supported shader settings update while you play. Default and saved profiles retain editable vkBasalt configuration files for custom chains and ReShade-compatible effects. Layer activation and manual configuration edits take effect after restarting the game. - **Image Processing and Live Status:** Frame Generation, Scaling, and Shaders have separate tabs. Live Status shows active modes, limits, fallbacks, and input and display resolutions. - **Frame Generation pause:** **Enable Frame-gen (Restart)** loads Frame Generation at launch; select `0x` to pause or resume it while playing. Steam and Decky menus pause generated frames automatically while real frames and scaling continue. - **Fractional real-frame priority:** Choose **Automatic**, **Low**, **Medium**, **High**, or **Very High**. Automatic keeps the previous behavior; other levels estimate a real-frame cap from Target FPS without changing your saved manual Base FPS Cap. The displayed cap is an estimate, not a guaranteed frame rate. - **VRR and pacing:** Follow Steam uses Gamescope's VRR state for eligible pacing modes without resetting the Adaptive level. Fixed Smooth Cadence and stable Steady 2x also gain ordered pacing without VRR. - **Scaling with Frame Generation:** Improved frame delivery reduces stalls when the two features run together. The frame rate shown in-game may sit slightly below the selected target. - **Adaptive and recovery:** Adaptive avoids raising the multiplier when it already reaches at least 98% of the target, and backs off after an unsustainable promotion. Recovery responds to frame-acquisition deadlines rather than ordinary slow rendering; eligible resolution changes can retry resource allocation once. - **Steam Desktop FPS counter:** Native and Proton Steam launches retain Steam's Vulkan overlay with MAKO's managed layers in Desktop Mode. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. Compare Fixed, Adaptive, and scaling-only modes one at a time. If a feature does not work, try Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed. For Scaling, test in-game resolutions and check that Live Status shows Input smaller than Display. - **Adaptive target:** Adaptive aims for an average frame rate; it cannot lower a game’s native rate or exceed available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and latency. Smooth Cadence may trade responsiveness for steadier motion. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Frame Generation and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. The open MAKO Scaler does not use it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v4.0.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 4.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v4.0.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Known limitation - **HDR frame generation and scaling are unavailable:** MAKO Decky does not expose the engine’s HDR path yet; in-game HDR controls may be unavailable. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use Frame Generation or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `4.0.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v4.0.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v4.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v4.0.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v4.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v4.0.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

eugeniosegala/mako.body: > Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v3.3.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v3.3.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v3.3.0 ### Release codename: Neptune Fury > _“The realms of ocean and the fields of air are mine, not his.”_ > > **Virgil, _The Aeneid_, Book I, translated by John Dryden** --- - **Independent upscaling:** Scaling no longer enables Gamescope WSI automatically. Supported 64-bit and 32-bit Gamescope games can upscale with WSI off. - **Lower CPU and memory use:** The updated MAKO Renderer reduces CPU overhead and RAM/VRAM use, with improved memory handling during resolution changes. - **Smoother Frame Generation cadence:** Smooth Cadence is on by default and uses validated ordered Gamescope presentation to stabilize delivery. Fractional Adaptive retains real frames, while Fixed and Steady Base Cap can favor an even cadence at the cost of real-frame rate and responsiveness; turn it off per game if preferred. - **A cleaner panel:** Press R1 for a compact view that retains Live Status and warnings. Centered headings, solid deep-blue dividers and preserved controller focus make navigation clearer. - **Clearer model warnings:** See LS1 and LSFG compatibility problems together, with troubleshooting guidance and separate instructions when Lossless Scaling is missing. - **Improved Japanese translations:** Translated scaling and Live Status messages, with consistent control names and updated Adaptive guidance across MAKO Decky and MAKO Renderer. Thanks to [Tak-attack](https://github.com/Tak-attack) for [PR #64](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/64). - **Clearer vkBasalt integration:** Updated controls and documentation cover 64-bit and 32-bit use, with a separate matching installation and links to official effect configuration guidance. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try the game’s V-Sync setting both on and off.** It can make frame delivery feel steadier, but may also add input lag or clash with the game’s FPS cap, VRR, or compositor. Every game is different: compare both options and keep the one that feels smoother and more responsive. Every game, renderer, and display setup behaves differently. Compare Fixed Frame Generation, Adaptive Frame Generation, and scaling-only operation one setting at a time. For most games, fullscreen is the best starting point for performance and frame pacing. Keep the configuration that feels best for that game. - **Adaptive target behaviour:** Adaptive varies the generated-frame count toward an average target. It cannot reduce a native frame rate already above that target, and the result still depends on the selected multiplier plus available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency tuning:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and input latency. Smooth Cadence may improve motion consistency while reducing responsiveness, so compare the available choices per game. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Frame Generation and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. The open MAKO Scaler does not use it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v3.3.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Preferred clean update:** To prevent Decky retaining an older backend or bundled payload, uninstall **MAKO Decky**, install the newer ZIP, restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine, then open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer**. This also resolves cases where Decky does not show or reload the plugin after installation. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 3.3.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v3.3.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Known limitation - **HDR frame generation and scaling are unavailable in this Decky release:** The engine foundation is included, but the plugin locks HDR exposure off and does not provide a per-game opt-in. In-game HDR controls may be unavailable by design. A later release can unlock the path after activation, presentation, colour, and performance are validated across games. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use Frame Generation or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `3.3.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v3.3.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v3.3.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v3.3.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v3.3.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v3.3.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.name: v0.14.1 The LSFG-VK 2.0.0 Update
xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.body: This release is a ground-up rewrite of Decky LSFG-VK, focused on better alignment and integration with [LSFG-VK 2.0.0](https://lsfg-vk.dev/). > This release changes how per-game profiles are created and managed. Existing v1 profiles are not compatible with this release and will need to be recreated. **New Layout and Automatic Organization** - Separate tabs for Steam Games, Non-Steam Games, Flatpaks, Settings, Config File (optional debug) - Collapsible lists that automatically organize by LSFG-VK enabled games and not-yet enabled - No more copy-pasting launch commands for each game! - Enabling a Steam or Non-Steam game will automatically configures its steam launch options while preserving existing launch arguments. - Streamlined flatpack integration and cleanup, does not require any manual launcher pastes in `target` section. - Enable All and Remove All actions for each category - Steam Deck "Game Mode" specific workarounds section better organized and managed in conjunction with LSFG-VK 2.0.0 config on a per application basis automatically. - LSFG-VK per-app config properly implemented by Steam AppIDs for automatic per-profile management. **Reworked Profiles** - Reworked Flatpak support with per-app profiles and improved application detection - Steam and Non-Steam games are automatically patched and unpatched as profiles are enabled or removed - Added detection and repair of broken/missing wrapper configuration **Now Playing Tab** - Added a Now Playing view that automatically follows the currently running game - When an enrolled game is detected to be running, automatically open a Now Playing tab, with only the applicable controls that apply in real time while game is running (FPS Multiplier, Performance Mode, Flow Scale etc) - When a non Steam shortcut such as an EmuDeck ROM or Heroic launcher game is running through an LSFG-VK-enabled Flatpak, the Now Playing tab automatically identifies the underlying Flatpak and exposes its real-time frame gen controls. **Misc** - Simplified LSFG-VK installation, configuration, and cleanup - Automatic conflict resolution with previously patched games - Higher multiplier options for Steam OS devices with higher HZ rates (ex 40 native FPS * 6x to saturate a 240hz monitor) - Moved FP16 acceleration to global option in settings tab, to more correctly follow lsfg-vk config conventions. - Better uninstallation cleanup discipline in-plugin and through Decky uninstall. > it is still recommended to first "Uninstall LSFG-VK" from plugin settings, then uninstall from Decky settings, in order to properly unpatch steam launch options before removing plugin overall **This is a major change from previous iterations of the plugin. Big reports and feedback on the new layout are greatly appreciated in Github Issues or the plugin Discord**

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.8.0
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: # UNIFIDECK v0.8.0 **Added support for Xbox PC game downloads, fully native Steam game details layout, and integrated achievement and unlock popups** ## New Features - **Added Xbox PC games (experimental).** Install and play the PC games you own on Xbox or through PC Game Pass, with achievements, offline play and cloud saves. You can turn it on and sign in from Unifideck's settings. Thanks massively to [Xodus](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/xodus) and [Nexus Launcher](https://github.com/domsvoboda/nexus-launcher) projects. - **UI Update** Game pages now use Steam's own layout and UI, including the download bar, cloud play and achievements. - **Added** Steam-style achievement popups for Epic, GOG and Xbox games. GOG achievements are tracked faster with Comet v0.4.1 bump. - **Added** a version picker for Battle.net games with more than one edition installed on the same shortcut. - **Changed** Xbox Cloud Gaming to play streams in Unifideck's own player instead of via Edge. The Microsoft Edge Flatpak is now replaced by a built-in browser. - **Added** Xbox Cloud Gaming for accounts without Game Pass. Free-to-play streams such as Fortnite now sync. - **Added** cloud saves for native Linux GOG games. - **Added** a prompt to claim an itch.io bundle game before installing it, with a button that opens the claim page. - **Added** Steam review scores and tags to game pages. - **Improved** download time estimates so they no longer jump around as often with unstable speeds. ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** sync replacing the names of games you renamed in Steam. - **Fixed** TabMaster tabs built from Unifideck collections breaking after a sync. - **Fixed** the sync progress bar freezing just before the end of a sync. - **Fixed** missing descriptions and publishers on some game pages. - **Fixed** every game crashing when GE-Proton's files were damaged after install. Unifideck now checks and repairs them automatically. - **Fixed** large itch.io libraries timing out during sync, and itch.io sign-ins whose API key cannot read the library. - **Fixed** native Linux GOG games always showing an update, and updates installing the Windows version. - **Fixed** GameVault downloads failing with "That compression method is not supported". - **Fixed** GameVault games with a native Linux build installing without anything to launch. Thanks @kergoth - **Fixed** the Steam Store banner saying you own every Battle.net game, such as Overwatch 2. Thanks @kmturley - **Fixed** the store switcher on a game page showing outdated stores after a sync, and "Group duplicates" occasionally showing the wrong tiles. Thanks @kmturley - **Fixed** itch.io installs failing at the end when your Games folder is a link to an SD card. Thanks @kmturley - **Improved** DirectX 12 games by keeping their shader cache between launches. - **Improved** security: Xbox sign-in now verifies Microsoft's certificates, and itch.io browser games run in their own browser profile, separate from your store sign-ins. Thanks @kmturley **Notes** - If you are already logged in to Microsoft, you might be logged out once you enable experimental Xbox PC. Also, you will need to login twice in the same window. - Warcraft III: Reforged now needs GE-Proton11-7 or newer to sign in. Unifideck tells you if your selected Proton is too old. Thanks @kmturley - Paid itch.io browser games ask you to sign in to itch.io once more, inside the game window. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Special thanks to @kmturley and @kergoth for their contributions to this release, and to everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing, specifically @opsidao, @tall_dumb_guy, @kev.benjam, @reactivefuture. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)! If you like our work, please support the project - https://ko-fi.com/mubaraknumann

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.6
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: # UNIFIDECK v0.7.6 **Added itch.io** as a new store, game de-dupe across stores, and a way to highlight games that you already own on other stores (happy autumn sale!) ## New Features - **Added itch.io.** Sign in through the usual login window to install linux and windows games. You can also play HTML5 games via browser. If you want add Free games to your library, add them to a collection and they will show up after sync. - **Added** an "owned elsewhere" banner to Steam Store pages in Gaming Mode. It lists the other stores where you already own the game, and you can turn it off in the Quick Access Menu. - **Changed** Xbox sign-in to Microsoft's code-based sign-in to allow for broader entitlements, so the Steam Store banner can also show the Xbox games you own. - **Added** a "Group duplicates" option that shows a single tile for a game you own on several stores. Thanks @kmturley - **Added** Battle.net free-to-play and subscription games, such as World of Warcraft, Hearthstone and Heroes of the Storm, to your library. - **UI Update** The Quick Access Menu now uses Decky UI elements, with scrolling labels for long names. Thanks @kmturley ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** Steam crashing when a game's details page opened before Steam had finished loading it. - **Fixed** the Stop button not closing some games properly. - **Fixed** Warcraft III: Reforged sign-in failing with a "check your VPN" error. - **Fixed** other plugins and themes, such as Grey Uninstalled games (CSS Loader), TabMaster's Installed filter, etc seeing every Unifideck game as installed. Thanks @HoLuLuLu - **Fixed** library tabs still showing for stores you had signed out of. - **Fixed** games failing to launch when an incomplete GE-Proton was already on disk. Unifideck now downloads a fresh copy instead of reusing it. **Notes** - After this update, your Microsoft account will be logged out and you will need to login again with the new method. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Special thanks to @kmturley and @HoLuLuLu for their contributions to this release, and to everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.5
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: ### **UNIFIDECK v0.7.5** **Added GameVault** support, for installing and running DRM-Free games via Unifideck. ## New Features - **Added GameVault**, so you can browse and install from your own GameVault server or from local folder of game files (Thanks @stm85). See guide here - [Unifideck-GameVault-Setup.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32020645/Unifideck-GameVault-Setup.pdf) - **Added** support for GE-Proton installed outside Unifideck, such as through ProtonPlus. Unifideck can now use existing protons instead of downloading them again. Thanks @EricwanAR - **Added** a way to open logged in stores from the plugin UI. You can use the Cart icon to open the store's landing page/launcher. - **Improved** the plugin updater. UI is more compact now and update options open in a new popup. - **Added** a visible badge when Unifideck has stopped retrying a game that keeps failing to launch, with a button to reset it and try again. - **Added** better support for Steam Machine and its own tab and compatibility classifications. ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** games launching behind Steam's loading screen instead of coming to the front. - **Fixed** games starting without keyboard or controller focus in Gaming Mode. Thanks @stm85 - **Fixed** being signed out of your stores after switching Proton version. - **Fixed** a Ubisoft game launching the wrong title when two games shared an ID. - **Fixed** Ubisoft sign-in being lost when you played a different Ubisoft game. - **Fixed** Ubisoft installs reporting themselves finished before the download was done. - **Fixed** wrong artwork appearing on sequels and other same-series titles. - **Fixed** Battle.net sign-in failing in certain scenarios. - **Fixed** GOG game setup inheriting CheatDeck settings and hanging. Thanks @matheussilva421 - **Fixed** a finished install being marked cancelled, so the game never appeared in your library. - **Fixed** the Play button still offering Install for a game that had just finished installing. - **Fixed** a download row that could not be cancelled and never cleared. - **Fixed** cancelling a download leaving work running in the background. - **Fixed** an interrupted GE-Proton download leaving a broken copy behind. - **Fixed** selected Proton version not taking effect in some cases. Thanks @stm85 - **Fixed** manually added non-Steam shortcuts being removed by a library sync. - **Fixed** launch options support. - **Fixed** the Update button on the Downloads page showing no highlight on controller focus. Thanks @FreudsCAT - **Improved** sync so it skips work it already did and repairs metadata left behind by an interrupted run. **Notes** - If the plugin update installation gets stuck, please uninstall the plugin and install the attached installation file manually. - Restart Steam after a sync or cleanup so the library refreshes fully. - The bundled GOG CLI was updated, which seems to have fixed stalling GOG downloads. - Capture Logs now includes a short history of Unifideck's own memory use, which helps us diagnose slowdowns. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Thanks @HSNEM for the Arabic translations. Special thanks to @moi952, @kevbenjam, @uglierwan, mmmtimmah and everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing, development and documentation. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.40
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is now supported

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is out of "under construction". It was tested on a Legion Go 2 with the 12 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections (QoL & Extras, Henry From Skalitz, and Kingdom Come 2: Refined Experience). Each one was installed through the plugin from a clean game, loaded with no mod errors, and played from a save in Trosky.

Some mods were checked in game, not just loaded: Unlimited Saving II saves with F5, More Carry Weight raises the carry limit, and the Letters From Theresa quest starts on its own.

What the plugin handles for you:

- Mods go into the folder the game loads them from, and mods that update another mod lay over it as they do on Windows.
- LuaDB, the script library some mods need, is installed with any collection that needs it, along with the launch option that loads it under Proton.
- Mods that change game settings are combined into one settings file instead of replacing each other.
- A mod's "required mods" can be installed from its page in one go.

Smaller fixes:

- A collection's installed count now includes its optional mods.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.37
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor is supported, and Shadow of War is on the way

**Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor** \* is now supported, contributed by zomars (#48). Mods that replace the game's own files, loader dlls and `.arch05` archives all install from Gaming Mode:

- Files a mod replaces are backed up first, and come back when the mod is uninstalled or switched off. Two mods replacing the same file never cost you the original.
- Archive mods are registered in the game's archive list on install and taken out again on uninstall or switch-off.
- Mods that load through a proxy dll get the Proton launch option they need set for you, added to whatever launch options you already have.

**Middle-earth: Shadow of War** (on the roadmap, not yet supported) has its groundwork in, also from zomars (#47): the DLL Loader and Packet Loader as Step 1, with the game file the loader overwrites backed up and restored on reset, and the loader's console hidden so the game shows in Gaming Mode.

**ReShade keeps your launch options.** Installing a ReShade preset no longer replaces the game's launch options, and installing ReShade itself now adds its setting to what is already there instead of overwriting it.

\* Community added game. Not tested by author.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.34
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## See more from a mod's author, and mods that come back on their own

**Tap a mod's author to see their other mods** (#46). On a mod page the author's name is now a button: "by Name · more from this author". It opens the store showing all of their mods for that game. To return to every mod, press B, pick "All mods" in the Filter, or use "Show all mods".

**Mods switched off for a missing file come back once it is there** (#36). If a mod was switched off because a file it needs, such as `_ResourcePack.esl`, was not installed, it used to stay off even after the file arrived. Opening My Mods now switches those mods back on as soon as everything they need is on disk. Mods you switched off yourself, or ones switched off for crashing the game, stay off.

**Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, early support (under construction).** The 10 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections install and load on a Legion Go 2, and LuaDB is set up as the game's mod loader. It stays marked "under construction" until mods have been checked in game.

Smaller fixes:

- A missing mod loader is always shown in a collection's to-do list, even if it had been skipped earlier.
- A mod made of a single loose XML patch now says which file you need to apply by hand.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.29
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance is now supported

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is out of "under construction". It was tested on a Legion Go 2 with the 10 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections (Fun And Working 2024, Fun & Working 2022, and Realistic & Immersive Overhaul 2023): each one installed, loaded in the game, and played from a save in town.

Some mods were checked in game, not just loaded: Unlimited Saving adds a working Save Game to the pause menu, Unlimited Weight raises the carry limit, and SimpleHUD hides the HUD.

What the plugin handles for you:

- Mods go into the folder the game loads them from, and the game is stopped from moving that folder aside on its first launch with mods.
- Mods with an installer, and engine mods such as Better Rain, install like any other.
- Mods that change game settings are combined into one settings file instead of replacing each other.
- An engine mod's list of game files is added to the game's own list, so an older mod cannot drop the game's newest patch.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.28
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Search finds every mod again

Reported in issue #43. The plugin remembers mods it has seen fail on your exact game version and keeps them off the store's front page. It was also hiding them from search, so a mod could vanish even when you searched for it by name. On the reporter's Cyberpunk 2077 that was Virtual Atelier and many other popular mods.

Search now finds every mod. The front page still leaves out mods that failed on your game version.

## Switching a mod back on clears its "broken" mark

If the plugin marked a mod as broken and you switched it back on, the mark stayed until the next game update, even through a reset, so a mod you were happily using stayed hidden from the store. Switching a mod back on now clears the mark. If the mod really is broken, the plugin will notice again the next time you play.

## Problem reports say what kind of trouble

"Report a problem" now says how many marked mods are broken and how many just need an update, rather than one number for both.

bschelst/protondb-decky.body:
* Added several checks to help avoid future Decky errors, ensuring data is validated in case API servers change their data structure.
* Changed the submit button to an icon-only button.
* Added an analysis button showing a detailed ProtonDB-based summary of:

  * Game details, working/not working status, and confidence level.
  * Report history and trends.
  * Recent reports, limited to 20. More reports are available via the ProtonDB link.
  * Proton version summary based on reports, allowing users to see which Proton version has the best results.
* Added trend highlighting to the ProtonDB badge. For example, if new reports show degraded behaviour, a red line will be visible. If results improve, a green line will be visible.
* Added indicators to artwork and the library showing whether a game should work, is borked/not working, or is unknown:

  * Green: should work.
  * Red: borked/not working.
  * Grey: unknown.
* Added a setting to make badges on the game page rounded.
* Optimised caching to reduce ProtonDB/API stress and minimise resource usage on the Deck. Data may refresh more slowly as a result.
* Updated the instructions, including user-reported localisation changes.

michpalm/game-glance.body:
# Game Glance 4.0.0-rc.3

This release candidate improves Library Search and the Compact keyboard, restores menu blur over Steam Home on Anatase, and makes several menu controls more responsive.

- **Anatase Home frost.** The Steam Home menu can blur even when Gamescope and Steam omit HDR feedback. This was verified on an Anatase Steam Deck, handheld and docked. The in-game Gamescope blur still has its existing SDR requirements. [Issue #80](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/issues/80)
- **Compact keyboard.** Library Search uses the same Compact size as Social. The D-pad moves between keys and A selects the highlighted key. Hold A on the move strip and use the D-pad to reposition it. The Search keyboard is frosted when parked and suspends blur while moving.
- **Compact shortcuts.** Y inserts a space, X deletes, L2 shifts, R2 finishes, and L1/R1 move the text cursor. B closes the keyboard.
- **Library Search.** A brighter highlight with an inset outline makes the focused result easier to see. Closing Search clears the query and scroll position. Going back from results to edit keeps the query for that search.
- **Live sliders.** Quick Settings sends volume, microphone and brightness changes as the slider emits values. Performance does the same for frame limit. Writes are rate-limited during continuous input.
- **Spotlight Home.** B on the game row stays on Home.
- **Status bar → Profile style:** choose a simple **Dot** inside the status pill, or a **Circle** or **Square** avatar.

## Performance changes

- **Display.** Turning on **Disable Limit** switches the slider slot to **Refresh rate** when a display mode is available. Fixed displays show the current mode as read-only. The FPS cap supports intermediate whole-number values within the range Steam reports.
- **Live Performance sliders.** Refresh rate, overlay level, TDP limit, manual GPU clock, and Sharpness apply changes as the slider emits values. The first change is sent immediately, and subsequent writes are rate-limited during a drag. The value beside each slider follows your selection.

## Install or roll back

In **Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates → Choose version**, enable **Show prereleases**, select **4.0.0-rc.3**, and confirm through Decky. You can also install the attached `game-glance.zip` through Decky's **Install plugin from ZIP**. To roll back, choose a stable version from the same picker.

See the [first 4.0 prerelease](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/releases/tag/v4.0.0-rc.1) for the full feature overview and the known in-game screenshot issue.

michpalm/game-glance.name: 4.0.0-rc.1
michpalm/game-glance.body:
# Game Glance 4.0.0-rc.1

The first 4.0 prerelease brings library search and a redesigned menu to Steam Gaming Mode. I’m putting it out early to get feedback on how it feels to use with a controller on real devices.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e99edb54-c334-4485-859b-7b46baed088c

![The Game Glance menu over Home, on the Social section](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/blob/main/docs/images/4.0/menu-social.jpg)

## What’s new

- **Library Search.** Find games, demos, and shortcuts in your Steam library from the top bar and open their game pages. Dismiss the keyboard to browse the results, then select the search field to reopen it. Use Steam’s Store for store search.
- **Two controller keyboards.** Choose a movable Compact keyboard or a dual-stick Radial keyboard for Search and Social. The QWERTY-family radial layouts group letters by typing hand and row. Move the text cursor with the D-pad or arrow keys.
- **Optional Game Glance menu.** A frosted menu with pinning, Steam navigation shortcuts, Quick Settings, Performance, and an In game page with shortcuts for the running game. Supported controls depend on the device.
- **Social, Notifications, Soundtrack, and Plugins.** Open a direct Steam chat, act on notifications, control Steam soundtrack playback, and open Game Glance settings from the Plugins section.
- **Shared status bar and footer.** The same visual style carries across Home and game pages. With the interactive bar enabled, press Up from the game page’s Play row to enter it. Wi-Fi, battery, clock, and avatar open Internet, Power, System, and your Steam profile. Returning from a status shortcut preserves the selected Home game.
- **Optional Steam Settings restyle.** A compact layout with frosted artwork and native settings controls. Enable **Restyle Steam Settings** under **Game Glance → Menu** with the Game Glance menu enabled. The restyle defaults to off.
- **Choose version inside the menu.** **Game Glance → General → Choose version** lists published versions in the menu itself, with **Show prereleases** for test builds. Picking one hands over to Decky’s own confirmation. The same list is in **Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates**.
- **Visual and integration polish.** Clearer menu edges on dark scenes, adjustable Home and game-page shading, smoother handoffs, and improved Unifideck cloud and Resume/Stop controls.

## Install and roll back

From **Game Glance 3.6.1**, open **Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates → Choose version**, select **Show prereleases**, pick **4.0.0-rc.1** in the list, and select **Install 4.0.0-rc.1**. Decky asks you to confirm. Earlier versions need [3.6.1](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/releases/tag/v3.6.1) first, or the manual install below.

For a manual install:

1. Download the attached `game-glance.zip` and save it to your device.
2. In Gaming Mode, open **Decky → Settings → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP** and select the file. Enable Decky’s developer options if needed.
3. Open Game Glance settings to enable the menu and choose the features you want to try.

Automatic update checks stay on the stable channel. Prereleases are only installed when you choose one. To return to stable, open **Game Glance → General → Choose version** in the menu (or **Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates → Choose version**) and select **3.6.1**, or install the [stable 3.6.1 ZIP](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/releases/tag/v3.6.1) through Decky. Your settings are kept either way.

## Screenshots

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![Quick settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-quick-settings.jpg) | ![Performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-performance.jpg) |
| **Quick settings** | **Performance** |
| ![Social, with a Steam chat open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-social.jpg) | ![Soundtrack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-soundtrack.jpg) |
| **Social** (friend names blurred) | **Soundtrack** |
| ![Choosing the sections shown in the menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-configure.jpg) | ![Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michpalm/game-glance/bf970f5958dfe7aea44b2f4f1b2f8ebe92f4e846/docs/images/4.0/menu-plugins.jpg) |
| **Configure menu** | **Plugins** |

## Known issues

**Taking a screenshot with the in-game Game Glance menu open can restart Gaming Mode.** This has been reproduced on the ROG Ally running SteamOS 3.9.5 with compositor frost active. The crash can interrupt the running game. Close the menu and let it disappear before taking a Steam screenshot. [Upstream Gamescope ReShade screenshot issue](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/gamescope/issues/2416)

## Feedback

I’d especially like to hear how Search and the keyboards feel with a controller, whether the menu reads well on your display, and whether focus returns where you expect after opening a page or pressing B. Include your device, OS version, handheld or docked mode, and the steps that led to the issue. [Report an issue](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/issues/new/choose)

# Game Glance 3.6.1

This stable update adds an optional prerelease picker. Open **Game Glance → General → Choose version → Show prereleases** to see published test builds. Each test build is labelled **prerelease**, and Decky asks before installing it.

Automatic update checks continue to offer stable releases. If you try a prerelease and want to switch back, open **Choose version**, select a stable version, and confirm the downgrade in Decky.

otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.body:
# Changelog

## 1.7.0
- The panel shows a preview of the selected popup template under the template picker, an animated loop of the whole popup, drawn by the popup renderer itself (the slide in from the screen edge is not part of it). *Preview as* picks common, uncommon, rare or ultra rare. The Test buttons stay.

- New option: screenshot on unlock (off by default), with *Include the popup* and a *Test screenshot* button. Saved to `Pictures/Finally Achievements/Screenshots`.

otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.name: v1.6.3
otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.body:
## Near-instant popups and TV placement

Popups now appear about a second after an achievement is earned, instead of 10-15 seconds later.

### What changed since v1.6.2
- **Popups no longer wait on slow downloads.** The icon, unlock percentage, description and game art now load at the same time, and the popup waits for them at most 1 second. Anything slower is left out of that popup and saved for the next one. Before, each was waited for in turn with multi-second network timeouts, plus a gray-icon check and retries.
- **Unlocks are read the moment Steam writes them.** A change to Steam's `UserGameStats` file is read as soon as Linux reports it, instead of waiting for Steam's library data, which lags. The backup check now runs every 0.25 seconds instead of every second.
- **Downloads happen ahead of time.** When a game starts, its unlock percentages, game icon and art, and the icons of achievements still locked are downloaded and checked. An unlock's popup then reads them from disk.
- **Cheaper gray-icon check.** It runs in one helper that stays running instead of starting a new Python process per icon, and each icon's answer is saved.
- **Faster when a display fails.** A display setup the popup couldn't open on is skipped for 10 minutes instead of being tried first on every popup.
- **MangoApp is stopped earlier.** It now stops while the unlock sound's lead-in plays instead of after it.
- **TV placement fix.** With the popup screen size on "auto", popups use the screen size Steam's own interface reports, so they land in the right place on a TV.

otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.name: v1.6.2
otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.body:
A tester on a Steam Machine reported popups only appearing after pressing the Steam button, or 1–2 minutes late, and then with just a title.
The plugin now reads Steam’s own stats file directly, so an unlock should show up about a second after Steam writes it.
Names and descriptions now come from Steam’s local schema first. It has every language and includes secret achievements, so descriptions don’t go missing.
Nothing is shown twice if another detection path catches the unlock first.
Unlock history: a list of recent unlocks with the game, rarity and time. It starts from the day you install 1.6.0 and keeps the last 500. There are “Show more” and “Clear history” buttons.
Share card: select an unlock to make a 1200×630 image with the icon, name, description, rarity, game and date. It’s saved to Pictures/Finally Achievements and previewed in the panel. The plugin doesn’t post anywhere. You open or copy the file yourself.
Session summary: when you close a game, one popup such as “3 unlocked, 1 rare”. It only appears if you unlocked something.
Almost there alert: a popup such as “Only 2 achievements left”. You set the count from 1 to 5, and it fires once per count. It skips finished games and games with very few achievements.

Languages: English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Simplified Chinese and Polish.

kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard.body:
![PS5 Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/main/docs/screenshots/home.jpg)

## What's new in 1.10.0

### 🌍 The plugin speaks your language
PS5 Dashboard now follows the language you picked in Steam on each device, in **14 languages**:

English · Português · Español · Français · Deutsch · Italiano · Polski · Русский · Українська · Türkçe · 日本語 · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

- Any other Steam language gets **English**, never the operating system's language.
- Plurals follow each language's rules ("2 дня" / "5 дней", "2 miesiące" / "5 miesięcy"…).
- Translations live in [`src/locales/`](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/tree/main/src/locales), one file per language. Spotted something off in your language? Issues and pull requests are welcome!

### 🟦 Rounded corners actually work now
Steam registers a CSS property called `--r` as an angle, and the plugin used that same name for its corner radius, so Steam threw the value away and every tile, card and button came out square. The **Tile corner radius** setting (0–24 px) now rounds the game covers on the home row, the lower rows, the Game Library, the info cards and the buttons.

### ✨ The glass aura follows the corners
The animated edge around the focused game curves with the tile, and its light now shades through grey and the accent blue as well as white and translucent black.

Also includes everything from **1.9.0** (Hide bottom bar setting, header spacing). See the [changelog](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

1. Download **`ps5-dashboard.zip`** below.
2. In Game Mode: **Quick Access (`…`) → Decky → ⚙ Settings → General**, turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install plugin from ZIP**, pick `ps5-dashboard.zip`.

Updating? Install the new ZIP the same way; your settings are kept. The plugin panel should then show **v1.10.0** at the bottom. If it still shows an older version, restart Steam.

[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20a%20Coffee-support-FFDD00?logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/kromossomoc)

kromossomom-debug/decky-xbox-dashboard.body:
### Fixed
- **Tile corner radius really works now.** Steam registers its own CSS variable called `--r` as an angle, so the plugin's `--r: 25px` was thrown away and every corner came out at 0. The plugin's variables are now `--xbd-r`, `--xbd-a` and `--xbd-f`. Checked in Big Picture: 25 px in the settings gives 25 px tiles.
- **Power menu** (Sleep / Shut down / Restart) no longer turns red: the selected item uses the accent color (Xbox green), Shut down and Restart included.
- The selected power menu item no longer pokes out of the right edge of the panel.

### Changed
- **Power menu looks like the Xbox power options**: one solid dark panel with an accent stripe on top, a bold title above it, roomy rows instead of separate pills, and the selected row filled with the accent color and a white ring.

## Install
1. Download **xbox-dashboard.zip** below.
2. On the Deck: Quick Access (`…`) → **Decky** → ⚙️ → **General** → turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP** and pick the file.

Requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader) 3.x.

kromossomom-debug/decky-xbox-dashboard.name: Xbox Dashboard v0.0.5-alpha
kromossomom-debug/decky-xbox-dashboard.body:
### Added
- **Main row source**: choose what fills Home's big first row: recently played, pinned, installed, favorites or any of your collections (plugin panel → **Home rows → Main row**).
- **Customize Home games**: a new page with every game that can show on Home. **A** hides or shows a game, **X** pins or unpins it, **B** goes back. Hidden games are dimmed with a “Hidden” badge, pinned ones get a pin and a “Pinned” badge.
- **Unhide all**: a button in the panel brings every hidden game back at once (only shown when something is hidden).

### Fixed
- **Tile corner radius** now always applies on the plugin's own screens (Home, My games & apps, game page). The slider goes up to **32 px**, and the focus ring follows the corners.

### Changed
- **Reset to defaults** keeps your pinned and hidden games.

## Install
1. Download **xbox-dashboard.zip** below.
2. On the Deck: Quick Access (`…`) → **Decky** → ⚙️ → **General** → turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP** and pick the file.

Requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader) 3.x.

cyruzin/loadout.name: Loadout v0.6.0
cyruzin/loadout.body:
- Remove Loadout's FPS cap: Steam's QAM frame limit works for every
  game. Profiles show the target they're made for ("Made for 40 FPS at
  1280x720"). A cap block from 0.5.0 or older is removed on the next
  apply. Launch options stay for per-game env and args.
- Remove the Uncapped profile (without the cap it was Performance again).
  Profiles: Quality, Balanced, Performance, plus Default.
- Profile list shows only the profiles the device's (or borrowed) block
  has; applying one it doesn't have is refused (games.profile_spec).
- ELDEN RING: Quality only (40 FPS costs too much image quality).
- Baldur's Gate 3 (native Linux): Quality only, FSR 2.2 Quality, mostly
  Low with Medium textures, VSync and the game's frame cap off.
- lsxcfg: Larian .lsx read/set by MapKey, byte-preserving. Absent key =
  the game's default: null removes the entry, a missing int32 is added,
  and Default undoes both.
- {xdg_data} path root (~/.local/share, Steam's folder refused) for
  native games' settings.
- Device detected at load, generic if unknown: no Setup screen. Reset
  Loadout clears settings and stays on the main screen.
- Recommended resolution per profile (shown, never written).
- Confirm modal leads with a plain summary; full diff under Show details.
- Games without an entry are no longer listed, except while a profile
  from an older version is applied ("(no settings)").
- Docs: README, GAMES, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cyruzin/loadout/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0
