🎵 Game Theme Music 4.6.7

Stability, Performance & Customization

Stable Release | November 6, 2026

Hey everyone, Valentine here!

GTM 4.6.7 is here, bringing a collection of bug fixes, performance improvements, customization options, and better integration with ResonaDeck.

This update focuses on making the features already in GTM more reliable, responsive, and enjoyable to use.

A lot of work has gone into refining how GTM interacts with Steam, Decky Loader, and other plugins. Several of these improvements also came directly from community feedback.

Thank you to everyone who has been using GTM and reporting issues!

✨ What’s New?

🎛️ Customizable Library Context Menus

You can now independently control which GTM shortcuts appear in Steam’s Library context menus.

Available options include:

* Change Music
* Change Ambient Playlist
* Change Store Playlist

Each shortcut has its own visibility toggle.

Want to keep Change Music but hide the Ambient and Store options? You can!

These settings only affect the visibility of GTM’s shortcuts. Your playlists and music features remain available.

This improvement addresses community-reported GitHub Issue #10.

🧭 Improved Quick Menu Navigation

Navigating GTM is now easier.

* Added the Browse All Pages A–Z dropdown for direct page navigation.
* Preserved LB/RB controller paging.
* Improved focus handling between sections.
* Reduced unnecessary scrolling and page movement.
* Improved Quick Menu responsiveness.

These changes are particularly useful when navigating GTM with a controller.

🛍️ Store Music Reliability

Store Music has received several important fixes.

Both Steam’s native Store and the Decky Plugin Store now have improved detection and playback handling.

Improvements include:

* More reliable Store Music startup.
* Better recognition of the Decky Plugin Store.
* Improved detection when entering and leaving Steam’s native Store.
* Reduced delays when stopping Store Music after navigating away.
* Improved recovery from stalled playback initialization.
* Better handling of changing Steam navigation states.

Store Music also respects ResonaDeck’s audio priority.

If you’re already listening to music through ResonaDeck, GTM won’t interrupt it just because you open a Store page.

These improvements were verified on a physical Steam Deck without requiring a system restart.

🌈 GTM + ResonaDeck Visualizer Integration

GTM’s shared visualizer integration has received additional improvements.

When paired with ResonaDeck 1.5.7:

* Visualizers respect the user’s ON/OFF controls.
* Saved preferences no longer act as unwanted startup activation commands.
* Visualizers remain hidden when there is no eligible music playback.
* Enabled visualizers can appear when supported music begins playing.
* Disabling visualizers does not stop music playback.
* ResonaDeck can provide music-reactive frequency information to compatible GTM visualizers.

The goal is simple: music and visualizers should work together without fighting over settings.

⚡ Performance Improvements

We’ve also reduced unnecessary background activity.

Improvements include:

* Fewer redundant playlist-state storage writes.
* More efficient Ambient and Store state synchronization.
* Reduced unnecessary Steam interface observation.
* Better cleanup of background listeners.
* Improved plugin initialization and reload handling.
* Reduced unnecessary interface work.

These changes are intended to make GTM lighter without removing existing functionality.

🔧 Preserved Features

This update retains GTM’s existing music features, including:

* Steam and non-Steam game soundtracks.
* Ambient/Home Music.
* Steam Store and Decky Plugin Store Music.
* Music playlists and crossfading.
* Custom visualizers and visualizer packs.
* Optional AI-versus-AI Arcade Spectator scenes.
* CSS Loader theme compatibility.
* Sleep and wake handling.
* ResonaDeck audio coordination.
* YT-DLP downloading functionality.

YT-DLP and its required bundled components have not been removed.

✅ Testing & Verification

GTM 4.6.7 underwent multiple rounds of development testing and physical Steam Deck verification.

Confirmed working during the maintainer’s testing:

* Independent Library context-menu visibility controls.
* Quick Menu page navigation.
* Steam Store Music startup.
* Decky Plugin Store Music startup.
* Store Music stopping after leaving Store pages.
* ResonaDeck audio priority.
* Visualizer visibility controls.
* Store Music functionality without restarting Steam after installation.

Additional automated checks covered JavaScript/Python syntax, package integrity, Store navigation behavior, and preservation of bundled downloader components.

Testing does not guarantee identical behavior across every SteamOS version, Decky Loader release, or CSS Loader theme.

📦 Installation

Download Game-Theme-Music-4.6.7.zip from the Assets section below.

Install using Decky Loader’s manual ZIP installation option.

Please download the actual plugin ZIP rather than GitHub’s automatically generated source-code archive.

Your existing GTM settings and playlists are intended to remain intact when updating normally.

A Steam Deck restart is not normally required. If older interface components remain after updating, restarting Steam may help.

❤️ Thank You!

GTM has grown considerably since its earlier releases.

Although I’m focusing more on maintenance and stability now, I’m still paying attention to feedback and improving what we’ve already built.

If you discover a reproducible problem, please open a GitHub issue and include your GTM version.

Thank you for downloading, testing, and supporting Game Theme Music.

Enjoy the music!

Valentine
Developer of Game Theme Music

valentinebsaa/resonadeck.name: ResonaDeck 1.5.7
valentinebsaa/resonadeck.body:
🎧 ResonaDeck 1.5.7

Quick Menu Performance, Stability & GTM Integration

Stable Release | November 6, 2026

Hey everyone, Valentine here!

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 is now available!

This release focuses on improving Quick Menu responsiveness, fixing interface rendering issues, reducing unnecessary background activity, and improving compatibility with Game Theme Music.

ResonaDeck has grown into a full-featured music player for Steam Deck Gaming Mode, and keeping that experience reliable is just as important as adding new functionality.

This update focuses on polishing what we already have.

✨ What’s Improved?

⚡ Faster Quick Menu Rendering

One of our biggest priorities was reducing the amount of work ResonaDeck performs when opening Quick Access.

Previously, ResonaDeck could spend unnecessary time recalculating theme colors, observing Steam interface changes, and rebuilding portions of its interface.

We’ve made several improvements:

* Reduced unnecessary theme calculations.
* Improved reuse of previously detected colors.
* Reduced redundant background monitoring.
* Improved initialization of the Quick Menu interface.
* Reduced unnecessary visual updates.
* Improved cleanup of background tasks during plugin updates.

These changes aim to make ResonaDeck feel more responsive while preserving its appearance and functionality.

🎨 Quick Menu Styling Fixes

ResonaDeck’s premium interface has also received important rendering corrections.

An earlier optimization caused some styles to load outside the plugin’s rendering environment.

This could result in oversized album artwork, overlapping labels, and incorrectly positioned controls.

The original styling behavior has been restored while retaining compatible performance improvements.

ResonaDeck continues to support:

* Artwork-inspired colors.
* Adaptive Steam/CSS Loader themes.
* Frosted-glass interface elements.
* Controller-friendly navigation.
* Full player controls.
* Album artwork and playback information.

The interface was verified again on a physical Steam Deck after these corrections.

🌈 Improved Game Theme Music Integration

ResonaDeck’s visualizer integration has received additional synchronization improvements.

When paired with Game Theme Music 4.6.7:

* Visualizer controls remain available from both plugins.
* Saved settings no longer automatically force unwanted startup activation.
* Enabled visualizers remain hidden when no eligible music is playing.
* Visualizers can become active when supported playback begins.
* Disabling visualizers does not interrupt Plex music.
* Music-reactive audio analysis and GTM communication remain supported.

The integration includes diagnostic information for audio capture and communication.

During testing, music-reactive behavior was successfully restored by refreshing the visualizer connection through the ON/OFF switch.

If visualizers appear but do not initially react to music, switching GTM Visualizers OFF and back ON in ResonaDeck can refresh the connection.

🎵 Better Background Efficiency

ResonaDeck now performs less unnecessary work while running alongside other Decky plugins.

Improvements include:

* Reduced redundant power-state polling.
* More selective theme-change monitoring.
* Better cleanup of background listeners and timers.
* Improved management of visualizer bridge resources.
* Reduced repeated interface color calculations.

The goal is to reduce unnecessary background activity while keeping music playback dependable.

🧹 Interface Cleanup

The previously introduced Cash App donation button and associated artwork have been removed.

ResonaDeck’s interface remains focused on music playback, library browsing, and player controls.

🎼 Existing Features Preserved

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 retains its existing functionality, including:

* Plex music libraries.
* Jellyfin integration.
* Audiobooks and podcasts.
* Surprise Me music discovery.
* Keep Playing and continuous queue replenishment.
* Favorites and saved listening options.
* Music crossfading.
* Long-duration track handling.
* Sleep and wake recovery.
* Full ResonaDeck Manager.
* Album artwork and playback controls.
* Music-reactive GTM integration.
* Controller-friendly navigation.

Previous improvements to multi-hour playback and crossfade countdown accuracy are also preserved.

✅ Testing & Verification

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 builds on several rounds of testing and fixes.

The following behavior has been confirmed during development and Steam Deck testing:

* Quick Menu styling displays correctly.
* Album artwork and player controls render in their intended layout.
* The player interface remains functional after the styling corrections.
* Visualizers remain hidden without eligible playback.
* Visualizers can activate during supported music playback.
* Music-reactive communication can function after refreshing the GTM visualizer connection.
* ResonaDeck playback takes priority over GTM Store Music when already playing.

Automated checks also covered JavaScript/Python syntax and ZIP integrity.

Not every Plex/Jellyfin configuration, media format, SteamOS version, or CSS Loader theme has been tested.

📦 Installation

Download ResonaDeck-1.5.7.zip from the Assets section below.

Install through Decky Loader’s manual ZIP installation option.

Use the named plugin ZIP rather than GitHub’s automatically generated source-code archive.

Existing settings, libraries, and preferences are intended to remain intact during normal updates.

A full Steam Deck restart is not normally required. If the interface retains old styling after an update, close and reopen Quick Access or restart Steam if necessary.

For the latest shared visualizer improvements, use Game Theme Music 4.6.7.

❤️ Thank You!

ResonaDeck started with a simple idea: bringing a dedicated Plex music experience directly into Steam Deck Gaming Mode.

Since then, it has grown considerably, with more playback controls, discovery features, library management, and integration with Game Theme Music.

I’m continuing to focus on making ResonaDeck reliable, responsive, and enjoyable to use.

Thank you to everyone who has downloaded it, tested it, or shared feedback.

Your support helps keep these projects moving forward.

Enjoy your music!

Valentine
Developer of ResonaDeck

beallio/decky-metadata.name: v0.6.3 — Fix game page freezes with Unifideck 0.8.0 and add a Store info row with HowLongToBeat and ProtonDB
beallio/decky-metadata.body:
Fix game page freezes with Unifideck 0.8.0 and add a Store info row with HowLongToBeat and ProtonDB

### Added

- **Store info row.** Steam Store game pages now show a boxed info row directly
  below the trailers and screenshots, in the style of Steam's own **Reviews**
  and SteamOS Compatibility rows. It holds a **HowLongToBeat** box with the same
  times as the game page, honoring the stat switches, and a **ProtonDB** box
  with the game's tier. Selecting a box opens that game on HowLongToBeat or
  ProtonDB. The row works for games you do not own, and you can select the boxes
  with the D-pad.
- **HLTB Store switch.** The new **Store** switch in **HLTB times** controls the
  **HowLongToBeat** box on Store pages. It is on by default.

### Changed

- **ProtonDB Store switch controls the Store box.** The ProtonDB **Store**
  switch now turns the **ProtonDB** box in the info row on or off. If only one
  box has data, it fills the row. If both switches are off, there is no row.
- **Mini achievements for non-Steam games.** When another plugin, such as
  Emuchievements, gives Steam the achievements for a non-Steam game, its
  ACHIEVEMENTS row now shows beside Play Time, as it does for Steam games.
  Non-Steam games without achievements still get no row.

### Removed

- **Floating ProtonDB Store badge.** The colored ProtonDB icon at the bottom
  right of Steam Store pages is gone. The **ProtonDB** box in the info row
  replaces it.

### Fixed

- **Game page freeze with Unifideck 0.8.0.** Opening a Unifideck game's page
  no longer freezes Steam on a spinning logo when Decky Metadata and Unifideck
  have a different Steam Deck compatibility rating for it. Decky Metadata's
  rating is shown, and Unifideck's other game details stay in place.
  ([#35](https://github.com/beallio/Decky-Metadata/issues/35))

beallio/decky-metadata.name: v0.6.2 — Mini achievements and Activity news work again after Steam's November update
beallio/decky-metadata.body:
Mini achievements and Activity news work again after Steam's November update

### Changed

- **HLTB "Details" button.** The button that opens a game's HowLongToBeat page
  is now called **Details**. In the **Default** style it looks like the
  **Details** button in Steam's Deck Compatibility section. In the **"Clean"**
  styles it looks like the ProtonDB and controller buttons beside Play, and it
  follows the corner rounding of the CSS Loader theme "Round". The **"View
  Details" color** option is removed.
- **HLTB "Clean" bars match the Play bar.** In the Clean Gameview
  **Transparent**, **Blur**, and **Connected with Body** Play bar styles, the
  HLTB row always uses the Play bar's background. The new **Background blur**
  option matches the Play bar by default and can also force or remove the blur.
  **Background opacity** now applies to the **Default** style only.
- **"Clean" HLTB Details corners.** The new **Use Steam button corners** option
  keeps the **Details** button corners as Steam draws them, so the "Round" theme
  does not round them. It is off by default.

### Removed

- **Show/Hide HLTB Stats in the game menu.** The entry is removed. Games you
  hid this way show their times again. To hide all times, turn off **Show
  HowLongToBeat times**.

### Fixed

- **HLTB background and blur.** The "Clean" bars match the Play bar's
  background and opacity. When the Play bar is blurred, the **"Clean" Default**
  times and the Play bar now share one seamless blurred panel. **Background
  blur** never changes the Play bar's blur.
- **HLTB times no longer push the Play button down.** The **Default** and
  **"Clean" Default** rows now sit on the bottom of the game's header image, so
  the Play row stays in its usual place.
- **Mini achievements works again after Steam's November client update.**
  Steam's update hid its own mini achievements row on the Steam Deck game page.
  Metadata now turns Steam's own row back on, so it looks and behaves exactly
  like Steam's, and selecting it opens My Achievements. Games without Steam
  achievements get no row.
- **Activity news shows again for matched non-Steam games.** Steam's new
  activity cards need fields the plugin did not supply, which made the page
  show a render error instead of the news.
- **Debug logging follows Decky Loader's debug switch.** Turning on debug
  logging for Decky Metadata in Decky Loader now records debug messages, even
  when the plugin's own **Debug logging** setting is off.

mdeguzis/decky-proton-pulse.name: Proton Pulse v1.15.0
mdeguzis/decky-proton-pulse.body:
Proton Pulse v1.15.0

- Accept Armada, Pocknix, and Android as valid OS entries, letting Retroid Pocket / AYN Odin / AyaNeo Pocket DS and DroidDeck users submit reports (refs mdeguzis/proton-pulse-web#544)
- Multi-config-per-app: a game can now hold any number of named launch-option profiles ('Default', '60fps low', 'framegen', etc.). Save creates a new profile when the name differs; matching names still upsert. Storage keyed by (appId, profileName); Supabase user_proton_configs schema migrated to a composite (voter_id, app_id, profile_name) primary key.
- Save vs Apply split in the Config Editor: Save persists to storage + cloud without touching Steam launch options or bumping the active slot. Apply writes to Steam launch options + promotes the profile to ACTIVE. Save-only profiles no longer steal ACTIVE from a profile you are currently playing.
- ACTIVE badge on the row whose profile is currently applied. Playtime attributes to that specific profile.
- Per-config Pending Approval / Published pills. Two profiles on the same game no longer both light up when only one was submitted; each row reflects its own report state via config_key. Legacy null-key submissions from before this fix light up only the ACTIVE profile as a fallback.
- Submit modal fires onSubmitted so the Manage tab refreshes the row status without waiting for a remount.
- Submit modal is passed configKey so the DB row's config_key is populated. Report status becomes truly per-profile going forward.
- Plugin submits now set game_owned=true. The admin report detail no longer shows 'Game Owned: false' for plugin-sourced reports.
- 'Applied X ago' meta line now ticks live: ManageTab subscribes to onConfigSaved (immediate refresh after Apply / Reapply) plus a 60s tick so the relative label doesn't go stale.
- Draft pill hidden when there is no submitted report for a profile. SYNCED green badge already covers the cloud state; the extra 'Draft' gray pill next to it read as noise.

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.45.4 — Server folders, threads and forums
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### New

- Server folders: the server lists (Quick Access voice and text tabs, expanded view) show your Discord folders as collapsible rows, closed by default, with a preview of their servers like in Discord. Folders you open stay open. A folder with only one visible server shows that server directly. While you reorder servers or browse hidden ones, the list stays flat ([#101](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/101)).
- Threads: active threads appear under their text channel, and the threads button next to each channel lists all of them, archived ones included. A thread opens like any channel: read, reply, live updates ([#100](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/100)).
- Forums: forum channels appear in the channel list and open onto their posts, most recently active first, with their tags and a "Show more" button for large forums ([#100](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/100)).
- Search threads and forum posts by title, and filter forum posts by tag ([#100](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/100)).
- Create a thread in a text channel, with an optional first message, or a forum post with its message and tags. The button only appears where you are allowed to post; forums that require a tag ask for one ([#100](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/100)).

### Fixes

- Errors coming from Steamcord's backend are shown with their actual reason instead of "Python Exception". This also brings back the automatic retry of the server lists while Discord is still starting or reconnecting, which never triggered because the reason was hidden.

### Thanks

Thanks to [@Torun-S](https://github.com/Torun-S) for both suggestions ([#100](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/100), [#101](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/101)).

**Full changelog:** [v1.45.3...v1.45.4](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/compare/v1.45.3...v1.45.4)

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.45.3 — Chat Mix volumes, overlay and expanded view fixes
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### Fixes

- Chat Mix no longer lowers an application further each time it reopens. WirePlumber gives an application's new audio stream the volume Steamcord had set on the previous one, and Steamcord took it as the normal volume and lowered it again (100 → 50 → 25 → 12 → 6 %). Steamcord now remembers each application's own volume, even across restarts, and restores it once the call ends; a volume you set yourself is left alone ([#96](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/96)).
- The voice overlay switch shows the right state when Steamcord turns the remembered overlay on at the start of a call ([#92](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/92)).
- No more stray red line from your name to the deafened icon in the voice overlay ([#92](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/92)).
- The expanded view is no longer cut off at the bottom when opened over Steam's menus in Game Mode: its height now follows the space left under Steam's top bar ([#98](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/98)).
- The loading icon shown while Steamcord starts is no longer cropped ([#98](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/98)).

### Improved

- The warning shown when Steam's game recording runs during a screen share now also mentions an image split into copies, the other symptom it causes ([#91](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/91), thanks to [@BeanieBoy981](https://github.com/BeanieBoy981) for testing).
- The voice overlay log now records the screen and window size it uses, to look into centred positions that sit too high ([#92](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/92)).

### Thanks

Thanks to [@arsaban](https://github.com/arsaban) ([#96](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/96)) and [@nawavon](https://github.com/nawavon) ([#92](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/92), [#98](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/98)) for their detailed reports.

**Full changelog:** [v1.45.2...v1.45.3](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/compare/v1.45.2...v1.45.3)

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.45.2 — Vesktop port no longer blocks other plugins
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### Fixes

- Steamcord no longer blocks other plugins' sign-in windows. Vesktop's debugging port moves from 9223 to 39223, away from the 9222–9224 range that other Decky plugins use for their own browser windows; Unifideck's Microsoft sign-in works again while Steamcord runs. After the update, Vesktop restarts once on its own ([#95](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/95)).
- On Linux, Steamcord now checks that this port belongs to Vesktop before connecting, as it already did on Windows. If another program uses it, Steamcord leaves it alone and logs which program it is.

### Thanks

Thanks to [@humzakh](https://github.com/humzakh) for the detailed report and the tested workaround ([#95](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/95)).

**Full changelog:** [v1.45.1...v1.45.2](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/compare/v1.45.1...v1.45.2)

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.45.1 — Steam menu choice survives restarts
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### Fixes

- Turning off the Steamcord entry in Steam's main menu now lasts after Steam restarts. Steamcord also saves this choice in its own settings, because Steam could reload an older value and bring the entry back ([#86](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/86)).

### Improved

- Game detection diagnostics now say how many windows were read, how many belong to GeForce NOW, and what kind of title they had (game name, GeForce NOW only, a launcher page). Game titles are still never included ([#88](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/88)).

### Thanks

Thanks to [@zerothecat4564](https://github.com/zerothecat4564) and [@JDLKMR](https://github.com/JDLKMR) for reporting and confirming the menu issue ([#86](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/86)), and to [@j2v454sj](https://github.com/j2v454sj) for testing GeForce NOW detection ([#88](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/issues/88)).

**Full changelog:** [v1.45.0...v1.45.1](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/compare/v1.45.0...v1.45.1)

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.45.0 — Proxy for Discord
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### New

- **Proxy for Discord.** In countries where Discord is blocked, Settings ▸ Proxy can send Discord through an HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4 or SOCKS5 proxy, with an optional login, and a Test button checks that Discord answers through it. Discord's connection, sign-in (QR code included), images and Go Live signalling use it, as do Steamcord's own downloads (updates, attachments, the Windows Vesktop download). The password is stored on the device only, never shown again in the panel, and never written to a command line or the log. Voice and video calls cannot go through a proxy: in countries where calls are blocked too, a system-wide VPN is still needed. Thanks to [@borborisovai](https://github.com/borborisovai).

### Fixes

- Screen sharing started from Vesktop's own button in Desktop Mode works again. It no longer goes through the Go Live timeout and fallback, which could leave the button unresponsive for the rest of the session ([#94](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/pull/94), thanks to [@simonesessa](https://github.com/simonesessa)).
- A Discord start that keeps failing no longer writes the whole injected script to the log every 2 seconds, which could grow the log by hundreds of MB (thanks to [@SilvertongueRED](https://github.com/SilvertongueRED)).

**Full changelog:** [v1.44.1...v1.45.0](https://github.com/Necrosiak/Steamcord/compare/v1.44.1...v1.45.0)

jinzhongjia/decky-music.name: v1.1.7
jinzhongjia/decky-music.body:
## 修复

- 修复左侧 Steam 菜单注入的 wrapper 递归：复用 `<Ie>` element 时不再重复包裹，避免栈深度累积导致 Steam UI 报 `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`（#83）。
- 左侧菜单注入改为 fail-closed：`fe.type` 保持 FunctionComponent，真正的 React ErrorBoundary 作为子组件；注入 render 有硬深度上限，异常时永久熔断并还原 `fe.type`。注入自身异常不会再升级成整个 Steam UI 错误页。
- 旧版本残留的、无法解链的 wrapper 会直接断开，避免历史 wrapper 链继续递归。

## 验证

- `pnpm build`、`pnpm lint`、`pnpm test:ui`（51/51）通过。
- 20,000 次复用同一个 `<Ie>` element 渲染：wrapper 不加深；v1.1.6 旧实现会直接 `RangeError`。

mimed95/decky-voxtype.name: 0.2.0 Fixed naming and build pipeline
mimed95/decky-voxtype.body:
## Changes

- **Plugin identifier unified as `decky-voxtype`.** Appears under that name in Decky Loader; previously registered as "Voxtype", which diverged from the directory, package name, and zip filename.
- **Single source of truth for the name.** Defined once in `plugin.json`; consumed at runtime via `@decky/manifest`, in packaging via `jq`, and in CI via a metadata step.
- **Release pipeline fixed.** The `0.1.0` release shipped with no zip attached because the CI upload gate was `refs/tags/v*` and the tag was `0.1.0`. Both the trigger filter and the upload gate now accept any tag.
- **Packaging hardening.** `scripts/pack.sh` now copies `dist/*.js` (not only `index.js`), guarding against future Rollup code-splitting.
- **Dependency alignment.** Pinned `@types/react-router@5.1.20` to match Decky Loader upstream and `@decky/api`'s own devDeps — resolves a dangling type import under `tsc --noEmit`.

mimed95/decky-voxtype.name: First Release 0.1.0
mimed95/decky-voxtype.body:
# Voxtype v0.1.0 — voice dictation comes to Steam Deck Game Mode

  **The first voice-typing plugin for Decky Loader.** Press a controller button, speak, release — and the
  transcription lands on your system clipboard, ready to paste into any text field on your Deck. Fully local,
   fully offline, built on [voxtype](https://github.com/peteonrails/voxtype) and [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp).

  No cloud. No API key. No account. Your voice never leaves the Deck.

  ## Highlights

  - **Controller-native push-to-talk.** Bind any button (or a two-button chord) directly through the plugin's
   settings. No fiddling with Steam Input keyboard mappings; the plugin listens at the Steam Input layer
  itself. Default: **R4** back grip.
  - **Vulkan acceleration on the Deck's GPU.** Ships with both an AVX2 CPU build and a Vulkan-enabled build
  of voxtype. One toggle switches between them — no `pacman`, no read-only root gymnastics, no lingering
  system packages after SteamOS updates.
  - **Works in the background.** Recording fires even when the Decky menu is closed. Open a search box, hold
  your PTT button, speak. Clipboard updated.
  - **Multiple Whisper models.** `tiny.en` / `base.en` / `small.en` / `medium.en` plus multilingual
  equivalents. Base (~140 MB) is the default and is plenty accurate for most dictation. Download from the
  plugin settings.
  - **Fails gracefully.** Idempotent daemon lifecycle, `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)` so voxtype processes can
  never be orphaned, `--no-hotkey` so the daemon doesn't fight with the OS, truncated per-run crash log at
  `/home/deck/homebrew/logs/decky-voxtype/voxtype-daemon.log`.

  ## What you get

  - Push-to-talk via any Deck button or chord.
  - Optional two-button chord mode for PTT without a dedicated button.
  - CPU or GPU backend, switchable at runtime.
  - Auto-start on boot (opt-out).
  - A "Listening to voice input" toast when recording begins, and a preview toast with your transcription
  when it completes.

  ## Install

  1. Download `decky-voxtype-v0.1.0.zip` below.
  2. In Desktop Mode: Decky → Settings → Developer → Install from URL / zip, or drop the unzipped folder into
   `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/`.
  3. In Game Mode: open the plugin, flip **Enable Voxtype**, download the `base.en` model from the Settings
  panel (one-time, ~140 MB).
  4. Pick your PTT button. Press it. Talk.

  ## Requirements

  - Steam Deck (OLED or LCD). Linux x86_64 with Vulkan support works too.
  - Decky Loader installed.
  - ~180 MB of disk space (binaries + default model).
  - A working microphone (Deck's built-in mic is fine).

  ## Known limitations

  - Model downloads use voxtype's built-in setup path; first download runs synchronously from the plugin
  panel.
  - Auto-paste (Ctrl+V) mode is intentionally not shipped — on SteamOS it would require `ydotool`, which
  SteamOS updates wipe. Clipboard + paste-from-OSK is the supported flow.
  - Transcription quality follows the Whisper model you pick. For games/apps with unusual vocabulary, the
  `small.en` model is a meaningful upgrade over `base.en` at the cost of longer transcription time.

  ## Thanks

  - [peteonrails/voxtype](https://github.com/peteonrails/voxtype) — the whisper.cpp-based daemon doing the
  actual speech recognition.
  - [SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader) — the plugin
  platform.
  - [decky-lsfg-vk](https://github.com/pluto2023/decky-lsfg-vk) — reference for the Web Clipboard pattern
  used for output.
  - Whisper by OpenAI, whisper.cpp by ggerganov.

  ---

  First release. Feedback, bug reports, and feature requests welcome in Issues.

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.6.1 - Volume-routing boot delay + TV-clobbering fixes
jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.body:
### Fixed
- **Volume-routing boot delay**: after a reboot, the guide+stick volume shortcut sometimes fell back to SteamOS's normal volume slider instead of routing through this plugin, until a volume slider was touched manually. SteamOS only checks once, at Gamescope session start, whether the HDMI output supports external volume control — WirePlumber is now always restarted as the very first step of plugin startup (not only when its config changed) so the check has the best chance of succeeding on its own. Confirmed fixed across a real reboot.
- **TV sync blueprint**: none of the TV actions (Steam device turning on, volume buttons, mute, guide button) touch the TV anymore while it's on and showing something other than the configured HDMI input — previously the guide button and volume buttons would act on the TV regardless of what was currently on screen.
- **Blueprint crash**: leaving the volume buttons / guide button / Steam Link streaming entity inputs unset could crash automation validation ("Entity ID is not a valid entity ID"), since Home Assistant rejects an empty string as a target entity_id for the `event.received` trigger. Those inputs now default to a syntactically valid but nonexistent placeholder entity instead, which simply never fires.

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.6.0 - Steam Link streaming detection for the TV sync blueprint
jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.body:
### Added
- **Steam Link streaming sensor**: a new `binary_sensor` reflects whether the device is actively streaming to a Steam Link / Remote Play client, published on the retained `<base>/streaming` topic. Detected via `SteamClient.RemotePlay.RegisterForDevicesChanges` (undocumented, community-reverse-engineered, see the README note).
- The [TV sync blueprint](blueprints/automation/steamos_tv_sync.yaml) uses it: starting a stream turns the TV off (only if it's on the right HDMI input), ending the stream turns it back on — with a fix so the existing "TV off suspends the Steam device" rule doesn't fire because of this new TV-off action.

### Fixed
- Entity pickers in the blueprint no longer include a non-functional `integration: mqtt` filter where it wasn't narrowing anything on some Home Assistant versions; kept where it's paired with `device_class` (the power sensor), which does narrow correctly.

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.5.0 - Current app sensor + update notifications
jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.body:
### Added
- **Current App sensor**: Home Assistant now shows which game/app is running (including non-Steam shortcuts), published on the retained `<base>/app` topic — great for automations like "dim the lights when a game starts". Also shown in the plugin's Live Status panel.
- **Update notifications**: the plugin checks GitHub for new releases (on boot and twice daily). You get a toast in Game Mode when an update is available, a version notice with a release-page button in the plugin panel, and an update entity in Home Assistant.

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.4.0
jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.body:
### Added
- Home Assistant blueprint (`blueprints/automation/steamos_tv_sync.yaml`) for a full Steam Machine ↔ TV sync: power on/off follow each other (with HDMI source switching and Wake-on-LAN), the Steam controller's volume buttons control the TV, and the guide button switches the HDMI input. Configurable per-state delays and per-direction on/off toggles, both collapsed with sensible defaults — just pick your entities instead of hand-writing the automation. One-click "My Home Assistant" import badge added to the README.
- Volume-button events (up/down/mute) are now debounced directly inside the plugin.

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.3.0 - Guide button events + docked sensor
jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.body:
## What's new

hostsrc/decky-prysm.body:
# Prysm v0.2.0 - First Public Release

Stream your Steam Deck screen to any browser on your network. One-tap start from Game Mode.

## Features

- **Two streaming methods** - choose in QAM settings:
  - MPEG-TS (~500ms latency) - stable, works on any browser
  - WebRTC (~200ms latency) - lower latency via MediaMTX
- **VAAPI hardware encoding** - H.264 on AMD GPU, near-zero CPU usage
- **Quality presets** - 480p30, 720p30, 720p60, 1080p30, 1080p60
- **Live stats in QAM** - viewers, bytes sent, encoder status
- **Auto-restart** on capture failure
- **Native Decky UI** - all standard Steam Deck components

## Install

1. Download `Prysm-v0.2.0.zip`
2. Extract `Prysm/` folder to `~/homebrew/plugins/` on your Steam Deck
3. Restart Decky Loader: `sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader`

Or one-liner:
```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hostsrc/decky-prysm/main/install.sh | bash
```

## Requirements

- Steam Deck running SteamOS 3.5+
- Decky Loader installed
- Game must NOT have `ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=0` in launch options

## Performance (720p30 over WiFi/Ethernet)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Bitrate | ~5 Mbps |
| Decoded FPS | 29 fps |
| Dropped frames | <1% |
| Buffer | 0.4s |
| CPU usage | <3% (VAAPI) |

## What's New

### Streaming
- kmsgrab capture with VAAPI H.264 hardware encoding
- HTTP MPEG-TS server with mpegts.js viewer (low-latency tuned)
- MediaMTX WebRTC backend as alternative streaming method
- Auto-restart on FFmpeg/capture failures
- TS packet-aligned reads to prevent sync errors
- ThreadingHTTPServer for non-blocking stats

### QAM Plugin
- Clean single-panel layout with Start Streaming as primary action
- Method selector (MPEG-TS / WebRTC)
- Quality presets (480p30 to 1080p60)
- Audio toggle
- Live stats: viewers, total sent, encoder status
- All native Decky UI components

### Infrastructure
- GitHub Actions CI/CD (build + release pipelines)
- Makefile with build/dist/deploy targets
- Distribution zip matching Decky Plugin Store requirements
- Full GPL-2.0 license

## Contributors

- [@hostsrc](https://github.com/hostsrc)
- Claude Opus 4.6 (AI pair programmer)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hostsrc/decky-prysm/commits/v0.2.0

kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.name: xgmobile-manager v0.3.0
kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.body:
## XG Mobile Manager 0.3.0

The first stable release since 0.2.4. It brings a new compact panel, CachyOS support, a much more reliable Enable and Eject, and **support for SteamOS 3.9.5**.

> **SteamOS users, please read:** SteamOS 3.9.5 moved to a new kernel (7.2) that older plugin versions can't build the NVIDIA driver for. After installing 0.3.0, open the plugin → **▸ Setup & Maintenance** → **Install NVIDIA Drivers**, then reboot. 0.3.0 installs NVIDIA driver **620.70.06**.

### Highlights
* **SteamOS 3.9.5 support:** NVIDIA 620.70.06 for kernel 7.2. Booting with the XG Mobile enabled works again: the boot service notices when the driver loaded before its firmware was readable and reloads it (about 3 seconds on those boots).
* **A compact panel:** a status line (Active / Connected / Not connected), one Enable/Eject button, live temperature, power (`used / limit W`), VRAM and load, with colours. Details are behind ⓘ pop-ups, and rarely used buttons are under ▸ Setup & Maintenance.
* **CachyOS support:** an NVIDIA driver installer that uses CachyOS's own packages, plus fixes for its login manager.
* **A safer Eject:**
  * Eject now asks before closing your game.
  * Changing the power profile can no longer "click through" to the Eject button.
  * Bazzite's `cardwired` service is restarted instead of killed (killing it left Game Mode stuck at login).
  * The eGPU is released in a safe order, and the session returns to Game Mode reliably.
* **Full power on the RTX 4090:** the NVIDIA power services start after the eGPU is up, so Performance reaches 150 W.
* **A boot safety net:** powering off with the XG Mobile enabled and booting without it no longer leads to a black screen.
* **Clearer errors:** pop-ups say what went wrong and what to do, including a separate message when the NVIDIA driver doesn't build for a new SteamOS kernel.
* **Logs in their own folder:** `~/homebrew/logs/xgmobile-manager/activity/`. Old logs are moved there automatically.

### Upgrading
* **SteamOS:** install 0.3.0, then **Install NVIDIA Drivers** and reboot (see above). After every future SteamOS update: Reset Driver Environment → update → reboot → Install NVIDIA Drivers.
* **Bazzite:** nothing to do; the drivers come with the bazzite-deck-nvidia image.
* **CachyOS:** if you haven't yet, **Install NVIDIA Drivers** once. After that, the drivers update with `sudo pacman -Syu`.

Quick install (latest stable):
```bash
curl -sL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/refs/heads/main/bin/install.sh" > /tmp/install.sh && bash /tmp/install.sh
```

### Tested on
ROG Ally (RC71L) + RTX 4090 XG Mobile, on a 4K TV (resolution set to 2K):
* SteamOS 3.9.5 (kernel 7.2.7), NVIDIA 620.70.06 installed by the plugin
* Bazzite 45.20261112 (bazzite-deck-nvidia), NVIDIA 620.70.06
* CachyOS Handheld (kernel 7.2.9 deckify), NVIDIA 615.78.08

**Hardware I don't own** (AMD XG Mobile, RTX 3080, ROG Flow laptops) relies on community testers. Thanks to @tanayabhay-creator for the RTX 3080 reports and measurements.

### Known issues
* **Bazzite + NVIDIA:** waking from sleep with the eGPU active forces a hard reboot (upstream). Eject before sleeping.
* **4K and ultrawide in Game Mode** may not work fully (gamescope). Desktop Mode supports more resolutions.
* **On SteamOS, Steam's performance overlay** shows 0 °C / 0 MHz for the XG Mobile. The plugin's panel shows the real values.

See the [README](https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager#readme) for details. Starting with 0.3.0, development is AI-assisted (see [AI-Assisted Development](https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager#ai-assisted-development)).

## What's Changed
* feat: descriptive SteamUI pop-ups with actionable error messages by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/19
* test: Tier 0 no-hardware test harness (pytest + bats + vitest, CI) by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/20
* fix: CachyOS session compatibility and egpu-enable robustness by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/21
* feat: automated NVIDIA driver install and session fixes for CachyOS by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/23
* fix: eject release order, boot safety net, and failures that outlive the panel by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/24
* feat: plugin logs in their own folder, with automatic migration of old logs by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/26
* fix: start the NVIDIA services after the eGPU is up, so the XG Mobile gets its full power by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/27
* fix: hardware pass 2 follow-ups (desktop-eject black screen, logs, power docs) by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/28
* fix: desktop Eject returns to Game Mode, restart an eGPU-tainted user manager, boot sync waits for the card by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/29
* feat: compact Quick Access panel with status colours and telemetry limits by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/30
* ci: rewrite the release workflow around build.sh with a Tier 0 gate by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/22
* chore: version 0.3.0-beta-1 by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/31
* fix: don't rewrite an unchanged power profile; restart (not kill) system services holding the eGPU by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/32
* docs: README for 0.3.0: the new panel, CachyOS, betas, badges and an AI-assistance disclaimer by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/33
* docs(testing): a stable release gate instead of a full Tier 3 pass by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/34
* fix(steamos): SteamOS 3.9.5 support: NVIDIA 620.70.06 for kernel 7.2, boot with the eGPU on, honest DKMS failures by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/35
* fix(panel): a profile change can't click through to Eject; Eject asks first by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/36
* chore: version 0.3.0 by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/37


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/compare/v0.2.4...v0.3.0

kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.name: v0.2.4 - NVIDIA Driver Update, Kernel Validation & Stability Fixes
kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.body:
# v0.2.4 - NVIDIA Driver Update, Kernel Validation & Stability Fixes

This release consolidates all improvements from the 0.2.4-beta cycle and resolves critical installation failures caused by recent upstream changes in the SteamOS Client Stable channel. 

### 🚀 Changelog

#### 📦 NVIDIA Driver Maintenance
* **Driver Bump:** Upgraded the backend driver to **610.43.02-3**.
* **Driver Version Decoupling:** Separated the core kernel driver versioning from the desktop settings application package, allowing for more flexible maintenance.
* **Deep Clean Uninstaller:** Enhanced the uninstaller script to track down and thoroughly purge stale, lingering files from older installations to prevent dependency conflicts.

#### 🎮 AMD / SteamOS Fixes
* **Display Priority Override:** Added experimental environment variable injection for AMD hardware configurations. This explicitly informs Gamescope to prioritize the external eGPU over the handheld's internal APU when entering Game Mode.
* **Fixed Background Installation Failures:** Adjusted the plugin backend to sanitize environment variables without stripping critical D-Bus routing. This restores DNS resolution and package syncing functionality for the UI-based installer.
* **Smarter Kernel Validation:** Overhauled the kernel-vs-repository check. The installer now translates and accurately compares the exact Valve revision strings (e.g., `-valve24.1` vs `.valve24.1`). If Valve pushes new headers to their repository before the OS update is applied, the script will safely halt and warn you, preventing broken DKMS builds.

#### 📱 UI & Plugin Stability
* **Decky UI Upgrade:** Bumped `@decky/ui` package version to **v4.11.4** to ensure proper rendering of UI dropdown menus and overlays.
* **Log Viewer Fixes:** Patched `LogViewerModal` to adapt to upstream structural changes and prevent potential overlay freezes.
* **Reboot Prompt Fix:** Resolved an issue where the system reboot pop-up would fail to display after completing a driver installation or uninstallation.

### ⚠️ Installation Notes
As always, after successfully installing or updating the NVIDIA drivers via the plugin, **please reboot your device** to activate the newly compiled kernel modules before connecting your XG Mobile.

## What's Changed
* Pull Request: v0.2.4-beta Update by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/9
* Update to v0.2.4: Kernel Check Overhaul & SteamOS Environment Fixes by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/11


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/compare/v0.2.3...v0.2.4

ag69075/steamos_plugin_achievements.body:
fix: hide badge/bubble for 5 min on game launch

Remove RegisterForGameActionEnd and RegisterForAppLifetimeNotifications
handlers from registerGameActionTracking — both fire within seconds of
launch and were clearing the "launching" state prematurely, causing the
badge/bubble to reappear almost immediately.

Now rely solely on a 300 000 ms safety timer (5 min) started on
GameActionStart (LaunchApp).

ag69075/steamos_plugin_achievements.name: v1.2.3
ag69075/steamos_plugin_achievements.body:
v1.2.3: remove Web API fallback, hide badge during game launch

Fully remove the Steam Web API fallback path (SteamAchievementsClient,
api_key/steamid64 settings) from main.py — the badge now relies solely
on SteamClient.Apps.GetMyAchievementsForApp, no account setup required
Hide the badge while a game is launching, using
SteamClient.Apps.RegisterForGameActionStart/End ('LaunchApp' action),
registered once at plugin mount with a 20s safety timeout in case
GameActionEnd doesn't fire reliably
Restore badge z-index so it still renders above the native bottom bar
during normal library browsing
Update README (features, requirements, project structure, limitations)

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.6 — Brings back Steam's own mini achievement row on the game-details page and updates
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Brings back Steam's own mini achievement row on the game-details page and updates
development dependencies with security fixes.

### Fixed

- Stop drawing a plugin-owned achievement row. Steam's native mini achievements row returns
  because the plugin supplies the `onSeek` prop that the Gaming Mode game page omits
  ([#13540](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/13540)), so Steam's own
  layout, count format, progress bar, navigation, and visibility rules apply on all three
  game-details routes. Turning the feature off hides the row without a reload. The approach
  matches Decky Metadata v0.6.2.

### Security

- Update `happy-dom` from 20.11.6 to 21.0.4, `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker` from 4.1.11 to
  4.1.12, `vite` from 8.3.0 to 8.3.6, `fast-uri` from 3.1.6 to 3.1.9, and `source-map-js`
  from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2, resolving 18 GitHub Dependabot alerts in development-only
  dependencies. The `deepmerge` advisory (GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4) has no patched release and
  affects only the build-time `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve`.

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.5 — Releases the old game-details page promptly when navigation removes the whole PlayBar
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Releases the old game-details page promptly when navigation removes the whole PlayBar.

### Fixed

- Detect when navigation detaches the row's entire PlayBar and remove the injected row,
  observer, and stale page references instead of retaining them until another event.

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.4 — Restores the mini achievement progress row on the November 2026 Steam client and updates
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Restores the mini achievement progress row on the November 2026 Steam client and updates
the frontend test toolchain.

### Fixed

- Restore the achievement progress row beside Play Time after Steam removed its native
  `MiniAchievements` component. The plugin draws the row in Steam's PlayBar layout from
  Steam's achievement progress cache, keeps it hidden when totals are unavailable or an
  uninstalled game has no unlocked achievements, and does not duplicate a native row
  ([#14](https://github.com/beallio/Decky-UI-Restored/issues/14)).
- Poll Steam's achievement progress cache on a bounded retry schedule after requesting an
  update, so a response that arrives late still appears without navigating away. Ported
  from the Decky Metadata fix (`fab5c51`, `6e4d8ac`).

### Security

- Update `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker` from 4.1.10 to 4.1.11, preventing path traversal
  and arbitrary file reads through redirect mocks (GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9).

stevensnoeijen/decky-insignia.body:
Initial release of the Insignia Decky plugin.

Features:
- Quick Access Menu panel showing live Insignia network stats: active
  games and player counts, with manual refresh and 60s background
  polling.
- Active Games sub-page listing per-game player counts, distinguishing
  "offline" from "Insignia service unreachable" states.
- Events page listing upcoming Insignia events/tournaments (14-day
  lookahead window).
- Xbox-ROM playcount badge on library game pages and home-page poster
  tiles, gated to titles matched against the Insignia game list, with
  a toggle in Settings.

rayekkk/deckyvibrancehdr.body:
### ✨ Added

- **About:** **Use Rayek's store** makes Rayek's store Decky's store channel after you confirm, so Decky's Store
  tab lists Rayek's plugins and offers their updates.

### 🔧 Changed

**Menu**
- Descriptions use plain words instead of terms such as LUT, EDID or gamut. Control names are unchanged.
- **Last applied** replaces "Last LUT sent" under **Now** and also appears for SDR on screens that use the
  additional colour table above 200%.
- While the plugin starts, the menu shows a spinner.
- If the plugin cannot start, it says **Decky Vibrance HDR unavailable** with the reason, a **Try again**
  button and the Updates section, so a broken install can still be updated.
- Texts use American spelling ("colors") and a single "…" character.
- While an external display is connected, it explains that your saved settings apply again once you
  unplug it.
- It checks for changes every 3 seconds while idle, and every second while colors are being prepared or
  something needs attention.

**Errors**
- A setting that fails after you close the menu now shows a **Decky Vibrance HDR** message with the
  reason, instead of the slider silently moving back the next time you open it.
- A change the plugin refuses now also says why under that switch, slider or **Back to defaults**, until
  you use that control again.

**About**
- It is the new last row of the menu. Its page shows the version, author and license, with **Updates** at
  the bottom; Updates is no longer on the main menu.

**Updates**
- Wording now matches the other plugins: **Installed version**, **Checking GitHub…**,
  **Download <version>** and **<version> downloaded**, with the saved file shown as `~/Downloads/…` and a shorter
  install hint.
- A failed check or download shows **Could not complete** with the reason in the section instead of a
  message over the screen.
- When no release can be offered (none published yet, or its ZIP is not ready), the section says why
  instead of "Up to date".

**Sliders**
- A switch or reset no longer jumps ahead of a slider change you made before it; changes reach the
  plugin in the order you made them.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Display**
- Disabling the plugin or restarting Decky puts the original colors back even when the plugin was in the
  middle of another display change.
- A screen that reports no EDID at all is treated as standard gamut, as gamescope does, so 101% no longer
  jumps to the strongest SDR setting there.
- An unusual HDR entry in a screen's EDID no longer hides what the rest of the EDID says about HDR.
- When the plugin starts while docked and the display server answers slowly, it no longer takes its
  color calibration from the external display.

**Sliders**
- Slider and switch changes wait less for background display checks when the display server answers
  slowly.

**Settings**
- Settings survive a power cut right after a change, and files left by an interrupted save are cleaned
  up.
- A damaged settings file no longer resets everything: the plugin goes back to the last good copy it
  keeps beside it, keeps the damaged file as `settings.json.corrupt-…` and says so in the menu.

**Updates**
- Downloads accept only the release ZIP GitHub lists for this plugin, with the exact size and SHA-256
  GitHub reports, and every file in it is checked before saving.
- A download is refused unless the release is newer than the installed one.
- Stopping or updating the plugin no longer waits for a slow or stuck update check.
- A download that ends early is reported as failed instead of being kept, and a download in progress
  stops when the plugin stops.

**Errors**
- Messages in the menu no longer show folders that contain your user name; the full details are in the
  Decky log.

### 🔧 Changed

**Menu**
- A backend that is slow to answer is shown as **Waiting for backend** (a change) or
  **Backend unavailable** (a read) instead of a silent spinner, also after the panel was closed and reopened.
- The **Retry** button is gone; the open panel already asks again every second, so it never did anything
  extra.
- Clearer wording for what to do when a setting cannot be applied, and for the SDR and HDR slider
  descriptions.

**Updates**
- The result fields can be reached with the gamepad, and the section keeps its focus when the plugin
  becomes ready or loses its display.

**Install**
- Instructions now match Decky: turn on Developer mode, choose **Browse** next to
  **Install Plugin from ZIP File**, accept Decky's warning and confirm. That replaces the installed version itself,
  so there is no need to uninstall first, and settings are always kept.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Settings**
- An empty settings file no longer keeps the controls paused forever. It can be left by an interrupted
  first start, or by version 1.0.0 after a power loss, and now loads as defaults.
- A settings file that cannot be used (broken JSON, wrong content, or nesting deep enough to break the
  reader) no longer stops the plugin or stalls startup.
- Such a file is kept as `settings.json.corrupt-<time>`, the plugin starts from defaults, and
  **Settings reset** in the menu names the kept file.
- Your last slider change is saved even when a slow display server delays shutdown.
- Disabling or uninstalling the plugin, or restarting Decky, saves your last slider change and puts the
  original colors back whenever Decky lets the plugin shut down.
- On Odin 3 this usually failed, because Decky stopped the plugin halfway and the effect stayed on
  screen until gamescope restarted. Decky can still stop a plugin before its shutdown starts
  ([decky-loader#975](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader/issues/975)): after a restart the plugin
  applies your settings again anyway, but after disabling or uninstalling the colors can stay until gamescope
  restarts.

**Display**
- A single slow display query no longer drops the plugin into **Plugin not ready** for a moment, and can
  no longer leave a false "another plugin" conflict warning behind. Only a real gamescope restart reconnects.
- A reconnect that fails with an error is retried instead of leaving the plugin not ready, and a color
  table that keeps failing is retried every 16 s rather than rebuilt every 4 s.
- Waking the device twice in quick succession reapplies your color settings again; before, the second
  wake could skip it until the next one.
- Waking up in a dock no longer sends the built-in screen's settings to the external display for the
  few seconds before the plugin notices the dock.
- The "another plugin is driving the same SDR setting" warning now appears only while that plugin is
  actually writing and fades once it stops. It also no longer prevents the plugin from restoring an SDR value
  gamescope dropped.
- Switching an effect off restores the right previous value after a lost reply, a brief disconnect, a
  return from an external display or another tool's color table.
- A change whose confirmation was lost is still undone; before, the boost could stay on.
- After gamescope restarts, the value another tool set on the new session is the one restored.
- Switching an HDR or SDR look on while the display server is slow to answer no longer forgets another
  tool's color table.
- The panel is judged the way gamescope judges it: an EDID without color data counts as a standard
  (Rec.709) panel with D65 white, and odd red values are taken as they are.
- On sessions where gamescope does not publish its EDID path, the built-in panel's EDID is read from the
  kernel. A standard-gamut panel whose information cannot be read for a moment keeps its own mapping.
- The items above used to put a standard screen on the wide-gamut mapping, where every setting is much
  stronger.
- Docking is read from the display server that reports it. Lasting errors are logged once rather than on
  every retry, and in Desktop Mode the plugin no longer logs every X server every few seconds while it waits for
  gamescope.

**SDR**
- 100% writes gamescope's own default, which is neutral on every panel, so it stays neutral even when the
  panel could not be identified.

**HDR**
- 100% no longer briefly shows **building the LUT...** for a table it never builds.

**Updates**
- A successful download clears the error of an earlier failed attempt, and checking again, or a check
  that fails, keeps a finished download of the same release.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Settings**
- Saved settings are protected when the plugin cannot read them or Decky stops during startup.
  Controls now wait for settings to load instead of replacing your choices with defaults.
- Startup and display checks no longer get stuck on invalid settings or display-information files.

**Errors**
- Startup errors now explain what failed. A settings-file problem is no longer described as a missing
  Game Mode connection or a failed save.

**Menu**
- Slow or missing backend replies no longer let repeated status checks build up a queue of requests.
- Status checking resumes when the pending call finishes, keeping newer choices made after reopening the
  menu or using **Back to defaults**.

**Updates**
- Update checks and downloads keep their progress when you close and reopen the Quick Access Menu.
  Completed download paths and errors remain available.
- Reopening the menu no longer starts duplicate update requests, buttons from a closed menu cannot start
  another operation, and the installed version is reused instead of fetched again each time.

### 🔧 Changed

**Performance**
- Much faster controls on Armada devices running Decky through emulation. On Odin 3, saturation
  changes took about 0.6 seconds for HDR and 0.7 seconds for SDR, and turning an effect off during a build took
  41–121 ms. Results may vary by device and workload; ordinary SteamOS keeps its existing execution path.
- Faster color-LUT generation, and recent results are reused when you return to a previous
  saturation value. LUT resolution and color calculations are unchanged.
- Fewer repeated display checks, unnecessary saves and rebuilds, leaving more room for the controls
  to respond to your next change.

**Errors**
- Connection problems and failed changes are shown more clearly, and the plugin retries operations that
  could not be completed.

**Display**
- Better recovery after sleep, temporary display connection problems and changes between the built-in
  screen and an external monitor.
- Better detection of the panel's color capabilities and HDR support.

**Updates**
- Better update detection, including preview versions, and more reliable downloads on slow connections.
- Stricter checks of update files; failed downloads or packaging attempts keep the previous usable file.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Menu**
- The "Backend unavailable - python exception" message that could prevent the plugin menu from working.

**Sliders**
- Sliders keep your latest selection instead of jumping back to an older value, and closing and
  reopening the menu no longer brings back outdated changes.
- Rapid slider moves and repeated toggles no longer create a long queue of work. Turning an effect off
  or resetting settings cancels changes you no longer want.

**Settings**
- Settings are saved more reliably, including when Decky stops during startup. Slow or failed saves no
  longer hold up the controls or prevent a reset.

**Display**
- Disabling the plugin restores the previous display settings more reliably, including when another tool
  has changed them while the plugin was active.
- Returning saturation to neutral no longer leaves an older color effect active.

**Updates**
- Download folders and filenames containing special characters are handled correctly.

### 🔧 Changed
- **HDR:** the status shows the saturation of the last LUT successfully sent, without claiming gamescope has
  confirmed loading it.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Display**
- Failed HDR and SDR look builds or replacements are retried. An older working file no longer counts as
  a completed slider change.

**Errors**
- SDR, SDR look and HDR errors are kept independently. A successful operation on one control no longer
  hides another control's failed apply or reset.

**SDR**
- Enabling again after a failed release preserves the original baseline instead of capturing the plugin's
  own value.
- Missing SDR properties and failed initial SDR writes are retried. A missing property is recreated only
  after confirming gamescope is still reachable.
- The standard-gamut SDR look above 200% now converts gamescope's generic source gamut to BT.2020 for ICtCp
  and back before clipping. Native white from EDID is adapted to D65; unreadable white falls back to D65.

**Sliders**
- Pending edits remain visible, and outdated status responses cannot overwrite newer slider values.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/parvagans/achievement-companion/compare/v0.38.1...v0.38.2

# v0.38.2

## RetroAchievements Architecture Overhaul

This release rebuilds how Achievement Companion retrieves, stores, and synchronizes RetroAchievements data. Existing features now share a persistent data foundation designed to reduce redundant requests, handle provider interruptions, and keep progress consistent across Quick Access, full-screen pages, and Steam integrations.

### What's New

**Unified caching and synchronization**

* Replaced fragmented RetroAchievements data paths with shared canonical resources backed by persistent SQLite storage.
* Introduced resource-specific freshness policies so profile data, game progress, Community statistics, catalogues, and Rich Presence refresh independently.
* Concurrent consumers share in-flight requests instead of downloading the same data separately.
* Valid cached responses survive plugin restarts and remain available when a refresh fails.

**Centralized request management**

* Routed RetroAchievements requests through one scheduler with pacing, request priorities, bounded retries, and shared provider cooldowns.
* Manual retries follow the same scheduling and cooldown rules.
* Navigation and targeted updates reuse available data rather than triggering broad profile refreshes or repeated history imports.

**Consistent and durable data**

* Added publication ownership and revision tracking so delayed responses and database reads cannot overwrite newer progress.
* Derived presentations retain their source revisions, allowing re-entered pages to rebuild locally when canonical data changes while preserving open-page navigation.
* Completion-library refreshes assemble and validate the paginated collection before replacing the previous complete snapshot.
* Durable invalidation and shutdown handling preserve authorized work across consumer cancellation and asynchronous storage operations.

**Incremental history and verified discovery**

* Achievement history uses bounded, resumable imports with atomic checkpoints and incremental synchronization.
* Subset discovery retains verification checkpoints and established relationships through partial responses or interrupted work.
* Community resources update shared consumers independently and preserve valid statistics when optional requests fail.
* Added synchronization diagnostics, sanitized exports, and targeted recovery actions.

**Independent Rich Presence synchronization**

* Separated Current Game freshness from the general dashboard cache.
* Integrated game lifecycle events and bounded visible-session checks with the shared request infrastructure.
* Ordered launch verification and corroborated ROM-session evidence so delayed results cannot replace a newer session.
* Preserved recent-session evidence for Continue Playing while authoritative Recently Played data catches up.

### Additional Improvements

* Preserved native controller focus across Community loading and ready states.
* Adjusted the full-screen RetroAchievements profile header to give account names sufficient space.
* Allowed long Quick Access game titles to wrap without a two-line cutoff.
* Added a green activity indicator beside Current Game when RetroAchievements Rich Presence reports active play.

---

**The familiar Achievement Companion experience, supported by a shared, persistent, and more resilient RetroAchievements data architecture.**

Search and display controls make it easier to find an achievement and return to your place. ### What's New **Up Next Across Achievement Companion** * Achievement Companion’s full-screen Game Overview shows up to three recommendations. Open their details, jump to them in Achievements, or hide and restore suggestions. * Quick Access dashboards now show game progress and a recommended achievement for the current or a recently played game. Open its details, skip it, or browse its achievement list without leaving Quick Access. * Compact Game pages show up to three expandable recommendations alongside Achievements, Actions, Game Info, goal settings, and full-screen access. * Hidden suggestions and RetroAchievements Beat or Master goals stay shared between Quick Access and the full-screen Game page. A full-screen achievement jump can reveal an Up Next choice without changing saved search or filters.

**Up Next on Native Steam Game Pages** * Matched RetroAchievements shortcuts gain an Up Next tab between Activity and Your Stuff, with recommendations for the selected Beat or Master goal. * Select a recommendation or an Activity unlock to find it in Steam’s native achievement list. Press X to skip a focused recommendation, or use Suggestions to restore hidden choices. * Win Condition, Progression, and Missable labels appear on recommendations and in the native achievement list where available.

**Achievement Browsing and Details** * Search achievement titles and descriptions, sort results, and choose Detailed or Compact rows in Quick Access and full-screen views. Full-screen game libraries also gain Sort & View. * Quick Access achievements open in a shared details modal over the current screen. Closing it restores the originating list, filters, search, scroll position, and controller focus. * Quick Access achievement lists show every matching result without paging controls. **Game-Page Badges** * Choose the new monochrome Minimal badge or the existing colorful Classic badge. Classic remains the default, and switching styles preserves saved Classic colors. * Both styles support three sizes, six positions, controller activation, and Left/Right navigation between neighboring badges. Minimal includes a subtle loading animation. ### Additional Improvements * Quick Access profiles have clearer progress and artwork fallbacks; selecting the identity card opens the full-screen profile. * Switching provider credentials clears account-specific data and prevents an earlier refresh from displaying results from the previous account. * Failed loads surface a retryable error. Steam scans preserve earlier unlock history when an individual game refresh fails and update progress as games finish. * RetroAchievements game titles omit the `~Homebrew~`, `~Unlicensed~`, `~Prototype~`, `~Demo~`, and `~Hack~` catalog markers without changing game matching. * Selected theme colors carry through more dashboard, profile, history, settings, and controller-focus surfaces. --- **Find your next achievement wherever you open a game, then return to where you left off.**

# v0.36.5

## Full-Screen Game Experience Overhaul

A complete redesign of the full-screen game experience for Steam and RetroAchievements, built around personal accomplishments, achievement progression, and community insights.

### What's New

**Redesigned Game Overview**

* New, non-scrollable dashboard optimized for Steam Deck.
* Improved progress tracking, game artwork, and latest achievement unlocks.
* Dedicated milestone presentations for Beaten, Mastered, and Perfected games.

**Up Next — Achievement Recommendations**

* Three suggested achievements based on game progression and available provider data.
* Community unlock percentages, rarity indicators, and achievement classifications.
* Hide unwanted suggestions and restore them anytime.
* Jump directly to recommended achievements or open their details.

**RetroAchievements Goals**

* Choose between **Beat** and **Master** as your personal objective.
* Set a global preference or override individual games.
* Goal-aware recommendations and completion milestones.
* Full support for Hardcore and Softcore accomplishments.

**SteamHunters & Community Insights**

* Improved achievement obtainability and completion statistics.
* SteamHunters points, community completion rates, and set information.
* Streamlined Game Info and access to detailed community statistics.

**Steam Deck Navigation**

* Improved controller navigation throughout the full-screen experience.
* Contextual achievement shortcuts.
* Organized Actions and Manage Suggestions menus.
* Consistent footer navigation and controller focus.

### Additional Improvements

* Refined achievement presentation and information density.
