lopesleo/decktools.name: v0.5.0 — SLSsteam injection overhaul
lopesleo/decktools.body:
## What's new

### SLSsteam injection
- Injection now targets `/usr/bin/steam` on SteamOS — survives Steam client updates without needing to repatch
- Fallback to `steam.sh` on desktop Linux
- Active verification via `/proc/*/maps` before attempting any patch

### Headcrab repair
- Full recovery sequence: reset → Steam bootstrap reconfiguration → repatch
- Orange banner on the main page now detects unknown hash automatically and shows the repair button directly
- Toast shows progress and duration hint (~20 s)

### Depot downloads
- Per-depot OS detection via steamcmd API
- Support for `DepotDownloader` binary name alongside `DepotDownloaderMod`

### Installer
- Downloads all `enter-the-wired` companion scripts into a temp dir and runs with correct working directory

### UI
- Settings: bottom spacer so content clears the Steam Deck controller bar
- i18n: new strings for headcrab repair feedback (EN + PT-BR)

## Installation

Download `DeckTools.zip`, extract and copy the `DeckTools/` folder to `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/` on your Deck, then restart Decky Loader.

Ou instale selecionando o zip baixado, na opção de modo desenvolvedor do Decky Loader.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/lopesleo/DeckTools/compare/v0.4.4...v0.5.0

lopesleo/decktools.name: v0.4.4 — Game info card, download speed, library size indicators
lopesleo/decktools.body:
## What's new in v0.4.4

### UI
- **Game info card** — before downloading, shows game name, developer, Metacritic score, platform tags, achievements count, PT-BR support, and required storage
- **Download progress on main page** — progress bar with percentage, bytes read, and real-time download speed (MB/s) now visible directly in the game list, not just in Game Detail
- **Library picker size indicators** — each storage path shows a disk usage bar, free space in GB, and a color-coded fit indicator (green = fits, yellow = tight, red = won't fit)
- **SLScheevo hint** — if a game has achievements but SLScheevo is not configured, a warning card is shown with setup instructions

### Fixes
- **Game size for non-installed games** — fixed: was always showing 0 due to broken SteamSpy fallback (SteamSpy has no `size` field). Now parses storage requirement directly from Steam store API `pc_requirements` HTML
- **Morrenus search by name** — fixed: search results were empty because `NativeAsyncClient` silently ignores `params=` kwarg; URL now built with `urlencode`
- **Uninstall read-only ACF** — fixed: uninstall failed on games repaired with `chmod 444` ACF; now applies `chmod 644` before removing the file
- **Remove appaccesstokens.json** — removed sensitive token database from git history

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/lopesleo/DeckTools/compare/v0.4.3...v0.4.4

lopesleo/decktools.name: v0.4.3 — DRM & Launcher Notices
lopesleo/decktools.body:
## What's new

### DRM & Launcher Notices (before download)
- Added informational notices in the **Add Game** section, displayed below the AppID field before clicking *Download Manifest*
- Notices are fetched from the Steam store API via backend (avoids CSP restrictions in Decky's Chromium context)
- Detects: **Denuvo Anti-Tamper**, third-party DRM, and external launchers (EA App, Ubisoft Connect, Rockstar Games Launcher, Battle.net, Epic Games, Xbox App, 2K Launcher, Bethesda.net)
- Notices are **informational only** — amber card with left border accent and bullet list

### Update Check Reliability
- Fixed update baseline being built from SteamCMD (current remote) instead of depotcache (what's installed), causing checks to always return "up to date"
- Post-download snapshot now saves exact manifest IDs from the API instead of scanning depotcache

### Download Stability
- Removed `-validate` flag from DepotDownloaderMod to prevent IOException when Steam has game files open
- File lock errors are now treated as non-fatal and skipped instead of aborting the download

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/lopesleo/DeckTools/compare/v0.4.2...v0.4.3

santojon/deck-shelves.name: Deck Shelves v3.4.1
santojon/deck-shelves.body:
- **Profiles say whether they switch your shelves**: a profile that also switches your shelves is marked "Includes shelves", you can turn that on or off at any time, new profiles include the shelves by default, and every profile text and prompt now says what applying it really does.

- **A restore point before every risky change**: switching profiles (by hand or by a trigger), importing anything and signing in with a different Steam account first save a snapshot, labelled with what made it.

- **Snapshots are easy to find**: the Backup tab explains backups and snapshots, says when the last one was made and has a **Restore a snapshot** button; recovery notices lead there. The snapshot screens say when snapshots are made and how long they are kept.

- **No more leftover files**: unreadable settings copies and interrupted writes no longer pile up, and **Delete all** clears every snapshot and leftover while keeping your current settings.

- **Importing is clearer**: **Choose file…** comes first, the screen shows whether the file is there before you confirm, a missing `deck-shelves-shelves.json` falls back to your full `deck-shelves.json` backup, and failed imports say why.

- **Each Steam account keeps its own shelves**: on a shared Deck, every account that signs in gets its own shelves, smart shelves, saved filters and profiles, and switching accounts swaps them (with a snapshot first). A new account is asked whether to copy the current shelves or start fresh; nothing is ever deleted. Prefer one set for everyone? Turn off **Separate settings per Steam account** in Settings → Backup. Your account ID is never stored or sent, and clearing the Steam client's storage no longer makes every account choose again.

- **Updates on your other devices show up right**: a game installed only on another device offers that copy's Update or Pause, as Steam's menu does, instead of Stream, and a game updating on the Deck appears on update shelves even when Steam marks it as unsupported there.

- **Steam and Quick Access buttons work in games started from the Home (#135)**: launching a game from the Home no longer leaves both buttons doing nothing until the game is closed.

santojon/deck-shelves.name: Deck Shelves v3.4.0
santojon/deck-shelves.body:
- **The Quick Access tab stays on after the restart it asks for**: turning the own tab on and choosing "Restart now" no longer brings it back switched off, and a setting changed right before Steam restarts is no longer undone at the next start.

- **Games waiting for an update update instead of launching**: on a game with a pending update, the View button and the game menu now start with Update, as in Steam's own menu, and the "Update pending" filter also finds games whose update is required.

- **Showcase mode stops on any input**: the keyboard, the mouse and the Deck's touch screen now stop it as the controller does, and it no longer starts while you are using them.

- **Turning the plugin off and on in Decky Loader works**: Deck Shelves comes back right away instead of staying stopped until Steam restarts.

- **The menu button behaves normally with "Use shelf as Recents"**: it opens Deck Shelves' menu only on the replaced row and on Deck Shelves cards; everywhere else Steam handles it.

- **Settings from older versions load cleanly**: shelves saved with old on/off flags no longer cause a validation error at every start.

- **Reordering by touch or mouse keeps every move**, and Steam's logs no longer fill with a navigation warning.

- **"Add to shelf" in every game menu**: Steam's library menus keep the plugin's entries while the menu redraws, and no longer lose them on the first menu after Steam starts when other menu plugins are installed.

- **Store game names read correctly**: names with "&" no longer show as "&" on online shelves, and such games are matched to your library when owned games are hidden.

- **"Use shelf as Recents" works on the Steam Deck's beta client**: Steam's Recents row shows your first shelf, keeps the focus when its games change, and goes back to Steam's own games as soon as you turn the option off.

- **Add a game to a hand-ordered smart shelf from the library**: the library card's menu now lists smart shelves that keep a manual order, for adding and removing.

- **Games you hid in Steam stay off your shelves**, as in Steam's own library: shelves built from a library tab or a collection leave them out (a shelf on the Hidden tab, or filtered to "Hidden only", still shows them), and smart shelves without a visibility condition (the ones you created before 3.3.4) gain the same visible "Exclude hidden" condition new ones have — once; remove it afterwards and it stays removed.

- **Hide a game on a smart shelf too**: the card's X button and the game menu's Hide now work on smart shelves, and so does removing a game you added to one.

- **The refresh card reshuffles every time**: on the Roulette and any shelf in random order, each press of the refresh card or of the shelf's Refresh action gives a new order.

- **Shelves in the right place on the beta client's Big Art home**: the current-game row is now recognised in every language and the shelves sit right after it.

- **Safe mode catches a home that fails every other start**: the shelves switch off when the home screen failed to finish loading on three of the last six Steam starts; leaving safe mode starts the count over.

- **Better bug reports**: System information and the pre-filled bug report now say how the session booted (origin, phase timings, watchdog verdict, long tasks, seeded cache), warnings and errors always reach the Diagnostic log, and an empty wishlist shelf always says why there.

- **Lighter visibility rules**: performance and peripheral checks behind visibility rules are answered from a short-lived backend cache instead of re-reading the system on every evaluation; System information still reads the hardware live.

- **Shelves placed right in every Steam language**: the Home now recognises Steam's own rows and tabs in any language, not only English and Portuguese.

- **Game pages open with the focus on them**: opening a game from the Home no longer leaves its page with nothing selected.

- **Tags stay on the card you touch**: discount and "New" tags no longer vanish from a card you touch or point at with a mouse.

- **Shelf look settings and global ones work together**: the global section only overrides what you set there, every global choice can go back to "Per shelf", and a reset button returns the whole section to its defaults.

- **Smart shelves use their own settings**: the logo, description, layout and hide options and the auto-pin and auto-collapse rules you set on a smart shelf now work on the Home, the same as on a regular shelf.

- **Game names line up with the card**: centre and right alignment now match the card exactly, and game info shown above the card follows that alignment without leaving the screen.

- **Highlight as many games as you like**: shelves with six or more highlighted games no longer show empty spaces where cards should be.

- **The Installed filter and tab are right for non-Steam games**: Unifideck's games count by their real install state with or without its collections, manual shortcuts, Heroic and emulators keep their own, and Proton / runtimes stay out of the Installed tab.

- **Back from a game page, the focus returns to the same game and shelf**, also when that shelf is further down the page and still loading, and scrolling sideways no longer jumps to another shelf.

- **The wishlist shelf fills after a slow start too.** A slow first answer from the backend no longer leaves it empty for ten minutes.

- **The Steam menu and Quick Access open again while a game is running.** The Home no longer pulls the controller focus back to a shelf card behind the game, and it runs no timers at all while a game runs — non-Steam shortcuts included — while the screen is off or while the device sleeps.

- **Game info above the cards no longer repeatedly rebuilds its own label.** Late-arriving titles and status changes still update, and toggling the option back on restores the label.

- **Smoother controller navigation on custom Home shelves.** Remove a focus-border adjustment that could repeatedly recalculate styling across the whole Home screen. Steam's native focus border is retained; the Recents replacement and Round Compatibility setting still work as before.

- **A "Show or hide settings" row under the master toggle opens or closes the quick-settings sidecar**, the same panel the double dpad-right opens, for anyone who prefers a tap. The sidecar is titled "Show or hide" in a tab header, and Ctrl+Shift+S opens it by default.

- **Quick Search lands on the game every time**, including games further along a row or on a shelf below the fold, and reopening it keeps the previous text selected instead of appending to it.

- **Pinned games, play history, queues and custom tags now work.** Once a shelf, smart shelf, saved filter or profile uses one of these sources, the game menu of a shelf card gains a **Lists** submenu that pins a game, queues it for this session or until you play it, and edits its tags; play history fills by itself, and Parser categories reads the categories your ROM manager or launcher integration gave each shortcut. Profile triggers now keep the settings you change while they are active, and the shortcut editor takes up to three buttons and can be cancelled.

- **Typing in Quick Search with the on-screen keyboard works again**, and profile triggers are more dependable: switching them off restores your previous settings, they survive a restart, and they wait for real readings before acting. Update notifications can now be muted like the other areas.

- **Fixes for profiles, sync and shortcuts.** Linked profiles keep applying their shelves after a restart; cross-device sync keeps your latest profile and saved-filter edits and, with a different profile active on each device, one device's look no longer overwrites the other's; keyboard shortcuts keep working in long sessions; Quick Search no longer pops up during a game; a back-grip shortcut no longer makes another shortcut fire twice; turning off the sidecar's button shortcuts now sticks.

- **Safer settings.** A damaged settings copy can no longer replace your last good backup, exports are written safely, and turning the screensaver off after a factory reset gives Steam back its own idle timeout.

- **A bit lighter in the background.** Features you don't use (friends, launchers) no longer keep polling, and update downloads are checked more strictly.

- **Reorder shelves with a controller row by row**: in the Quick Access lists, A on a shelf's name grabs it, the D-pad moves it, A saves and B puts it back, with those buttons shown in Steam's button bar while the row is held. Touch and mouse dragging work as before.

- **Games without artwork look like they do in Steam**: when a cover can't load, the card shows Steam's own dark tile with the game's name.

- **Deck Shelves' own Quick Access tab was rebuilt (experimental)**: under Decky Loader you can turn it on to get Deck Shelves as its own tab right after Performance; restart Steam after enabling. If another host already shows a Deck Shelves tab, that one is used instead.

- **Under the hood, the home-screen rendering code, the plugin's startup, the library code that builds every shelf and the game-menu code were reorganized into smaller pieces, with no change in behavior** — verified on a real Steam Deck. Reloading the plugin now also cleans up its Settings page route.

- **Release builds are a little leaner: diagnostics meant only for a debugger now stay in development builds.** Nothing visible changes.

gooorooox/ce-decky.name: v0.9.35
gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.35

A table that worked on a non-Steam game is now remembered as working for as long as the game's executable stays the same, and FearLess search is ready about an hour after a first install instead of more than five.

## New

- A table that worked on a game with no version number, which is common for non-Steam games, is marked **Worked with this executable** with the solid green ring. It asks for a retest once the game's executable changes.

## Fixes

- FearLess search no longer misses a game whose topic the forum had just moved, and finds a topic titled only in another script for a game that also has an English name.
- A cheat with a fixed list of values offers only that list in **Configure cheats**, with no field to type another, and nothing outside the list is written into the game.
- A value saved outside such a list by an earlier version no longer stops **Apply** and **Load last table & cheats** for the whole table. The cheat's row says so, and choosing a value from the list replaces it.
- A cheat whose only choices are Disabled and Enabled is a plain on/off switch rather than a list.
- In **Advanced…**, **Table sources**, a FearLess refusal is counted once rather than twice, and background reading is no longer counted as a search.

## Changed

- FearLess search stays up to date with far fewer requests to the forum, usually one page a day, so it is refused less often.
- Opening the panel while Cheat Engine is running shows what pinned values hold in the game now, not what they held when the panel was last open.
- **Configure cheats** moves helper scripts that change nothing in the game by themselves behind **Scripts**. The values inside them stay in the list and show their current value without you switching anything on.
- The record of tables that worked is converted once when this version first starts, with every mark kept. An older version cannot read it, so going back to one means every working table asks for a retest.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. If the panel does not offer it, open **Advanced…**, then **Plugin updates**, and press **Check now**. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 or later installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.35.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept. The previous record of tables that worked is kept beside the new one as `table_compatibility.before-schema-4.json`.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

<!-- ce-decky:notes-end -->

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.34...v0.9.35

gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.32

Lets more non-Steam games, and games on a Proton your Linux distribution installed, start Cheat Engine.

## Fixes

- Some non-Steam games running under Proton could not start Cheat Engine: **Advanced** said "Proton not observed" and **Load table & start CE** said the game was not running.
- A game running under a Proton your Linux distribution installed, such as `proton-cachyos` on CachyOS, can start Cheat Engine instead of failing with "no installed Proton tool matches".
- Cheat Engine stops by itself shortly after the game closes. It could stay attached, with the game still shown as running and **Change** unavailable, until you pressed **Stop CE**.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 or later installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.32.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.31...v0.9.32

gooorooox/ce-decky.name: v0.9.31
gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.31

Fixes cases, in some tables, where a cheat stayed on or came back after you switched it off, or where **Load last table & cheats** failed; Auto-load also gives a game time to load before it starts.

## Fixes

- In tables that keep a script's own switches outside it, switching that script on no longer leaves them on without saying so, from the panel, in **Configure cheats** or at Auto-load.
- **Disable all** also puts back a cheat that showed off but was still active in the game, and a cheat it switched off no longer comes back at the next Auto-load.
- **Load last table & cheats** no longer fails because of a value set for a cheat that was off, or a setting inside a script that stays off.
- A script cheat with settings, such as jump or health, stays on while you switch other cheats; switching a script off switches off everything under it.
- A cheat inside a script that has not run yet can be switched on, in **Configure cheats** and from a pinned cheat.
- A table is no longer said to be written for a different build of the game when the game closed or every pattern it looks for is there, and a working table gets its green check.
- No more "Cheat Engine could not be launched" after a game exits or crashes with Cheat Engine attached.

## Changed

- **Load last table & cheats** waits until the game has been running for 10 seconds, and counts the wait down, so a table is not marked as not working because the game was still loading.
- **Configure cheats** opens with every cheat collapsed, and lists under **Scripts** only the scripts that hold other scripts.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.31.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.30...v0.9.31

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.1-beta.4
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
### Local diagnostics

- Add exact 32,768-byte and 32,769-byte Faceplate GIF transfer tests with the same visible pattern and timing. Record the requested size and the transfer result in the local report.

### Testing the 32 KiB boundary

In **Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics**, open **Faceplate GIF transfer test** with **Test**. Send **32,768 bytes (exact)** once, then **32,769 bytes (exact)** once. If a test times out, lacks a final confirmation, or hits flash protection, stop there. Choose **Export a local diagnostic** once after your last attempt.

A newly confirmed transfer at 32,768 bytes and a refusal at 32,769 bytes before any image data would suggest a 32 KiB limit on that Faceplate.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1-beta.4/CHANGELOG.md#161-beta4)

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.1-beta.3
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
### Fixed

- Reduce the GIF payload for Weather and Dashboard, including animated artwork behind Dashboard. The decoded pixels, frame timing, and loop behaviour are unchanged. Static images and frames that do not benefit from compression keep their existing encoding.
- Regenerate cached Weather and Dashboard GIFs with the new encoding.

### Local diagnostics

- Add an optional **Faceplate GIF transfer test** under **Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics**. Open it with **Test**, choose a size and send one dim pattern at a time.
- Report the actual GIF size and distinguish a new confirmation, an already stored GIF, a refusal before image data, and a missing final confirmation. The results are included in **Export a local diagnostic**. No automatic upload or private sign-in is needed.

### What to test

For [#14](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/14) and [#15](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/15), try the Weather preview or Dashboard that previously failed. If the problem returns, use the optional size test described in the [beta guide](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1-beta.3/docs/BETA_1.6.1.md), then export one diagnostic. Do not reset your settings just to run the test. Smaller files may help, but the reports do not yet establish a panel capacity, firmware fault or flash fault.

Existing settings and prepared artwork are kept. The Stable update channel remains the way back to 1.6.0 with current settings.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1-beta.3/CHANGELOG.md#161-beta3--2026-11-09)

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.1-beta.2
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
### Local diagnostics

- Expand the one-action local report with bounded process/service observations, serial-port holders, available USB descriptors and runtime power-management settings, recent Linux USB events and storage/permission facts.
- Capture a small passive process/USB observation when a transfer fails, at most once per second, retaining up to eight observations until the plugin restarts. Full command lines, personal paths and raw kernel messages are excluded. Nothing is uploaded automatically.
- Distinguish newly acknowledged transfers, stored-content reuse and BEGIN refusals by size. A reused image, bridge revision or descriptor power budget is not evidence of panel capacity, actual power draw, cable quality or flash health.
- Mark inaccessible processes, partial scans, unavailable service buses and missing measurements explicitly. Events not attributable to the Faceplate stay labelled as host USB events.

### Fixed

- Keep live transfer and restoration evidence consistent between diagnostic sections. Missing observations no longer become false negative flags.
- Preserve validated kernel versions and controlled technical field names while continuing to remove credentials and personal paths.

### Testing and recovery

- Keep beta 1 weather/recovery fixes, existing settings and the current GIF transport. Fixed minute remains the default only for new clock configurations; saved Conservative settings are preserved.
- Document the optional GCA reset after saving the report and backing up data to keep. A complete reset deletes GCA settings, saved content and the SteamGridDB key; it does not reset panel firmware or stop an external service.
- Continue investigating [#14](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/14) and [#15](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/15). This beta gathers evidence and does not claim to repair flash memory or resolve every BEGIN refusal. No additional transfer is triggered by exporting the report.

Install through **Settings > Updates > Preferences > Beta**, then check, download and verify **1.6.1-beta.2**, and confirm the update. To return with current settings and media, choose **Stable** and install **1.6.0** through the same flow. See the [beta guide](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1-beta.2/docs/BETA_1.6.1.md).

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.1-beta.1
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
This public beta improves weather refresh after system sleep and makes Faceplate recovery failures easier to understand and report. Stable remains **1.6.0**.

## Fixed

- Use sleep-aware weather freshness and request scheduling, request fresh data after resume and discard responses from an older request generation.
- Respect a Faceplate switched off explicitly in GCA while still allowing weather data to refresh.
- Stop repeating the same rejected image restoration. Show the failure and offer **Resume stored picture** when a power-only recovery is available.
- Show distinct status messages for intentional Off, restoration in progress and restoration needing attention.

## Clock transfer defaults

New configurations default to **Fixed minute**, about **60 transfers per hour**, independently for Home and games. Updating or switching between Stable and Beta preserves existing saved modes, including **Conservative** at about **15 transfers per hour**.

## Local diagnostics

One **Export a local diagnostic** action creates a JSON document with version consistency, key installed-file checks, available OS/kernel information, power intent, transfer stages and weather timing. The same document can be copied if the file cannot be saved. No automatic upload or private GitHub authorization is involved.

## Install or return to Stable

In **Settings > Updates > Preferences**, select **Beta**. Under **Update**, choose **Check now**, **Download and verify**, then **Update and restart Decky** and confirm.

To return, select **Stable** and repeat those steps for **1.6.0**. The stable archive keeps your current settings, keys and prepared media. Returning also brings back 1.6.0's known limitations. Leave the channel on Stable to stay on that release.

[Installation, testing and diagnostic instructions](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1-beta.1/docs/BETA_1.6.1.md)

## Still under investigation

This beta does not establish the cause of GIF BEGIN refusals or flash failures. It adds evidence and recovery handling for [#14](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/14) and [#15](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/15), and a weather fix to test for [#16](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/16). Confirmation on the affected machines is still needed.

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.0
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
### Faceplate clocks

- Add nine standalone clock faces: Meridian, Halo, Almanac, Quadrant, Cardinal markers, Horizon, Column, Week and Date card.
- Offer six palettes, separate Home and in-game selections, 24-hour/AM-PM formats and English/French dates.
- Add Conservative and Fixed minute transfer modes. Clock time advances inside scheduled GIF packets; each mode retains the normal USB and display protections.
- Default standalone clocks to Fixed minute (about 60 transfers per hour) for new configurations, independently for Home and games. Keep existing saved modes, including Conservative (about 15 per hour), when updating or switching channels.
- Extend a standalone clock’s colours onto the light bar using Bottom edge or Whole image sampling.

### Artwork and Home playback

- Open the Faceplate artwork editor directly from a game’s Steam library menu when a Faceplate is detected.
- List customized games in Artwork settings, with per-game layout choices and a confirmed return to the default. Keep prepared files, other games and the Home display intact.
- Add Home playback of prepared library GIFs, in order or randomly, at 5-, 15-, 30- or 60-minute intervals. Playback performs no new download or conversion.
- Reuse prepared artwork for a game, Home or both, with optional Dashboard information. Keep Home copies independent from later game changes.

### Setup, control and performance

- Make guided setup optional, including on first startup and after a settings reset.
- Add a visible Restart setup action that starts a fresh guide while keeping active settings, keys, routes and prepared media.
- Add Faceplate Priority controls: Automatic, GCA Priority and Other app, with separate allowances for Decky Animated Screensaver and Decky Vocal Assistant.
- Reduce repeated work in Audio Sync, move slow Screen Sync registry checks away from frame handling and reuse bounded LED read sessions while keeping reads fresh.
- Retry failed weather requests more quickly within a bounded recovery window, then return to the normal refresh schedule.


### Fixed

- Fix setup exceptions when an existing Home library or standalone clock is selected.
- Prevent an interrupted setup from locking normal displays, quick controls, Settings or updates.
- Fix Restart setup failures caused by an unusable draft, unexpected file owner/type or unavailable archive. Start fresh without resetting active settings, keys, routes or prepared media; keep progress for the current session if its file cannot be written.
- Keep old setup journals from being replayed over current settings at startup. Restart setup and Keep my settings actions do not activate hardware or change the active display.
- Keep setup headings, the restart action and the game artwork editor’s final controls clear of Steam’s top and bottom bars, with internal scrolling.
- Fix the game-summary card extending beyond the other artwork controls and wrap long game titles. Remove the redundant Back bar while preserving Steam’s native return navigation.
- Hide the game-menu Faceplate artwork entry when the device is absent or current detection is unavailable.
- Restore light-bar colour extension for prepared Home artwork and library GIFs without a Steam AppID.
- Preserve confirmed clock playback sessions when renewing packets, replanning playback or changing transfer mode. Avoid redundant power-on commands during normal renewal on the same confirmed connection.
- Prevent slow daylight calculations from being mistaken for a system-clock jump.
- Centre both analog hands on one shared pivot across all five dial designs, and invalidate older cached renders with offset hands.

The clock gallery and usage guides are included in the [1.6.0 guide](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/wiki/Release-1.6.0). These changes do not establish a fix for every Faceplate firmware/flash fault or stale weather after system sleep.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.3.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## More handhelds, more RGB

Ambideck 1.3.0 adds screen-following RGB implementations for Lenovo Legion Go/Go S/Go 2, MSI Claw, compatible AYANEO/AYN Loki/Zotac Zone kernel LEDs, and selected OneXPlayer/OneXFly/AOKZOE models.

- Colours adapt to the available lighting zones: four corners, left/right colours or one shared colour.
- Devices without a native rainbow use one static colour averaged from the last screen colours, with soft white before the first frame.
- Device detection, reconnect recovery and output rate limits keep lighting writes away from screen capture.
- Quick Access shows the detected device and its lighting capability. HueSync handback remains specific to Ally.

**Hardware validation is still outstanding for the new backends and output worker.** Support depends on the exact model, controller firmware/mode and available kernel interfaces. See [RGB compatibility and exclusions](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/blob/release/1.3.0/docs/rgb-protocols.md).

Validation: 146 Python tests passed (1 Linux-only test skipped on macOS), 66 frontend tests passed, TypeScript passed and the production bundle was verified.

### Install

In Game Mode, enable Decky Developer mode, then use **Install plugin from ZIP** with `ambideck.zip`. Existing settings are preserved.

Changes: [PR #3](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/pull/3).

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.2.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## What's new

- **Makes way for screen recorders.** While a recorder such as [Showreel](https://github.com/michpalm/showreel) holds the capture lock (`/run/decky-screen-capture.lock`), Ambideck lets go of gamescope's screen stream and hands the lights back (to HueSync's setting, or the rainbow). When the recording ends it follows again within about a second. The panel shows **Paused while Showreel records** meanwhile.

  gamescope has one screen stream whose size the first reader sets, so without this a recorder would get Ambideck's tiny frames, or both would share a full-size stream, which can crash gamescope. The README's **Screen recorders** section describes the lock for other recorder authors.

## Fixes

- The lock is checked again right before every connection to the stream, not only every half second, so Ambideck never joins a recorder's stream.
- A recorder that crashed and was never cleaned up (a zombie process) doesn't keep Ambideck paused.

## Install

Press **Update** in Ambideck's Quick Access panel, or download `ambideck.zip` below and use Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

Runs on a ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) with Bazzite or SteamOS 3.8.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.1.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## What's new

- **Follow outside games.** "Outside games" is now **Off / Normal colour / Follow**. With Follow, the rings follow the Steam interface just like they follow a game, and keep following without a gap when you quit. If you had **Artwork** selected, it becomes Follow. Following outside games keeps the capture running whenever Game Mode is up (about 7 % of one CPU core, roughly 0.2 W).
- **Dark scenes.** Dim scenes are lifted, so dark games show their colour more clearly. A new **Dark scenes** setting chooses what near-black does: **Glow** (a faint glow, as before) or **Off** (that half of the ring switches off and fades back in).
- **Updates from Quick Access.** Ambideck checks GitHub once a day. When a newer release is out, the panel shows **Update to X.Y.Z**; press **Update** and confirm in Decky's dialog. Decky checks the download against the release's SHA-256 and keeps your settings. **Check for updates** asks right away.

## Fixes

- The light controller is found again if it disappears (for example after the driver reloads), with one log line instead of one per frame.
- Steadier screen capture: buffer checks, evenly spaced retries, and a timeout when the stream never starts.
- HueSync is asked to step aside again when a game starts or quits while Ambideck keeps following.
- Turning the lights off outside games now holds against HueSync, like following does.
- Backend calls no longer block Decky while Ambideck connects to the screen stream.

## Install

Download `ambideck.zip` below, then Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**. From 1.1.0 on, future versions can be installed from Ambideck's own Update button.

Runs on a ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) with Bazzite or SteamOS 3.8.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.0.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
First release of Ambideck: an Ambilight for the ROG Xbox Ally's stick lights.

While a game runs, each half of each stick ring takes the colour of its corner of the screen. When you stop
playing, the lights go back to your normal setting.

## Features

- **Follows the screen** in any game: four corners (top and bottom half of each ring), or one colour per side.
- **Keeps colours alive:** colourful pixels count more than grey ones, so pastel scenes keep their tint, and
  dark scenes still glow faintly.
- **Hands the lights back** to your [HueSync](https://github.com/honjow/HueSync) setting, or to the
  controller's rainbow if you don't use HueSync.
- **Per game:** switch it off for games where it distracts.
- **Outside games:** off, your normal lights, or the colours of a game page's artwork.
- **Docked:** off by default, with one switch to keep it on.
- **Settings:** brightness, colour boost and speed (Smooth, Balanced, Fast), in Quick Access.

## Install

Ambideck is not in the Decky store.

1. Decky → Settings → General → turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Download `ambideck.zip` below.
3. Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

## Tested on

ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) on Bazzite, handheld and docked to a TV. Measured while playing ULTRAKILL: about
+0.18 W on battery and about 7 % of one CPU core.

## Known limitations

- The original ROG Ally and Ally X use the same driver and should work, but their light-zone order is untested.
- HDR games are not tested yet.
- Steam in Bazzite's Game Mode sends no sleep event, so after waking, the colours return within about 2 seconds.

## About

Written with [Claude](https://claude.ai), directed, reviewed and tested on device by the author. Not
affiliated with ASUS, Microsoft, Valve, Philips or any game shown.

jedirhymetrix/decky-bluetooth-order.name: Bluetooth Order v0.1.0
jedirhymetrix/decky-bluetooth-order.body:
## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-11

Initial public release of **Bluetooth Order**.

### Features

- Reorders Steam's existing paired Bluetooth rows in Quick Access and Settings.
- Native order, most recently connected, name A–Z, and name Z–A modes.
- Optional connected-first priority and independently enabled menu overrides.
- Passive, persisted successful-connection history; disconnects retain recency.
- Redacted diagnostics, history reset, and one-button restoration of native order.

### Reliability and distribution

- Scoped mounted-QAM attachment with owned-reference restoration; no root reset
  or automatic service restart.
- Settings adapter recognizes verified shared Decky renderer-patch chains.
- Stale panels disable their controls and explain how to reopen after updating.
- Bounded backend waits, render-loop regressions, isolated QAM session tracking,
  and a hash-checked XML fallback for Decky's frozen Python runtime.
- Immediate observer shutdown skips subscription/retry work when cancellation
  races a completed connection on Python 3.11.
- Complete ESM release ZIP, pinned dependencies, checksums, and CI/release checks.

### Verification and known limits

- User confirmed QAM and Settings working on the tested Deck with Decky 3.2.10.
- Automated frontend, backend, and packaging tests cover sorting, lifecycle,
  observer behavior, archive safety, and release metadata.
- Connection history starts with observed transitions; it cannot reconstruct
  earlier use. Fresh installs default both overrides off.
- Steam UI changes and other plugins' route patches can affect attachment.
  Every TabMaster registration order is not verified.
- Interaction can hold visible ordering. Exact QAM unload restoration can remount
  native rows on a later render. Full boot/resume acceptance remains incomplete.

For installation, privacy, and rollback instructions, see the repository README.

rayekkk/legiongo2companion.body:
### ✨ Added

- **Button mapping:** **Zoom (Steam + LB)** for the Desktop and Page buttons turns on Steam's screen zoom.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Fan Control:** works again after the battery ran completely flat ("Unknown initial EC selector"); Companion
  resets the fan controller's selector to its normal state once and logs the value it found.
- **Fan Control:** an error repeated by several recovery attempts is shown once instead of up to eight times.

### ✨ Added

- **About:** **Use Rayek's store** makes Rayek's store Decky's store channel after you confirm, so Decky's Store
  tab lists Rayek's plugins and offers their updates.
- **Device report:** names what blocks Fan Control (another app holding the fan controller, a conflicting
  driver), lists installed Decky plugins with their version and disabled state, and says whether Fan Control is on.
- **Fan Control:** **Take over fan control** appears when Fan Control is off and blocked. It makes one start
  attempt with every safety check; if another app still uses the fan controller, Fan Control stays off and
  names it.

### 🔧 Changed

**Fan Control**
- "Another app controls the fan" now names the app or driver. A fan reading that merely failed shows
  "Fan reading unavailable" with the reason instead.
- If another app changes the fan speed while Companion controls it, the error names the apps that have
  the fan controller open.
- The curve graph and the full screen editor use the shared frame and colors; B is now labeled "Done"
  while editing.

**Panel**
- The Decky panel now looks and reads like the other Rayek plugins (same layout, texts and states).
- **B** on a page goes back to All Controls instead of closing the Quick Access menu, and the row you
  came from is selected again.
- Leaving Fan Control with an unsaved curve, or TDP with Custom limits not applied, first asks
  **Discard changes?**; Cancel keeps you on the page with your edits.
- TDP and Vibration show a spinner while they start instead of "Initializing...".
- "Discard unsaved changes?" and "Delete profile for …?" now show Steam's warning style.
- Titles and labels use sentence case ("Hardware controls", "Manage modules", "Enable fan control");
  module names stay as they are.
- Toasts last the same in every module (longer for messages of more than one sentence).

**About**
- Shows the plugin's version and author first, then **Save device report**, and **Updates** at the bottom.
- A saved ZIP or device report shows as `~/…` instead of the full path.

**Updates**
- The update texts match the other plugins ("Installed version X", "Up to date", "Could not complete"
  with the reason).
- **Check for updates** asks GitHub again on every click instead of showing a result up to a minute old.
- A second **Download** while one is running is refused at once ("A download is already running.").
- Messages are clearer: a release that cannot be offered says why, a missing file in the release ZIP
  is named, and a network error says what went wrong.
- A release ZIP is fetched only from GitHub's own download servers.
- If something other than a regular file (such as a link) already has the release ZIP's name in
  Downloads, Companion refuses to save there instead of replacing it.
- When **Check for updates** or **Download** fails, the Desktop app shows why and keeps the last
  result, as the Decky panel does.

**Errors**
- A page that cannot read its status says so with one **Try again** button (it was "Retry status",
  "Retry settings" or "Check again").
- When something fails unexpectedly, the panel and the Desktop app show a short message and the details
  go to the Decky log, never file paths.

**Wi-Fi**
- When a band change or reconnect is refused, the Desktop app shows the reason in words instead of an
  internal code such as "unsupported_backend".

**Modules**
- Manage Modules also shows the reason in words when the saved band setting cannot be restored while
  turning Wi-Fi on.

### 🐛 Fixed
- **Settings:** a damaged settings file is kept as `.corrupt-<time>` before it is replaced, so it can still be
  looked at.
- **Settings:** settings that could not be read back are never written.
- **RGB:** when the controller briefly reports an invalid lighting profile, Companion rewrites your lighting
  at once instead of leaving the rings unread until the next restart.

### ✨ Added
- **Controller sleep:** under Gyro & touchpad, choose when detached controllers turn themselves off when unused:
  Never, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes, for both controllers, as in Legion Space.
- **Controller sleep:** until you pick one, Companion changes nothing and shows **Controller default**; the choice
  survives updates, and turning the module off leaves the controllers at their current time.
- **Controller sleep:** Companion checks your choice every two minutes and after a wake or reconnect and sets it
  only on a controller that reports another value, so a controller asleep when you chose gets it once it wakes.
- **Controller sleep:** available on the Legion Go 2 and on the Legion Go with the 2025 controller firmware (beta).

### 🔧 Changed

**Display**
- Needs SteamOS 3.9 or newer, which supports the Legion Go 2 screen natively; the page now holds only
  **Fix HDR brightness in games**.
- The HDR fix stays because without it games on SteamOS 3.9 still read a 1499-nit HDR peak instead of
  the panel's real values; on older SteamOS the page asks you to update SteamOS, and the fix works there too.
- After the update, Companion removes its old display script by itself (only the exact script it
  installed); a Gaming Mode that is already running keeps it until it restarts.
- If Setup had kept your own script as a `.backup`, it is put back on SteamOS 3.8 and left alone on
  3.9, where it would override SteamOS.
- The original EDID copy that the HDR fix restores is now kept root-only in
  `/var/lib/legiongo2companion/` instead of Decky's settings folder; the old copy moves there by itself.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TDP**
- With **Allow up to 50 W** the boost limits hold again; since 2.3.0 the firmware's custom mode put its own
  limits (37/45 W on the Legion Go 2) back within half a second while the page showed 50 W.
- Companion now leaves the firmware a moment to settle before it sets the boost limits.

**Vibration**
- While a controller sleeps or stops answering, Companion no longer keeps resending your settings to
  it, which could make it buzz now and then.
- After a wake it retries only the settings that did not take, and its periodic check slows from
  every 30 seconds to every 5 minutes until the controller answers or is reconnected.
- Controllers no longer buzz when Companion starts, is updated or uninstalled, or when a controller
  is attached or detached, unless their vibration mode really has to change.
- Companion reads each setting first and writes only one that differs, never one it cannot read
  reliably.
- A setting is confirmed only when the controller reports it twice in a row, so a delayed reply no
  longer counts as a failed write (many "did not confirm" log entries) or as a confirmed one.

**Controller sleep**
- A setting is confirmed only when the controller reports it twice in a row, so a delayed
  reply no longer counts as a failed or confirmed write.

**Controller firmware**
- Check, Download and Install need both controllers attached and say so: "Attach both
  controllers to check or install firmware updates."
- Install still refuses a controller below 30% battery.

**Battery**
- When the firmware turns on fast charging and battery protection at once, the page now says the
  charging mode cannot be read instead of showing "Invalid argument".
- The page offers **Reset charging mode to Standard**, and your saved protection choice is applied
  again afterwards.

**Lighting**
- The stick lights are set again once when Companion starts and once shortly after a wake, so they no
  longer stay wrong when the controller wakes with stale values.
- The stick lights now work while one controller is detached (they failed with "The joystick-ring
  interface does not belong to the expected controller.").
- The stick lights are set again after a controller is attached or detached.

**Fan**
- Fan Control no longer turns itself off for good when the fan briefly returns to firmware control on its
  own (seen once while a controller was reattached).
- Companion takes the fan back after its usual safety checks, up to 3 times in 10 minutes.
- Fan Control still turns off when anything else writes the fan speed, and a single misread of the fan
  setting no longer counts as such a write.

### 🗑️ Removed
- **Display:** display modes (PQ, Gamma 2.2, Hybrid), Setup, Reset display fix, Brightness slider in HDR and the
  Restart Gaming Mode buttons are gone from the panel, Desktop app and Manage Modules (SteamOS 3.9 does it).
- **Display:** turning Display off no longer asks for a Gaming Mode restart.

### ✨ Added

**Consoles**
- Companion runs as an early beta on the Legion Go and Legion Go S; each console shows only the
  modules and options that apply to it, in the panel, the Desktop app and Manage Modules.
- Battery, the stick lights and Wi-Fi work on all of them (the stick lights on the Legion Go S need
  its `hid-lenovo-go-s` driver in SteamOS).
- Vibration and Gyro & touchpad work on a Legion Go whose controllers have the 2025 firmware.
- Button mapping, Display, Fan Control and controller firmware stay Legion Go 2 only.
- None of this has been tested on these consoles yet; the README Compatibility table shows what is
  supported, beta or not needed.
- On the Legion Go 2 Z2 (83N1), the power-button light, controller firmware updates and Fan Control
  (beta) now work; Fan Control runs its one-time fan check first. Not tested on an 83N1 yet.

**TDP**
- Uses each console's own firmware limits; **Allow up to 50 W** is offered on the Legion Go (higher risk,
  untested there) but not on the Legion Go S, whose firmware already allows more.
- **Separate battery presets** (under **More**, off by default): Silent, Balanced and Performance use the
  lower limits each console's firmware sets on battery and their usual values on the charger, also in game profiles.
- The Legion Go 2 battery limits are Silent 8/8/20 W, Balanced 16/16/30 W, Performance 20/20/35 W; presets
  switch when you plug in or unplug, and Maximum and Custom are unchanged.

**Lighting**
- The power-button switch now appears on the Legion Go and Legion Go S with a Beta note; it stays
  hidden when the BIOS does not describe the light exactly as expected.

**Vibration**
- On the Legion Go S (beta), **Vibration strength** (Off, Low, Medium, High) and **Touchpad
  vibration**, also per game; the page shows what Companion set because the controller cannot report these.
- On the Legion Go S, Companion sends only the settings you change, so Legion Space's values for
  the others are not overwritten.

**Device report**
- **About → Save device report** (the **Logs** page in the Desktop app) writes a read-only text
  file to your Desktop with hardware and firmware details, firmware tables (DSDT) and EC readings.
- It contains no serial numbers, network names or user names; attach it to a
  [Beta report](README.md#reporting-a-problem-on-legion-go--go-s-beta) from a Legion Go, Legion Go S or new model.

### 🔧 Changed

**Updates**
- Updating from 2.2.x resets the gyro source, battery protection, lighting control and Wi-Fi band
  policy once (Decky runs the old uninstall first); set them again, later updates keep them.
- The gyro source, battery protection, lighting control and Wi-Fi band policy now survive an update
  (the band policy is applied once Wi-Fi has reconnected).

**Display**
- An update reinstalls the script for the panel mode you set up and asks for a Gaming Mode restart only
  when the running Gaming Mode does not already use that exact script (always after updating from 2.1.0 or 2.2.x).
- After updating from 2.1.0, whose script sat in /root where Gaming Mode never read it, the script is
  installed in the right place and the old copy removed; no Setup is needed.

**TDP**
- Presets now come from each console's BIOS table, so every console in the family gets its own firmware
  limits.

**Controller firmware**
- The updater, in the panel and the Desktop app, shows a red **Risk notice** above its
  buttons: it is the only Companion feature that could damage the hardware.
- It has been tested only by reinstalling the firmware already installed, not by updating
  to a newer version; the notice goes away once the next real update has been verified.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Controllers**
- The controller no longer stays dead until a restart, usually after sleep (Legion Go 2, and a
  Legion Go with the 2025 controller firmware), when SteamOS's InputPlumber loses it on a reset or reconnect.
- Companion checks about 17 seconds after a reconnect, a sleep and its own start, and restarts
  InputPlumber once if the controller is still lost; button mapping and gyro source come back on their own.
- That restart happens at most once per 10 minutes and three times per start, and never while
  InputPlumber is stopped or disabled or a firmware update is running.

**TDP**
- **Allow up to 50 W** keeps working after an update without **Retry helper download**; the verified
  `ryzenadj` helper is now kept outside Decky's plugin folder, which every update deletes.
- After updating from 2.2.x the helper is downloaded once in the background at the next start (turning
  **Allow up to 50 W** off cancels it); the firmware limits run until then.
- **Allow up to 50 W** always runs the firmware's custom mode under the higher limits; before, an earlier
  mode (for example Performance) could stay active and replace them.

**Controller firmware**
- Install no longer stops fwupd after a fixed 10 minutes while it is still writing; it
  stops it only after 10 minutes without progress, or 30 in total, asking it to exit cleanly first.

**Install**
- When Decky stops Companion while it is still starting (right after installing a ZIP), Companion now
  stops within Decky's time limit instead of being killed after 5 seconds.

**Startup**
- The panel and the Desktop app wait for the console to be detected instead of briefly showing every
  module.

### 🔧 Changed

**TDP**
- With **Allow up to 50 W**, the Legion Go 2 keeps sustained power at its firmware limit (35 W) even when a
  higher value is requested; only the boost limits go to 50 W.
- The panel shows the sustained power that actually runs, and Custom offers sustained power up to 35 W
  with boosts up to 50 W.
- In the Desktop app, choosing **This game** creates the game's profile at once, as in the panel.
- In the Desktop app, the power summary names the game and its preset from the limits that run now and warns
  "above Lenovo's limit" only while 50 W is not allowed.
- In the Desktop app, **Retry helper download** appears only while the helper is missing, and **CPU Boost**
  cannot be switched while its state is unknown.
- The Desktop app shows the "50 W paused", "TDP control unavailable" and "Could not load profile" (with
  **Retry profile**) notices.
- The Desktop app's CPU energy preference uses the panel's names (System default, Prefer CPU, Balanced ·
  Prefer CPU, Balanced · Prefer GPU, Prefer GPU) and stays shown at 50% when the system sets it.
- The Desktop app's readouts are **Limits now** (SPL · SPPT · FPPT) and **Set by**, also on the Overview.

**Fan**
- The 100°C point of a curve now runs at least 2000 RPM (before: 1500 RPM) and stays editable up to full
  speed; at 100°C and above the fan still runs at full speed.
- A saved curve whose 100°C point was lower is raised to 2000 RPM, with the rest of the curve unchanged.
- Dragging a curve point below the minimum running speed stops the fan only when dragged below half of that
  minimum; above it, the point snaps to the minimum. Stepping with the D-pad or keys is unchanged.
- "Assign curves to TDP presets" waits for unsaved curve changes and for a pending curve review.
- The Desktop app uses the panel's names and formats ("Maximum", "50.0%", "Save global curve", "Assign
  curve to …", "Starting curve", "Speed unit", "Speed edit step", "Full screen curve editor").
- The Desktop app can save an unchanged curve to confirm a review or to give a preset its own copy.
- The Desktop app offers "Use global curve" only for a preset that has its own curve, and always lets you
  turn Fan Control off while connected.

**Wi-Fi**
- **Automatic** always means the original Wi-Fi behaviour; if the band setting Companion applied was
  changed outside Companion, choosing Automatic puts the recorded original back (and says so) instead of refusing.
- A saved policy that is not recognized and changed nothing is simply cleared, and a profile that cannot
  be read still refuses.
- Automatic can be chosen whenever there is a saved setting to clear, also on another Wi-Fi card, during
  a recovery or while the link state is unknown.
- In the Desktop app, band choices and the reconnect buttons need a live connection and a supported Wi-Fi
  card, as in the panel.
- The Desktop app shows the panel's notes (settings locked, unsupported card, link state) and reports a
  change it could not verify.

**Display**
- In the Desktop app, all display controls pause while display settings cannot be read, and during an
  unfinished reset only "Retry display reset" can be used (without a second question).
- In the Desktop app, "Brightness slider in HDR" appears only when the screen supports it and no
  restart is pending.
- In the Desktop app, the first mode choice waits for the restart that finishes a reset, and "Reset
  display fix" appears once a mode is chosen.

**Battery**
- In the Desktop app, battery protection shows the saved choice while Companion manages charging and
  waits for a known battery state; controller levels outside 0–100% show "—" (a detached controller is marked).

**Lighting**
- In the Desktop app, effect, colour, brightness and speed wait for the stick lights, and the lights
  show "Restoring saved state…".
- In the Desktop app, "Restore original lighting" stays available while the lights recover.

**Vibration**
- In the Desktop app, Touchpad strength waits for Touchpad vibration, and vibration names match the
  panel (which keeps "Med", "Race" and "Std" on its narrow sliders).

**Button mapping**
- In the Desktop app, the button choices wait for button mapping and are hidden with Restore
  defaults when the controller does not support it.

**Gyro & touchpad**
- In the Desktop app, the gyro source waits for the controller test to end and reads "Not
  confirmed yet…" until Companion has confirmed it; test rates show one decimal.

**Controller firmware**
- In the Desktop app, the install asks "Install controller firmware?".

**Modules**
- In the Desktop app, Manage Modules shows each module's description, error or note as the panel does.

**Settings**
- Settings from the old standalone plugins (LeGoTDP, LeGo Vibe Control, LeGo2 Brightness Fix) and from
  versions before 2.1.0 are no longer imported.
- Companion still pauses while those old plugins are installed.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TDP**
- A first CPU Boost or EPP change that was interrupted part-way (Companion stopped, or the system could not
  confirm the old value afterwards) is now still put back when TDP is turned off or Companion is removed.
- A sustained power (SPL) above 35 W saved by 2.2.0 or earlier, globally or in a game profile, now reads
  as the 35 W that actually runs, in the panel and the Desktop app.
- TDP and battery share one firmware lock, so their firmware calls never overlap.

**Wi-Fi**
- With the iwd backend, when NetworkManager refuses to reconnect a network (seen with a WPA3 profile on a
  mixed WPA2/WPA3 network), Companion asks iwd to rejoin it.
- A 5/6 GHz switch, "Reconnect to 5/6 GHz" or a rollback no longer leaves Wi-Fi disconnected with the
  band policy stuck in recovery.
- Changing the band policy while `/etc/iwd/main.conf` has duplicate `[Rank]` sections or keys is refused
  up front, instead of leaving the band policy stuck in recovery.
- Wi-Fi never writes a line break or other saved text into `/etc/iwd/main.conf` from saved settings.

**Display**
- When another program keeps switching the panel's HDR mode back a moment after Companion sets it,
  Companion now stands off for a minute as intended instead of switching back and forth indefinitely.

**Controller firmware**
- Install refuses a controller that is detached from the console or below 30% battery, and
  checks it again with a fresh reading right before it is written.
- If Install stops there, the message says which controllers were already updated; Check
  refuses to start while another firmware updater is running.

**Modules**
- A module that failed to start can now be turned off from the Decky panel too; its switch reads On
  with the error and **Retry … start**.
- A module that is turned off no longer shows its old startup error.

**Desktop app**
- The Overview TDP badge reads "Off · Lenovo defaults" while TDP control is off and otherwise names
  the preset with its sustained power, as in the panel.
- The TDP page shows "Loading power limits…" instead of placeholder 15/20/25 W values until the
  first reading.
- A change that gets no answer in time now says to check the current value before trying again,
  since it may already have been applied.
- The connection to Companion refuses NaN and Infinity values, which the panels never send.

**Updates**
- About in the Desktop app shows the result of the update check ("Up to date", "No public release yet",
  …) instead of "Not checked".

**Vibration**
- The Desktop app shows "Controller driver not found" when the panel does.
- If the controller does not accept a change, the setting goes back to the value the controller really
  has, instead of showing the new one.
- A change made while no controller is connected now says "Controller not connected. The change is
  saved and applies when it connects." in the panel and the Desktop app, and both show the saved value.

**Startup**
- Modules now start one at a time, which avoids firmware errors when several of them touch the
  hardware right after boot.
- A module whose start takes longer than 15 s no longer holds back the others.
- Until it has finished, the panel and the Desktop app show it as **Starting** ("Still starting. Its
  controls appear when it has finished.") instead of hiding it or reporting an error.
- A module that is still starting can be turned off ("Turns off when it has finished starting."); the
  choice is saved at once and applied right after the start, never in the middle of a hardware change.
- Stopping or removing Companion during such a start no longer lets that start apply changes
  afterwards.

**Fan**
- The BIOS/EC versions Companion has already tested are saved in a way that survives a power cut, so the
  fan self-test is not repeated after one.

**Logs**
- Removing old plugin logs never follows a link out of the log folder, and Companion logs a warning when a
  Decky update stops its unload workaround from applying.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.1.0
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
**New**
- Send whole folders: drag a folder onto the Files tab or use "Choose folder". The folder structure is kept; if a folder with that name already exists, a new one ("Name (1)") is made.
- A folder that does not fit on the Deck is refused before anything is sent.
- Upload speed and time left, and the progress in the browser tab title (for example "42% · Elemental DeckKeys"), so you can follow it from another tab.
- The Deck and the PC stay awake while files are transferred.
- Faster with many small files (4 files at a time); a dropped file is retried automatically.
- "Resume" continues a stopped folder in the same folder on the Deck, skipping the files that already arrived (a file that was cut off starts again).

**Fixed**
- Ending the session or switching DeckKeys off now stops a file that is being sent or downloaded.

**Update** – run the install command again in Konsole on the Deck (pairing is kept, open pages reload by themselves):
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.0.1
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
**Fixed**
- Letters could repeat by themselves (for example "Enjoy" arriving as "Enjoyyy") when typing in Live or Touchpad over a laggy Wi-Fi. Holding a key, such as Backspace, still repeats as before.

**Update** – run the install command again in Konsole on the Deck (pairing is kept, open pages reload by themselves):
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.0.0
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
Control your Steam Deck from the browser on your PC or phone, over the local network. Works in Game Mode and Desktop Mode.

**What's in 1.0.0**
- **Text** – send typed or pasted text, optionally with Enter; saved snippets.
- **Live** – your keyboard types on the Deck as you press keys; Ctrl+V types the PC clipboard; macros (Alt+F4, Alt+Tab, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+A, F11, Super).
- **Media** – play/pause, previous, next, stop, volume, mute.
- **Touchpad** – the PC mouse (and optionally keyboard) controls the Deck until Esc; a touchpad on phones.
- **Files** – send files to `Downloads/DeckKeysTransfers/Received`, download from `Downloads/DeckKeysTransfers/Send to PC`.
- Pairing with a 6-digit code and a QR code, HTTPS with the Deck's own certificate, sessions, on/off switch.
- Optional Decky panel for Game Mode.

**Install** – in Konsole on the Deck:
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`. Then open `https://steamdeck.local:8443` on your PC.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.6
nukeador/deckyup.body:

- Stop showing ordinary folders as unknown plugins while keeping plugins with damaged manifests visible.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.5
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Read release notes before downloading an update or choosing another version.
- Expand or collapse longer notes with a compact arrow that works with a controller.
- Review downgrade warnings alongside the selected version’s notes.
- Fix security warnings opening halfway down the page and improve panel sizing.
- Translate the new interface into all ten supported languages.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.4
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Add a compact, expandable capability overview based on the validated plugin ZIP and installed files, with detected folders, commands, devices, domains and GitHub projects. Analysis is informational and does not restrict access.
- Require review for executable downloads moving to another GitHub project, newly insecure HTTP code downloads, and newly identified administrator-command execution without a root declaration. Preserve existing root acknowledgment and Decky’s native confirmation; unchanged routine updates do not repeat warnings.
- Simplify security details and installation review, remove duplicate summaries, and localize the new interface in all ten supported languages.
- Improve domain detection for HTTP sessions, Request objects, Decky fetch calls and larger JavaScript bundles. Exclude shell help text, syntax and pseudo-devices such as /dev/null from misleading capability lists.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.3
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Recognize release ZIPs with packaging suffixes such as `ResonaDeck-1.2.0-Stable.zip` while preserving validated plugin identity and version checks.
- Exclude clearly marked prerelease ZIPs from automatic stable updates.
- Show localized compatibility errors in Find Plugins across the ten supported languages.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.2
nukeador/deckyup.body: - Publish the same corrected code as v0.2.1 with v0.2.2 version metadata for the real self-update test, including recovery after repeated same-version frontend loads. No additional plugin behavior changes.

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.10
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release fixes Steam's in-game Media and Decky settings pages closing while AlarMe is installed, and makes the in-game overlay easier to place and read.

### Highlights

- **In-game pages fixed**
  - With AlarMe installed, opening Media or Decky settings from the Steam button no longer closes them, and the volume keys no longer make them flash. AlarMe only asks Steam to draw its overlay while the overlay or screensaver needs to be shown.
  - The modal layering override now applies only while the screensaver is showing.
- **Overlay placement**
  - Settings → Overlay → Position has an Anchor dropdown: top left, top center, top right, bottom left, bottom center, or bottom right. Offsets are measured from the chosen edge, and the center anchors take an offset from the middle.
  - Existing overlays keep their top-left position.
- **Overlay text color**
  - Settings → Overlay → Appearance has a Text color picker with a reset. The default grey is unchanged.
- **Overlay no longer fades**
  - The in-game overlay moves a few pixels for burn-in protection without fading out. The screensaver keeps its fade.

### Notes

- If Steam's Media or Decky settings pages still close in a game, restart Steam once after updating.

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.9
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release fixes controller input dying while Prevent Sleep or the screensaver is active on current Steam clients, and adds Pomodoro auto-start, per-item screensaver profiles, humidity on every weather view, and one consistent set of option badges.

### Highlights

- **Controller freeze fixed**
  - Steam's October client update changed how catch-all gamepad listeners are registered. AlarMe now follows the new API, so starting a Prevent Sleep timer, letting the screensaver come on, or using Standalone mode no longer leaves the controller unresponsive until Steam restarts.
  - The sleep inhibitor device is cleaned up on plugin unload and on setup failure.
- **Screensaver on/off and profiles**
  - The per-item Screensaver toggles (timers, alarms, reminders, stopwatch, Pomodoro) and Standalone mode are now the on/off switches; the global "Off" background mode is gone. Existing "Off" setups migrate to Dim with item toggles turned off, so nothing new appears.
  - A Profile picker under each Screensaver toggle applies a saved screensaver profile when that item's screensaver arms.
- **Weather**
  - Current humidity on the weather card and the compact overlay readout; mean humidity row on the 7-day forecast.
  - Weather cache refreshes immediately after a °C / °F change.
- **Widgets**
  - The calendar grid spreads over the full height of its card instead of leaving empty space above and below.
  - Calendar and forecast widgets render whenever they are picked in the widget list.
  - "Show weather in compact overlay" toggle is back for the compact layout.
- **Pomodoro auto-start**
  - Settings → Pomodoro → Start automatically begins a focus session when the Deck boots, or on boot and every wake from sleep, if none is running. Restarting Steam or reloading plugins does not count as a boot.
- **Settings layout**
  - Dropdowns, toggles and helper notes share one layout across every settings tab, with consistent indentation for sub-options.
- **Option badges**
  - One icon set, order, and color for Prevent Sleep, Screensaver, Auto Suspend, Subtle Mode, and gaming-only reminders across timer, preset, alarm, and reminder cards, the in-game overlay, and the screensaver alert list.
  - Badge rows stay on a single line, so cards keep their height. A legend lives in Settings → About.

### Notes

- If the controller is already unresponsive on your Deck, restart Steam once after updating.

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.5
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release ships optional screensaver weather, OLED-safe drift for static daily wallpapers, and a rework of in-game overlay composition so Quick Access stays usable over a running game.

### Highlights

- **Screensaver weather**
  - Optional Open-Meteo current conditions with backend disk cache and configurable refresh.
  - City search with live suggestions; approximate IP-based coordinates when no city is saved.
  - Weather card on large/fullscreen layouts and a short inline readout on the compact screensaver bar.

- **OLED protection for static wallpapers**
  - Slow drift on Bing Daily and NASA APOD images; optional drift for local-folder wallpapers in settings.

- **Overlay composition**
  - HUD and screensaver still surface when needed while QAM, settings, and modals remain interactive over game content.

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.3
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release focuses on screensaver quality improvements: smoother wallpaper behavior, more usable layout behavior, and stronger standalone input reliability.

### Highlights

- **Wallpaper transitions and refresh policy improved**
  - Crossfade behavior was refined to reduce flicker and abrupt swaps.
  - Added daily wallpaper refresh policy for the selected provider (with network-aware checks).

- **Smart wallpaper readability mode**
  - Added a new accent option: **Contrast with Background** (Wallpaper mode only).
  - Accent color is auto-picked after wallpaper changes to keep widgets readable.

- **Screensaver layout and widget organization polish**
  - Widget placement in non-compact layouts is now grouped and easier to read.
  - Removed standalone Floating mode; drift behavior is now tied to OLED burn-in protection in supported layouts.

- **Standalone wake behavior hardened**
  - Improved controller input capture/rebind flow after Steam Deck restart.
  - Added startup state cleanup for screensaver runtime state.

- **System stats responsiveness**
  - System stats widget now updates every second while visible.

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.2
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release improves Screensaver 2.0 usability and wallpaper handling, with a focus on faster activation and clearer controls.

### Highlights

- **Wallpaper prefetch and cache flow revamped**
  - Wallpapers are prefetched into runtime cache before activation, reducing loading delays when screensaver opens.
  - Provider cache paths and local folder paths are now visible in settings.

- **Wallpaper settings UX overhaul**
  - Wallpaper controls moved directly under the Screensaver background mode section.
  - Added pool size control, manual refetch action, fetch progress indicator, and last cache refresh visibility.

- **Smarter wallpaper rotation behavior**
  - Rotation now runs in random shuffled cycles.
  - Pool-size changes are debounced to avoid repeated downloads while dragging the slider.

- **Screensaver preview and header polish**
  - Preview action behavior and visibility flow were refined (including menu-close flow and clearer labeling).
  - Header layout was adjusted to avoid overflow in quick-access contexts.

outpox/bluetooth.name: v3.1.1
outpox/bluetooth.body:
Fixes 3.1.0 from the store, which showed "Bluetooth is unavailable" for everyone.

outpox/bluetooth.name: v3.1.0
outpox/bluetooth.body:
Fixes from the 3.0.0 testing round. Thanks to @zomars, @jwhitlow45 and @paulverbeke for the reports.

### Interface

- the device row now refreshes once the connect or disconnect really finishes, instead of straight away
- a spinner and a `Connecting` / `Disconnecting` label while the call runs
- a failed connect says so on the row instead of silently reverting to `Not connected`
- the primary button reads `Connect` / `Disconnect` instead of `Select`
- rows no longer offer a connect while the Bluetooth radio is off
- the battery level appears right after a connect, with no manual refresh
- battery level for DualShock and DualSense controllers, read from the kernel when BlueZ reports none
- a message when no device is paired, and a different one when the backend cannot be reached
- labels reuse Steam's own localized strings where they exist

### Backend

- D-Bus error replies are detected and logged instead of being read as data. This is what made the battery read as `o`, and it could leave the Bluetooth toggle stuck on
- adapter and device object paths are discovered through `GetManagedObjects()`, so the plugin no longer assumes `hci0`
- one D-Bus connection for the plugin's lifetime instead of one per call, dropped cleanly on unload

---

Installation:

- remove `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/Bluetooth` if it exists
  - Uninstall the plugin via decky interface
  - OR
  - `sudo rm -rf /home/deck/homebrew/plugins/Bluetooth`
- download `Bluetooth-v3.1.0.zip` to `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins` and extract it
  - `cd /home/deck/homebrew/plugins`
  - `unzip Bluetooth-v3.1.0.zip`

- timeout and retries on every backend call
