bschelst/deskflow-decky.name: v0.3.0
bschelst/deskflow-decky.body:
### What's new

- The plugin can now install, configure, and set up autostart for the stock desktop
  Deskflow app in one click, and sync your server address and screen name between it
  and the plugin in either direction. Handy if you use both Gaming Mode and Desktop
  Mode and dont want to type the server address in twice.
- Gaming Mode and Desktop Mode now actually hand off to each other properly: leaving
  Gaming Mode releases the connection instead of holding the screen name hostage, and
  coming back reconnects automatically instead of needing a manual restart every time.

### Fixes

- Found out mid-session that Gaming Mode detection has been silently broken this
  whole time: it checked an env var that plain doesnt exist on this kind of systemd
  service, so it always though it was in Desktop Mode. Replaced with checking for
  Gamescope's own process, which actually works.
- The "input enabled" toggle in the quick access panel used to just flip a flag that
  nothing read. It now actually starts and stops the helper, since there is no way to
  really pause input without dropping the connection anyway.
- tests/ had snuck into .gitignore by accident, which is a bit of a problem for a
  folder full of tests that are supposed to be committed.

### Other

- Every source file now has an author header.

bschelst/deskflow-decky.name: v0.2.0
bschelst/deskflow-decky.body:
### What's new

- Keyboard layot is now independent of the server. Pick your own keyboard language layout in the plugin
  and should remain like this regardless of what OS or layout the server side is running — needed
  a fifth patch that replays physical key positions instead of trusting the server's
  keysyms. Needs a reboot after changing.
- Settings shows a reboot button when a layout change needs Gaming Mode to restart before
  it takes effect, guarded behind a confirm dialog so it doesnt fire by accident.
- Autostart now retries while gamescope's input socket is not up yet, instead of staying
  in error on the first boot every time.

### Fixes

- Reboot now goes through Steam's own restart call instead of systemctl. The plugin
  backend has no permission to reboot directly ("interactive authentication required"),
  but Steam's own power-menu path needs nothing extra.
- Cleared out a pile of ruff lint debt so CI actually passes again.

### Other

- Rewrote the README with a logo and an overview.

necrosiak/skullkey.body:
### Fixes

- Download sizes and speeds now follow your Steam language (MB/GB in English, Mo/Go in French), on the Downloads page, game pages and the installed games list ([#14](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/14)).
- EA: the Game Explorer check now reads installer logs written in UTF-16, so Syndicate's harmless code 3 is recognised. A DirectX failure in the same run is still refused ([#10](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/10)).
- EA: older installers that read a staged product key (Battlefield 2142) now log what SkullKey finds in their `autorun.dat`, and the game id is also found in UTF-16 text and in paths written with `/`. Battlefield 2142 still needs to be confirmed ([#10](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/10)). The EA client updates automatically.

### Thanks

Thanks to [@bastiHST90](https://github.com/bastiHST90) ([#14](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/14)) and [@zavaro](https://github.com/zavaro) ([#10](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/10)) for their reports and logs.

necrosiak/skullkey.body:

### Known issue

- Battlefield 2142 and Syndicate still have separate installer problems under investigation ([#10](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/10)).

### Thanks

**Full changelog:** [v1.21.8...v1.21.9](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/compare/v1.21.8...v1.21.9)

necrosiak/skullkey.name: v1.21.8 — EA: older installers
necrosiak/skullkey.body:
### Fixes

- **EA: installs that only failed to register with Windows' game list now finish.** Some older EA installers (Syndicate, Battlefield 1942…) end with code 3 when Windows Game Explorer refuses to list the game, even though the game is fully installed. SkullKey now accepts that case, and only that case; any other installer error still stops the install.
- **EA: product keys for older installers.** Installers from the EA Download Manager era (such as Battlefield 2142) read the product key that the EA app stores in the registry. SkullKey now places your account's key there before the installer starts, as the EA app does. The key never appears in logs. Battlefield 2142 still needs to be confirmed (#10).
- SkullKey's background process now stops on its own if Decky Loader goes away without stopping it, instead of staying in memory.

### Thanks

Thanks to [@zavaro](https://github.com/zavaro) for the detailed logs and registry details in [#10](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/issues/10).

**Full changelog:** [v1.21.7...v1.21.8](https://github.com/Necrosiak/SkullKey/compare/v1.21.7...v1.21.8)

steamdeckchecker/github-decky-plugins-up.name: Version 1.9.2
steamdeckchecker/github-decky-plugins-up.body:
Version 1.9.2

Deutsch
Ist eine repos.txt in einem Downloads-Ordner vorhanden, erscheint unter „Überwachte Repositories“ ein Knopf zum manuellen Import in die interne Repository-Liste.
Der Import ergänzt nur neue gültige Links, ignoriert Kommentare und Leerzeilen, überspringt doppelte Einträge und verändert die Datei nicht. Hinzugefügte, vorhandene und ungültige Einträge werden gezählt.
Der Datei-Import kann später erneut gestartet werden; automatische Update-Prüfungen arbeiten weiterhin ausschließlich mit der gespeicherten Liste.

English
When a repos.txt exists in a Downloads folder, a manual import button appears under “Followed repositories”.
Import adds only new valid links, ignores comments and blank lines, skips duplicates, and leaves the file unchanged. Added, existing, and invalid entries are counted.
The import can be run again later; automatic update checks still use only the saved list.

Changelog – Version 1.9.1

Deutsch
- Der Updater prüft sein eigenes GitHub-Repository kurz nach dem Start und bei regulären Update-Prüfungen. Du musst es nicht zur Repository-Liste hinzufügen.
- Eine neuere Updater-Version wird auch im Modus „Vor Installation fragen“ automatisch installiert. Freigaben für andere Plugins bleiben davon unberührt; der Steam-UI-Neustart wartet, bis sie entschieden sind.
- Release-Tags wie 191 werden anhand der Version im ZIP-Namen ausgewertet. So kann auch ein unterbrochenes Selbstupdate korrekt erkannt werden.
- Startprüfungen innerhalb von fünf Minuten werden vermieden. Die Prüfung der Plugin-Identität, der Versionsvergleich und das Backup der bisherigen Installation bleiben erhalten.


English
- The updater checks its own GitHub repository shortly after startup and during regular update checks. You no longer need to add it to the followed repositories.
- A newer updater version installs automatically even in “Ask before installing” mode. Approvals for other plugins remain unchanged; the Steam UI restart waits until those decisions are complete.
- Numeric release tags such as 191 are handled using the version in the ZIP filename. This also allows an interrupted self-update to be recognized correctly.
- Startup checks within five minutes are throttled. Plugin identity checks, version comparison, and backup of the previous installation remain in place.

ciphay/decky-file-manager.name: Decky File Manager 2.2.1
ciphay/decky-file-manager.body:
## New

### Storage drives
- Drives are now shown as **capsules** with an icon, name, free space and a usage bar. Volumes that are read-only (ISO sticks, for example) show "Read-only" instead of a red "0 B free".
- **Mounted and unmounted** devices are listed, following the same visibility rules as Dolphin: EFI/boot partitions, partitions without a filesystem, swap, whole disks that have partitions and other devices hidden by udisks are not shown.
- Selecting an unmounted drive **mounts it** (an administrator password modal appears only if needed).
- **Y** on a drive opens a menu with **Rename**, **Unmount** and **Cancel** (not available for the system drives, root and home).
- Unmounting now always works: if the device is busy, it falls back to a lazy unmount.
- **LUKS support:** encrypted volumes appear as "Encrypted"; selecting one asks for the passphrase, unlocks and mounts it. Unmounting locks it again.

### Steam integration
- Steam's **"Browse..."** buttons (for example the executable and "Start in" fields in a game's properties) open the plugin's file manager instead of the Linux one.
- Other "open folder in the file manager" actions in Big Picture (install folder, screenshots, local directories) also open the plugin.
- Outside Big Picture, or if anything fails, the system dialog is used as before.

## Fixes
- Archive extraction protects against path traversal.
- Errors from the backend are now returned as results instead of raising exceptions.

ciphay/decky-file-manager.name: Decky File Manager 2.0
ciphay/decky-file-manager.body:
# Decky File Manager 2.0 - Beta

This release brings a major redesign and expansion of Decky File Manager, turning it into a more complete file management environment for Gaming Mode.

## What's New

### Dual-Panel File Manager

* Added a dual-panel file manager interface.
* Browse and manage files between two directories simultaneously.
* Improved navigation and file organization.
* Added support for selecting which panel is active.

### Background File Operations

* File operations can now continue in the background.
* Added operation progress tracking.
* Improved handling of long-running file transfers.

### Copy, Cut, Paste and Extract

* Added persistent copy and cut state.
* Added paste conflict detection.
* Improved file transfer handling between different drives and filesystems.
* Fixed .rar files not extracting.

### Storage and Drive Management

* Added drive selection and storage sessions.
* Added support for navigating between available storage locations.
* Added drive information and available space display.
* Added support for detecting unmounted drives.
* Improved storage navigation inside Gaming Mode.

### Text Editor

* Added a built-in text editor.
* Open and edit text files directly from Gaming Mode.
* Save changes without leaving the plugin.

### Steam Shortcuts

* Added the ability to add files as Steam shortcuts.
* Allows selected files to be accessed directly through the Steam interface.
* The shortcut can be added by plugin panel or in the file manager on context menu.

### File Management

* Improved file and folder operations.

# Decky File Manager

Decky File Manager is a native file manager plugin for SteamOS Gaming Mode, designed to provide a seamless and controller-friendly experience directly within the Steam interface.

Manage your files and folders without leaving Gaming Mode. Browse directories, copy, move, rename, and delete files using an intuitive interface inspired by SteamOS, making file management feel like a natural part of the console experience.

### Features

* Native Gaming Mode integration.
* Full controller navigation support.
* File and folder management.
* Copy, move, rename, and delete operations.
* Multi-language support.
* Designed for SteamOS and Bazzite.
* Lightweight and easy to use.
* SteamOS-inspired user interface.

Decky File Manager was created to fill the gap of native file management in Gaming Mode, bringing the convenience of desktop file managers to a console-like environment without sacrificing usability or immersion.

> **Beta Notice:** Decky File Manager is currently in beta. The plugin is fully functional, but new features, performance improvements, and interface refinements are actively being developed.

- **Определение eGPU** — автоматическое обнаружение через USB4/Thunderbolt (sysfs, DRM, PCI, EDID)

- **Статус док-станции** — чтение информации о USB4 доке (read-only)

- Lenovo Legion Go S (SteamOS) + AMD eGPU через ASMedia USB4 bridge

Major Changes:

rayekkk/fsr4injector.body:
Ubisoft games from Non Steam Launchers are listed under their own names, which 1.2.0 did not do.

### 🐛 Fixed
- **Games:** A shortcut that starts Ubisoft Connect with a game's id (`uplay://launch/…`, as Non Steam
  Launchers creates them) now gets that game, found through the Windows registry of its Proton prefix. If
  FSR 4 is on for the **Ubisoft Connect** entry, turn it off, press **Rescan library** and turn it on for
  the game.

A notification during the game when FSR 4 runs, as a lighter check than AMD's watermark.

### ✨ Added
- **Status:** **Tell me when FSR4 runs** (under **All games**, off by default) shows a short notification
  during the game as soon as AMD's library runs FSR 4, with its model. Problems are still told when the
  game ends.

### 🐛 Fixed
- **Games:** A game with its own non-Steam shortcut is no longer listed under its launcher's shortcut (for
  example Ubisoft Connect, whose games sit in its folder), so FSR 4 works when you start the game's
  shortcut. A launcher shortcut that already has FSR 4 on keeps its game until you turn it off.

Non-Steam games, a Repair button and an About page. Updating from 1.0.0 keeps your games set up: **Check
for updates** downloads the new ZIP, which you install the same way as before.

### ✨ Added
**Games**
- Windows games added to Steam with "Add a Non-Steam Game" and run with Proton are found too, from the
  folder of the shortcut's `.exe`. They have their own list, **Non-Steam games**, under **Steam games**.

**Repair**
- Re-checks AMD's library and puts the plugin's files and launch option back in every game that has
  FSR 4 on, for example after a game update or Steam's file check.
- If AMD's library itself is damaged or missing, it tells you to download it again first.

**Decky Launch Options**
- With [Decky Launch Options](https://github.com/Rayekkk/DeckyLaunchOptions) installed, **Add to Decky
  Launch Options** offers the FSR4 launch option and AMD's watermark to it, to switch per game there.

**About**
- **Use Rayek's store** makes Rayek's store Decky's store channel after you confirm, so Decky's Store
  tab lists Rayek's plugins and offers their updates.

### 🔧 Changed

**Panel**
- The About and Updates sections moved to an About page, opened from the last row of the panel; Updates
  is at the bottom of that page.
- When the plugin cannot start, the panel says "FSR4 Injector unavailable" with a Try again button, and
  you can still check for updates below it.
- When turning FSR 4 on or off, a setting or a rescan fails, the reason now also stays under that control
  until it next succeeds, not only in a message.
- An untested GPU gets its own "Beta" row; download sizes are in MB; an empty game list says what to do.

**Updates**
- A downloaded update shows its folder as `~/Downloads/…`, and the update texts match the other plugins
  (for example "Checking GitHub…").

**Launch options**
- Games that already set `WINEDLLOVERRIDES` (your own overrides, or another tool such as ReShade
  or OptiScaler) no longer refuse FSR 4; the plugin adds `amdxc64=n,b` to that variable.
- Turning FSR 4 off takes out only the plugin's own entry from `WINEDLLOVERRIDES`.

**Games**
- Games on the same drive share one copy of AMD's library instead of 82 MB each.

**Status**
- "DLL was not loaded" is shown only when it happens in two sessions in a row, so closing a game in its
  launcher no longer raises a warning.

### 🐛 Fixed

**AMD download**
- An unexpected error no longer leaves the panel stuck on "Downloading from AMD"; you can try
  again at once.
- It fetches exactly the part of AMD's package it needs (about 43 MB, which the progress now
  counts) and checks it before decoding.
- A slow connection gets up to 30 minutes, and Cancel stops the download at once.

**Launch options**
- After turning a game on, the plugin checks what Steam actually kept. If Steam did not keep the
  new launch options you are told, and turning FSR 4 off still restores your own options exactly.

**Settings**
- A switch that cannot be saved (for example on a full disk) stays as it was and says why, instead of
  looking changed until the next restart.
- Two switches changed in quick succession are both kept; before, the second could undo the first.

**Watermark**
- A game whose launch options could not be updated for the watermark is named in a message instead
  of being skipped silently.

**Game list**
- A damaged list of games set up is restored from its backup copy. If that is impossible, the panel
  says so and no game can be changed, instead of forgetting which files are the plugin's.

**Updates**
- "Check for updates" says when no release has been published yet instead of "Up to date", and a
  second download at the same time is refused.
- Updates are saved to your Downloads folder as the desktop names it in your language (for example
  `~/Pobrane`), instead of always `~/Downloads`.

**Files**
- Files written to game folders and the plugin's settings are flushed to disk, so a power loss cannot
  leave half a file.

**Errors**
- Error messages no longer show file paths.

**Status**
- The plugin's status file is written as UTF-8 whatever the system language, so a Proton folder with
  non-English letters no longer confuses the check after a Proton update.

### ✨ Added

**Plugin**
- First release.

**Install**
- Install from the release ZIP: in Decky Settings turn on **Developer mode**, then choose
  **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP** and select `FSR4Injector-1.0.0.zip`.

**AMD download**
- **Accept and download** fetches AMD's FSR 4 library from AMD's official driver package (about
  43 MB).

**Games**
- Turn FSR 4 on per game under **Games with FSR 3.1+**; in the game, choose **AMD FSR** as the upscaler.

**Status**
- After you quit the game, the panel shows "FSR4 active", or a notification says what went wrong.

60plus/decky-fileexplorer.name: FileExplorer 0.8.2
60plus/decky-fileexplorer.body:
## Changes

- Copy, move, pack and extract can now run together, with up to five background tasks. Operations that use the same files wait for each other.
- Rename, New folder, Move to Trash and Empty Trash stay available during unrelated transfers. Slow SMB file changes no longer hold up the queue.
- Fix opening RAR archives over SMB during copying. A loading message shows when the archive is being read, and transfer completion no longer interrupts it.
- Fix Empty Trash failing when checking inaccessible system partitions.
- Add **Open in FileExplorer** to an installed game's Steam library menu, including non-Steam shortcuts.
- Increase the file/folder options window height on PC and handheld so **Close FileExplorer** is visible without scrolling.

## Update

Use **FileExplorer → Update → Check for updates**, or install the plugin ZIP from this release through Decky's developer settings. Updates contain the complete plugin, so intermediate versions are not required.

Tested on a SteamOS PC and handheld, with 204 Python tests passing on each device. See the [testing guide](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md) for validation details.

60plus/decky-fileexplorer.name: FileExplorer 0.8.1
60plus/decky-fileexplorer.body:
FileExplorer 0.8.1 fixes navigation and transfer recovery, and keeps the built-in GitHub updater.

### Fixes

- The controller can reach Decky's top back arrow from FileExplorer, Settings, Update, Support and About. Back from a child page still returns one level.
- FileExplorer closes cleanly when Decky reloads or unloads it. Background transfers continue independently.
- Connection resets, broken pipes and timeouts now show a readable message. Other file errors retain their specific details.
- Failed moves clean up empty temporary folders while preserving partial data and source files for recovery.

### Update or install

Existing users can open **FileExplorer > Update** to download and install this release. You can update directly from an older version; intermediate releases are not required.

For manual installation, download **FileExplorer-0.8.1.zip** below and use Decky's developer ZIP installer. See the [installation guide](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/wiki/Installation).

The accompanying `.sha256` file lets you verify the download. This is the normal edition with our GitHub updater.

### Validation

The fixes passed 179 Python tests, 8 JavaScript tests, TypeScript checks and a production build. Navigation, updating checks and clean shutdown were tested on a SteamOS Stable PC. The final versioned package additionally passed all 16 updater tests and a verified 0.8.0 to 0.8.1 update simulation. See the [validation report](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/blob/main/docs/MAIN-FIXES-2026-10-16.md) for exact package and hardware test scope.

60plus/decky-fileexplorer.name: FileExplorer 0.8.0
60plus/decky-fileexplorer.body:
FileExplorer now includes an optional **Support** page with a red heart in the Decky sidebar.

- **Buy me a beer**, **Bitcoin** and **Cardano** each have a readable QR card, an icon and a copy button. Buy Me a Coffee also opens directly in Steam's browser.
- QR codes are bundled with the plugin. Viewing them does not contact an external QR service.
- Back returns from a QR card to Support, then to the plugin menu.
- The README includes download, star and MIT license badges, plus a support button. The manual includes a Support guide.

**The built-in GitHub updater remains available**, including the optional startup check. All FileExplorer features stay free. Existing preferences and saved SMB connections are preserved.

Update through **Decky > FileExplorer > Update**, or download the attached plugin ZIP from this release and install it through Decky's Developer settings. No intermediate version is required. GitHub's source-code archives are not installable plugin packages.

The release ZIP is identical to the package installed and checked on the SteamOS PC. Support was checked in Steam's native UI on PC and in local layouts at PC and handheld sizes. The new Support page has not yet been tested on handheld hardware. Backend files and the updater are unchanged from 0.7.9.

[Support guide](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/wiki/Support) | [Installation](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/wiki/Installation) | [Verification notes](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md)

60plus/decky-fileexplorer.name: FileExplorer 0.7.9
60plus/decky-fileexplorer.body:
Set up FileExplorer for a handheld or SteamOS PC, move and pack files, and manage several transfers without leaving Gaming Mode. This release also improves navigation, recovery and stored SMB credentials.

- **First setup:** choose Handheld or Steam PC, review the suggested appearance and edit any setting before saving. Controller help explains each option. A centered three-second splash appears once; repeating it is off by default.
- **Controller navigation:** Back returns one menu level, lists and menus wrap, and selecting a file advances to the next one. R3 switches between files and the toolbar; L3 hides the toolbar. Transfer controls are reachable with directional input.
- **Moving and packing:** Move to other panel verifies cross-filesystem transfers before removing the source. Create ZIP, 7z, TAR, TAR.GZ, TAR.BZ2 or TAR.XZ archives with a chosen name, compression level and destination.
- **Steam integration:** add supported launchers as non-Steam shortcuts and open a game's folder from its Steam menu.
- **Transfer queue:** run up to five copies in parallel or queue them. Browse, edit text and play media while transfers continue. Cancellation offers keeping partial copies for later or removing unfinished data.
- **Consistent conflict recovery:** Resume, Start again, Change name, Overwrite, Cancel and Open FileExplorer. Replacement asks whether to keep a backup; destructive overwrite is highlighted in red.
- **Editor recovery:** acknowledged drafts survive an interrupted editing session without changing the original file. Restore, keep or discard them when reopening.
- **Encrypted SMB passwords:** existing connections migrate automatically to user-scoped systemd credentials. TPM protection is used when available, with system-key storage on systems without TPM and no extra wallet password prompt.
- **File lists:** modification dates for files and folders, date sorting, and scrollbars that match the panel theme.
- **Documentation:** updated manual, source map and 104 new screenshots from a SteamOS PC and handheld. The two controller-legend comparison collages are retained.

Copy recovery supports retained partial copies. Stopped cross-filesystem moves, extraction and packing must restart. Recovery was tested with controlled process interruptions, not a physical battery cut. TPM-bound passwords cannot be recovered with the system-key fallback after losing or resetting the TPM; see the [network-share guide](https://github.com/60plus/Decky-FileExplorer/wiki/Network-Shares).

Update directly from an earlier release using **Decky > FileExplorer > Update**, or install the attached **FileExplorer-0.7.9.zip** through Decky's Developer settings. No intermediate version is required. Source-code archives are not installable plugin packages.

Release checks: TypeScript, production build, eight frontend tests, and the extracted package's Linux Python suite (169 passed, one skipped because system FFmpeg was unavailable). The published 0.6.1, 0.6.3 and 0.7.1 updaters accept this package in metadata-fixture tests. The ZIP is identical to the package already checked on both devices; native UI and systemd/SMB integration evidence is described in the verification notes.

60plus/decky-fileexplorer.name: FileExplorer 0.7.1
60plus/decky-fileexplorer.body:
Play audio and video in Gaming Mode, resume interrupted copies and choose where controller hints appear. This update also improves panel focus and adds an illustrated handheld guide.

- **Audio and video player:** play/pause, seek, stop, previous/next and fullscreen video. Audio uses an embedded cover or a speaker icon. Local files and SMB shares are supported; system FFmpeg provides compatibility playback when needed.
- **Copy recovery:** confirm cancellation, resume verified partial copies or start again in a new folder. A background interruption offers Resume, Start again, Cancel and Open FileExplorer. Recovery buttons fit in two rows with navigation in all four directions.
- **Controller legends:** choose the panel, Steam bar, both or neither. Labels and glyphs match across both surfaces. Shorter player and editor hints fit in one row on the tested PC and handheld viewports.
- **File recognition:** distinct icons for file categories, 238 recognized text extensions and common extensionless filenames. A opens supported previews; Options → Edit file handles unfamiliar text extensions and rejects binary data.
- **Navigation and archives:** L1/R1 keeps focus in the chosen panel. Plain GZ, BZ2 and XZ streams can be browsed and extracted.
- **Documentation:** complete format lists, a handheld guide, PC/handheld feature comparisons, four-mode legend collages and refreshed screenshots.

Media support depends on the codecs inside the file. Compatibility video playback is limited to 720p/30 fps. PDF and Office documents are not rendered; HTML, Markdown, SVG and similar formats open as source text. Interrupted extraction must be started again; copy recovery does not apply to extraction.

Update directly from an earlier release using **Decky → FileExplorer → Update**, or install the attached **FileExplorer-0.7.1.zip** through Decky's Developer settings. No intermediate version is required. Source-code archives are not installable plugin packages.

Validation: 85 Python tests on SteamOS, five frontend tests, TypeScript checking and a production build. Native Steam UI checks cover the PC and ROG Ally handheld; isolated SMB2 tests cover playback and copy recovery. The final package differs from the installed, tested 0.7.0 candidate only in version metadata and its built frontend version string.

artistro08/decky-youtube-music.name: v0.0.2
artistro08/decky-youtube-music.body:
## Reliability & Quality Improvements

- **Fix memory leaks:** Clear WebSocket/auth listeners and reconnect timers on disconnect to prevent accumulation across mount/unmount cycles
- **Fix silent API failures:** `post()` now returns `false` on network error; `del()`/`patch()` handle 401 auth errors
- **Cancellable requests:** Added `AbortController` support to song info fetch — requests are properly cancelled on unmount
- **Fix stale queue:** Queue reloads automatically on WebSocket reconnect instead of only on initial mount
- **Stable list keys:** Queue items now use `videoId` as React key instead of array index
- **Minor cleanups:** Remove unused `styleRef`, add `displayName` to memoized `TabsContainer`

### Install
Download `youtube-music.zip` and install via Decky Loader's "Install from ZIP" option.

ptflp/4deus-mod.body:
This release fixes Steam Deck keyboard and Nested Desktop input issues.

- Keep **Fn** visible when only one Steam keyboard layout is enabled, including when Steam hides the layout switch.
- Recognize renamed **Steam Os** shortcuts by their launcher path. Add / Repair preserves custom names such as **SteamOS Desktop** and reuses the existing shortcut.
- Recover the Nested Desktop AppID from its inherited environment when the Steam launcher exits.
- Prevent a stalled keyboard visibility request from permanently blocking input bridge pause/resume updates; retry failed state updates.
- Repair RustDesk input when its service remains running but its IPC socket files have disappeared. Explicit repair now restarts the service to recreate the input endpoints.

Validation: 74 frontend tests and 280 backend tests passed, along with TypeScript, ESLint, and the plugin build. RustDesk mouse and keyboard input were restored and confirmed on a Steam Deck. Long-session keyboard stability still needs broader usage testing.

hodapp/pixel-faceplate.name: Pixel Faceplate 0.3.1
hodapp/pixel-faceplate.body:
If you've got GabeCubeAura 1.5.0, Pixel Faceplate still works fine next to it, as long as GabeCubeAura's faceplate is switched off.

GabeCubeAura 1.5.0 (Alyenax's light bar plugin) came out today and it has its own JSAUX faceplate support built in now. 0.3.0 stepped aside as soon as it saw a GabeCubeAura that ships faceplate code, whether or not that faceplate was actually turned on... so with 1.5.0 installed and its faceplate off, nothing was driving the panel at all.

0.3.1 fixes that. 1.5.0 writes a claim while its faceplate is on, and Pixel Faceplate now only steps aside while that claim is live. Turn GabeCubeAura's faceplate off and within half a minute Pixel Faceplate takes the panel back, artwork, clock, random pictures and all, while GabeCubeAura keeps the light bar. Turn it back on and Pixel Faceplate lets go again. An older GabeCubeAura build with faceplate code but no way to say it's on still makes Pixel Faceplate step aside like before. So if you're on 1.5.0 and want Pixel Faceplate on the panel, switch GabeCubeAura's faceplate off in its settings. Up to you really, GabeCubeAura's faceplate wants a fair bit of setup per game and per screensaver, and Pixel Faceplate just does the artwork with no setup.

On 0.3.0 you'll get it through the built-in updater (Settings > Updates, hit Check now, then Update, and Decky asks you to confirm). On 0.2.x you need to install the ZIP by hand once (Decky > Settings > Developer > Install Plugin from ZIP File). Tested on my Steam Machine on SteamOS 3.9.5 with Decky Loader 3.3.0 and GabeCubeAura 1.5.0 with its faceplate off.

hodapp/pixel-faceplate.name: Pixel Faceplate 0.3.0
hodapp/pixel-faceplate.body:
If Pixel Faceplate is stuck on Loading... for you, this is the fix.

Decky Loader 3.3.0 came out on Oct 18, the same day as 0.2.2, and it moved its bundled Python from 3.11 to 3.14. The new build leaves out Python's termios module, which my serial code imported, so the plugin's background side crashed on load and the panel just sat there waiting forever. SteamOS has its own termios but it's built for Python 3.13, so it can't fill in. 0.3.0 does the four serial port calls it actually needs through fcntl instead. Tested on my Steam Machine on Decky 3.3.0, and it still works on 3.2.10.

If you're on 0.2.x, install this one by hand the same way as before (Decky > Settings > Developer > Install Plugin from ZIP File). After that it updates itself. It checks GitHub for a newer release when you open it, at most every 6 hours, or when you hit Check now. Tap Update and it downloads the release, checks it against the sha256 GitHub publishes, and hands it to Decky's own installer, which asks you to confirm. It never updates on its own. The flow is modelled on GabeCubeAura's updater (credit's in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), except GabeCubeAura runs as root and swaps its own folder, and this one hands off to Decky instead.

Other stuff:

Settings moved to a full screen page with a Steam style menu on the left (Display, Game artwork, Sleep and mounting, Status, Updates). The Quick Access sidebar keeps mode, brightness, a status line and a Settings button.

If the background side ever doesn't start again, after about 10 seconds the panel says so instead of Loading... forever. It shows the Pixel Faceplate and Decky versions and has buttons for the releases page and for reporting an issue.

And I now load the plugin into real Decky releases automatically, on every change and once a day against Decky's newest release, so the next time Decky changes something like this I should catch it before you guys hit it.

Tested on current SteamOS with Decky Loader 3.3.0 and 3.2.10.

hodapp/pixel-faceplate.name: Pixel Faceplate 0.2.2
hodapp/pixel-faceplate.body:
- Big thanks to @kjamert for PR #2. It added art for non-Steam games you've added to Steam (whatever art SteamGridDB put in Steam's grid folder, and if you've set custom art for any game it uses that), art from Steam's CDN for Steam games that aren't in the local library cache (it's downloaded once and kept in the plugin's folder), and random cats between games.
- Between games the panel can now show random pictures, not just cats. None of the sources need an API key: space photos from NASA's image library, the whole Earth from NASA EPIC, public domain paintings from the Art Institute of Chicago, cats (TheCatAPI, with CATAAS as backup) and twinkling stars drawn right on the console. Pick one in "Pictures of", or pick "A bit of everything" and it rotates through all of them except the cats.
- You get a new picture every 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes (10 is the default), and there's a Next picture button. Every picture is one flash write, which is why they change every few minutes and not faster. Each source keeps its last 40, so with no network you'll get ones you've already seen. The stars don't need the network at all so the mix always has something to show... a single source with nothing falls back to the Steam logo.
- The twinkling stars get uploaded once, then the panel itself slowly fades one star at a time down and back up, about a 20 minute loop. It's one GIF of about 40 KB so it's still one flash write per picture like everything else, and the way it fits is it's built from 1x1 frames that change one pixel at a time.
- Links the APIs hand back are only followed if they're HTTPS and on the host they should be.
- Downloads (pictures and Steam CDN art) happen on their own thread now, so a slow download can't hold up sleep. Sleep only waits 3 s for the panel, and a slow fetch could've left the screen on all night.
- Being offline doesn't mark a game as "Steam has no art" for 24 hours anymore, only a real 403/404/410 does that.
- Oddly shaped images get capped at 2048 px before cropping.
- If you had Random cats picked before, you still get cats.

To update, install the new ZIP the same way as before (Decky > Settings > Developer > Install Plugin from ZIP File). Your settings carry over.

hodapp/pixel-faceplate.name: Pixel Faceplate 0.2.1
hodapp/pixel-faceplate.body:
- If GabeCubeAura drives the faceplate itself, this plugin now gets out of the way: it lets go of the panel, stops handling sleep, and its panel tells you to set things up in GabeCubeAura and uninstall Pixel Faceplate. Switch GabeCubeAura off in Decky and this plugin takes over again.
- Nothing is sent to a CH340 serial port until it answers like the faceplate, so other gadgets that use the same chip are left alone.
- After a reconnect, brightness is capped as if a bright picture is showing, until the plugin sends its own.
- Sleep and shutdown no longer wait behind an upload in progress.
- The brightness slider applies once you stop sliding, and error messages stay on screen.

New since 0.1.9, in case you skipped 0.2.0:

- Artwork style: art + logo with the dark band behind the logo, art + logo without it, art only, or logo only on black.
- Logo position: top, center or bottom, in any style that shows the logo.
- Style and logo position can be set for one game. While a game is running, turn on "Just for" that game.
- Upside down: flips the picture if you mount the faceplate with the cable coming out the right side. The included cable won't reach, so you'll need a longer one.
- The plugin locks the serial port while it uses it, so two programs can't send to the panel at once.

To update, install the new ZIP the same way as before (Decky > Settings > Developer > Install Plugin from ZIP File). Your settings carry over.

raygunjohn/decky-trainers.name: v0.2.0
raygunjohn/decky-trainers.body:
## What’s new

- Shared-secret authentication protects the trainer API. The plugin creates and reuses the secret automatically.
- Request bodies are limited to 1 MiB, including chunked uploads. Oversized requests return `413` before an action runs.
- Support for 32-bit (WoW64) games, including fixes for 32-bit instruction encoding.
- Shutdown verifies that the trainer process has exited and its listener has closed. Failed stops keep tracking the process for retries.
- Status makes one API request and preserves the last confirmed attachment state while the trainer is busy.
- Trainer detection protects the game’s wineserver.

Thanks to [@coddingtonbot](https://github.com/coddingtonbot) for 32-bit support, wineserver safety and securing exposed endpoints ([#1](https://github.com/raygunjohn/decky-trainers/pull/1), [#2](https://github.com/raygunjohn/decky-trainers/pull/2), [#3](https://github.com/raygunjohn/decky-trainers/pull/3)).

## Install

1. On the Deck, press **…** (Quick Access) and open the **Decky** tab — the plug icon.
2. Tap the **⚙ gear** in the top right, then **Settings → General**, and turn on
   **Developer mode**.
3. A **Developer** tab appears in that same settings page. Open it and paste this
   into **Install Plugin from URL**:

```text
https://github.com/raygunjohn/decky-trainers/releases/download/v0.2.0/DeckyTrainers.zip
```

4. Tap **Install**. **DeckyTrainers** now shows up in the Decky menu.

## Use

Launch a game, open **…** → Decky → **DeckyTrainers**, pick a `.ct` table, and tap
**Build trainer**. When it finishes, tap ▶ to start it and **Attach** — the feature
list appears and you can flip cheats with the gamepad.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/raygunjohn/decky-trainers/compare/v0.1.2...v0.2.0

dpacc/deckcast.body:
# 📺 DeckCast v1.0.0

The first official release of DeckCast — cast your Steam Deck screen to any browser at 60fps, share recordings, upload to YouTube, and stream to Twitch. All from Gaming Mode.

## 📺 Tutorial

**[▶️ Watch the Installation Tutorial](https://youtu.be/WLSNrbv94IU)**

---

## ✨ Highlights

### 📺 Live Cast
Cast your Steam Deck screen to **any browser** on your local network at **60fps**. One tap to start.

- Hardware-accelerated capture via gpu-screen-recorder + PipeWire
- Configurable resolution (720p / 800p / 1080p) and quality (4–12 Mbps)
- ~5–8 second latency over local network
- Optional simultaneous recording while casting
- Browser player with volume control, fullscreen, and Picture-in-Picture

### 📲 Wi-Fi Transfer
Transfer recordings of any size — scan a QR code, download on any device. No internet needed.

### 🎬 YouTube Upload
Upload to YouTube from Gaming Mode. Title, tags, privacy — all configurable. Background uploads.

### ✂️ Clip Trimmer
Instant trim with zero quality loss (FFmpeg codec copy). No re-encoding.

### 📡 Live Streaming
Stream to YouTube, Twitch, or any RTMP endpoint.

---

## 🚀 Installation (Step by Step)

### Prerequisites
You need [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz) installed on your Steam Deck. If you don't have it:
1. Go to https://decky.xyz on your Steam Deck browser
2. Follow their install instructions (takes 2 minutes)

### Option A: Install from Desktop Mode (easiest)

1. Download **DeckCast.zip** from this page (click the file at the bottom ⬇️)
2. Switch to **Desktop Mode** on your Steam Deck
3. Open the file manager (Dolphin) → navigate to **Downloads**
4. Right-click `DeckCast.zip` → **Extract** → **Extract Archive Here**
5. You should now have a `DeckCast` folder. Move it to the plugins directory:
   - Open a **second file manager window**
   - Navigate to `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/`
   - Drag the `DeckCast` folder into `plugins/`
6. Open a terminal (**Konsole** from the app menu) and run these 3 commands one by one:
   ```
   sudo systemctl stop plugin_loader
   ```
   ```
   sleep 3
   ```
   ```
   sudo systemctl start plugin_loader
   ```
   Enter your password when prompted.
7. Switch back to **Gaming Mode** → open Quick Access Menu (`...` button) → Decky tab (🔌) → **DeckCast** is ready!

### Option B: Install via terminal (Desktop Mode)

1. Download **DeckCast.zip** from this page
2. Switch to **Desktop Mode**
3. Open **Konsole** (terminal) and run:
   ```bash
   # Go to Downloads (or wherever you saved the zip)
   cd ~/Downloads

   # Unzip to plugins folder
   sudo unzip -o DeckCast.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/

   # Restart the plugin loader (NEVER use 'restart' — always stop/start)
   sudo systemctl stop plugin_loader
   sleep 3
   sudo systemctl start plugin_loader
   ```
4. Switch back to **Gaming Mode** — DeckCast appears in Decky!

### Option C: Install from another computer via SSH

Make sure SSH is enabled on your Deck (**Settings → Developer → Enable SSH**).

```bash
# 1. Download the zip to your computer
curl -L https://github.com/dPacc/DeckCast/releases/download/v1.0.0/DeckCast.zip \
  -o /tmp/DeckCast.zip

# 2. Upload the zip to your Deck
scp /tmp/DeckCast.zip deck@DECK_IP:/tmp/DeckCast.zip

# 3. SSH into your Deck
ssh deck@DECK_IP

# 4. Unzip to plugins folder
sudo unzip -o /tmp/DeckCast.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/

# 5. Restart plugin loader (stop → wait → start)
sudo systemctl stop plugin_loader
sleep 3
sudo systemctl start plugin_loader
```

Replace `DECK_IP` with your Deck's IP address (find it in **Settings → Network → your Wi-Fi → IP Address**).

> ⚠️ **Never use `systemctl restart plugin_loader`** — it causes a port conflict crash loop that requires a hard reboot. Always use **stop → sleep 3 → start**.

---

## 🎮 How to Use

1. Open the **Quick Access Menu** ( `...` button) in Gaming Mode
2. Go to the **Decky** tab (🔌 plug icon)
3. Tap **DeckCast**
4. Tap **Start Casting**
5. The cast URL appears on screen (e.g. `http://192.168.1.231:8420/cast`)
6. Open that URL on **any device's browser** on the same Wi-Fi — your Deck screen streams live at 60fps!

To stop: tap **Stop Casting** on the Deck, or click **Stop** in the browser.

---

## 📋 Requirements

- Steam Deck running SteamOS 3.x
- [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz) installed
- gpu-screen-recorder (pre-installed on most SteamOS setups)
- FFmpeg (pre-installed on SteamOS)

For YouTube upload features only:
```bash
pip install google-auth google-auth-oauthlib google-api-python-client qrcode Pillow
```

otisabiburada/finally-3d-game-cases-plug.body:
## Finally 3D Game Cases 1.11.1

Install the new zip the same way as before. It replaces the old version and keeps all your looks, wears, names and settings.

### New
- **Eject animation when you quit a game.** The case flies out and opens, the disc (or game card) comes back out of the slot, drops into its tray, and the case closes and flies back to its place. It has its own switch and a **Preview the eject** button, and works without the insert animation too.
- **Shrink-wrap tear on first launch.** A sealed game (never played, or set to *Sealed*) gets its shrink-wrap ripped off when you launch it, with crinkle and rip sounds, then the case opens as usual. A game you set to *Sealed* yourself switches to normal wear afterwards.
- **Less motion.** Choose *Full motion*, *Less on battery* or *Less motion* under Effects. It turns off the drifting, the foil shine and the leaning neighbours; the covers stay 3D. *Less on battery* switches back when you plug in.
- **Template frames.** Use printed console frames instead of plain colours, for example the SteamGridDB [Templates](https://www.steamgriddb.com/collection/20087) collection by MANE0395. Put the pictures in `~/homebrew/settings/3d-game-cases/templates/` and press **Reload templates** (Looks, colours and presets → Colours → Templates). Each frame becomes a look for a game, a collection or the default, with the game's art inside the frame's window. No frames are included in the plugin.

### Faster
- **Near-zero cost at rest.** Covers you're not on are now flat 2D with the same look, so no extra GPU layers. Only the game you're on becomes 3D, and the turn in and out look the same as before.
- **Nothing animates forever.** The gentle drift plays two slow cycles and stops.
- **Sleeps while you play.** While a game is running the plugin stops watching Steam's pages, stops its timers and pauses its animations, then catches up when you quit.

### Fixed
- **Huge, blocky ghost with a white ring around the focused game on Home.** Steam draws a blurred glow copy of each cover next to the real one, and its newer scrambled class names meant the plugin turned that copy into a case too. The copy is now recognised by where it sits and left alone.
- **Insert animation sometimes played twice.** When Steam Cloud sync (or a cloud conflict dialog) delayed the game's start, the launch was counted twice. The animation now plays once per launch.
- **Black case and disc in the insert animation with 3D cases off.** The animation now finds the game's cover on screen by itself, or loads Steam's art or your custom art.
- **Strong perspective from Steam magnified the tilted case.** The plugin now uses its own perspective. Wide items also tilt a bit less.
- **Gloss, band and sleeve now show on every cover.** They were missing on covers that tilt on their own.

### Install
Download `Finally-3D-Game-Cases-v1.11.1.zip` below and install it from Decky (*Install Plugin from URL* with this zip's link, or *Install Plugin from ZIP File*).

## 1.10.2
Update from 1.9.0: install the new zip the same way as before. It replaces the old version and keeps all your looks, wears, names and settings.

### Fixed: huge, blocky ghost with a white ring around the focused game on Home
- Steam's Home draws every cover twice: the real cover inside the tile you move onto (a role=link Focusable), and a blurred glow copy in a box right next to it, outside that tile. Steam's class names are scrambled now, so the plugin no longer recognised the copy and turned it into a case too. On focus that copy was tilted, un-blurred and drawn on top of the real cover.
- The copy is now recognised by where it sits (same picture, next to the cover, outside Steam's focus target), is never turned into a case, and keeps Steam's own glow. When two copies can't be told apart, both are kept, so the real cover is never dropped.
- Works whichever of the two Steam creates first, and when Steam re-creates them. On Home the panel now shows about as many "glow/reflection copies left alone" as covers.

### Template frames (new)
- Use printed console frames instead of plain colours. Put frame pictures (PNG, WebP or JPG, 2:3, for example the SteamGridDB collection "Templates" by MANE0395) in `~/homebrew/settings/3d-game-cases/templates/` and press **Reload templates** (Looks, colours and presets → Colours → Templates).
- Every picture appears as a look next to the colours and can be set as the default, per collection or per game. The game's own cover art is drawn inside the frame's window and the frame over it, on the resting cover and on the 3D case.
- The window is found automatically. If one is off, add `<same name>.json` next to the picture, for example `{"window":[0.04,0.11,0.04,0.04]}` (left, top, right, bottom, as fractions of the frame).
- Nothing is downloaded or included in the plugin; only files you put in that folder are used. Works with the fallback injection too.

### Other
- The tilt no longer picks up a strong perspective that Steam sets on a parent (it could magnify the case); the plugin sets its own. Very wide items get a slightly smaller tilt.
- Covers whose tilting item is the cover itself keep their gloss, band and sleeve.

Updating from 1.8.2: install this zip the same way you installed 1.8.2. It replaces the old version and keeps all your looks and settings. **New: insert animation with its own switch. Press Play in the library or on a game page and the case opens, and the disc (printed with the game's art) goes into the slot, with sounds. Choose to play it before or after Steam's game logo. Works with or without the 3D cases.**
First Release of Finally 3D Game Cases Plugin

spidernic96/dimensions-toypad-aio.name: v1.1.0: Full Recompiled Support, Auto-Setup & Ecosystem Overhaul
spidernic96/dimensions-toypad-aio.body:
# 🚀 Changelog & Release Notes

### 🌟 Dimensions Recompiled Fully Supported!
We have completely overhauled the plugin to natively support playing **Dimensions Recompiled** out of the box on the Steam Deck, seamlessly bridging the Linux/Windows Proton gap.
* **Proton File-Mapping Fixed:** Fixed the bug where characters wouldn't place on the Toypad in Recompiled. Temporary tag files are now routed to `~/.local/share/`, guaranteeing the sandboxed Windows engine can safely read your tags and LED frames.
* **Smart Auto-Detection:** The Decky scanner now natively detects `legodimensions.exe`. It will automatically search through your Steam Library's `compatdata` folders (across both your internal SSD and SD Cards) so you don't have to go hunting for the game yourself.
* **Auto-Fixes Game Configs:** Creating a Recompiled shortcut now automatically patches your game's `legodimensions.toml` file. It converts hardcoded `C:\` drive paths into universal `Z:\` drive paths, completely eliminating the "game_data_root does not exist" crash!
* **Streamlined Shortcut Creator:** Bypassed the "missing emulator" safety locks specifically for Recompiled, letting you instantly add the Windows native game straight to your Steam Library from the plugin.

### 📚 Massive Documentation Overhaul
* Added exhaustive, step-by-step setup guides for every single backend: **CEMU, RPCS3, shadPS4, and Dimensions Recompiled**.
* Documented the underlying architecture of the **Anomaly** mod loader, Web App tag swapping, LED Sync timings, and shadPS4 PKG extraction.
* Added clear instructions on how to use custom `.bin` vehicle/character files so they persist across game updates.

### 🧹 Quality of Life & Repository Cleanup
* Purged duplicate stray Python scripts and old build files from the root directory to keep the repository extremely lightweight.
* Officially added the BSD-3-Clause `LICENSE` file to maintain proper open-source compliance with the original upstream architecture.

spidernic96/dimensions-toypad-aio.name: v1.0.0
spidernic96/dimensions-toypad-aio.body:
# LEGO Dimensions Toypad Plugin (Complete Edition)

Transform your Steam Deck into the ultimate, untethered LEGO Dimensions machine. This Decky Loader plugin completely eliminates the need for the physical USB Toypad hardware and RFID tags, allowing you to play the entire game **100% portably, on-the-go**, exactly as you would play any normal game in your Steam Library! 

### 🌟 Plugin Features
- **True On-The-Go Gameplay**: Play the entire LEGO Dimensions roster anywhere. Launch straight from Steam's Gaming Mode, hit the hotkey, and summon characters on the fly without ever touching a physical toy.
- **Decky Loader Virtual Toypad**: A beautifully native, centered modal interface that lets you browse, place, move, and remove characters and vehicles on a virtual 3-region Toypad directly over your game.
- **Universal Emulator Support**: Fully integrated and automated setup for RPCS3 (PS3), CEMU (Wii U), shadPS4 (PS4), and the Windows-native Dimensions Recompiled port.
- **Tri-Render LED Syncing**: Watch the Toypad light up dynamically exactly as the physical hardware would! Real-time RGB packets from the game are broadcast simultaneously to the Decky UI, the in-game Overlay, and the Phone App.
- **In-Game C++ Overlay**: A lightweight, custom-built overlay binary that draws the live state of your Toypad directly over the game's framebuffer, so you never lose track of where your characters are while playing portably.
- **Phone Web-App Controller**: Hosts a localized HTTP server on your Steam Deck, allowing you (or a co-op partner) to seamlessly connect a smartphone browser to control the Toypad wirelessly.
- **Advanced Tag Management**: Swap characters across regions, "Favorite" your most used figures for quick access, and Clear the board with single button presses using standard controller navigation.
- **Custom Tag Support**: Easily expand your roster by dropping your own 180-byte character `.bin` files into the persistent custom storage directory.
- **Steam Shortcut Generator**: Built-in backend scripts that safely parse and inject emulator execution arguments directly into Steam's `shortcuts.vdf` for flawless, console-like Gaming Mode launches.
- **Mod & Graphic Pack Automation**: Automates the injection of the Anomaly Modloader for shadPS4, and seamlessly manages necessary CEMU Graphic Packs to prevent crashes.

### 📦 Manual Installation
1. Download the `dimensions-toypad-release.zip` file attached below.
2. Unzip the folder.
3. Move the extracted `dimensions-toypad` folder into your Steam Deck's plugin directory: `~/homebrew/plugins/`
4. Restart your Steam Deck (or run `sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader` in the terminal) to load the plugin.

### 📚 Documentation
Please refer to the repository's `README.md` and `docs/TECHNICAL.md` for exhaustive, step-by-step emulator setups (including CEMU Graphic Packs, RPCS3 configs, shadPS4 payload extraction, and Windows Recompiled Proton routing).

feelsrat/decky-renodx.name: Decky RenoDX v0.7.0
Decky RenoDX v0.6.0
feelsrat/decky-renodx.body:
### New: best settings set up automatically
- **Resource upgrades from the RenoDX wiki.** Notes such as "`B8G8R8A8_TYPELESS` `Output Size`" or "`Upgrade Copy Destinations` `On`" are now written into the game's RenoDX settings. About 160 wiki entries carry them.
  - Settings marked optional or conditional ("if black screen occurs …") are left alone.
  - Where a note offers a wider alternative ("`Output Ratio` for other percentages"), that one is used, because it covers both cases.
  - Nothing is written when the generic RenoDX addon already has its own defaults for the game.
- **RHI's per-game RenoDX values** (for example `Set_Path=1` for Stellar Blade) are applied too.
- **Game and UI brightness follow Steam's "SDR content brightness"** (Settings → Display → HDR), so the game's UI matches the Steam overlay. Peak brightness still comes from the screen.
- **Unreal Engine.ini.** For the 25 or so Unreal games whose wiki entry says "Engine.ini", the wiki's HDR lines are added to the game's `Engine.ini` in its Proton prefix.
  - As the wiki advises, the file is made read-only, so in-game graphics settings won't save while HDR is installed.
  - Remove HDR puts the original file back.
  - If the game has never been launched, the panel asks for a Repair after the first launch.
- **"Did HDR work? → Yes" remembers your RenoDX settings** for that game. A later reinstall, even after Remove HDR, starts from them. Brightness is still matched to the current screen.

### Fixes
- Repair applies the wiki's notes again. It used to reinstall from a stored summary that didn't include them.

feelsrat/decky-renodx.name: Decky RenoDX v0.5.1
feelsrat/decky-renodx.body:
### Fixes
- **Steam Deck OLED peak brightness was set to 604 nits instead of 1000.** The panel's EDID reports about 604 nits, but SteamOS's compositor (gamescope) ignores that and uses its own profile for the panel: 1000 nits peak, 800 full-frame. Games see gamescope's values, so the plugin now uses them for the Deck OLED, the Zotac Zone and the OneXPlayer F1. Games set up with 0.5.0 show **Repair**. It replaces the old automatic value, and anything you set yourself is kept.

feelsrat/decky-renodx.name: Decky RenoDX v0.5.0
feelsrat/decky-renodx.body:
### New
- **Brightness matched to your screen.** On install, the plugin reads the active screen's HDR peak brightness from its EDID. Docked, that's the external screen. A Steam Deck OLED that reports none counts as 1000 nits. The value goes in:
  - **RenoDX**: as the mod's peak brightness (`ToneMapPeakNits`) in `ReShade.ini`.
  - **Special K**: as its HDR luminance.

  The screen and its peak are shown under Plugin → "Match brightness to the screen", which turns this off.

### Fixes
- **Reinstalling or Repair no longer resets your RenoDX settings.** Changes made in the RenoDX tab (presets, sliders) are carried over, and they win over the automatic brightness.

feelsrat/decky-renodx.name: Decky RenoDX v0.4.6
feelsrat/decky-renodx.body:
### Fixes
- **Unity games got ReShade as `opengl32.dll`, so it never showed up.** `UnityPlayer.dll` always links OpenGL, but Unity renders with Direct3D 11/12 on Windows, loading it at runtime. The plugin saw only the OpenGL import and hooked the wrong API: ReShade loaded, but never saw a frame. There was no banner, Home did nothing, and RenoDX never ran (Against the Storm, Wobbly Life). Unity games now get `dxgi.dll`, as in 0.0.x. Affected installs show **Repair**.
- When the graphics API is only a guess from a game DLL's imports, PCGamingWiki's API list wins if it has one.

turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.name: v0.16.0
turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.body:
- **Follows the game you start.** Start a different game and Quest Compendium switches to it with "Switched to …" and a fresh conversation. Go back to an earlier game and its conversation comes back.
- **More than Steam games.** Non-Steam shortcuts and emulators are recognized too: EmuDeck, ES-DE, RetroArch and standalone emulators, including Flatpak and AppImage builds and Windows emulators run through Proton. The game is read from the file the emulator loaded, or from RetroArch's history, else the shortcut's own name (without tags like "(GC)").
- **"Which game is this?"** If a file doesn't say which game it is, Quest Compendium asks once and remembers your answer for that file.
- **Stays on your Deck.** Detection runs on the Deck. Only the game's name is used.
- **New setting: "Follow the game you start".** Turn it off to keep your current conversation. A **Switch** button appears when a different game starts.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/TuriusX/Quest-Compendium-Decky/compare/v0.15.4...v0.16.0

- **The same guide as the website.** The guide screens now show what questcompendium.com shows: every section, everything that's live (no more "coming soon" for places and quests the site already has), the same short names ("Ciri"), the kind icons, the walkthrough with its route, choices and advice, and the pictures. When the website's guide gets better, the Deck has it the next day.
- **Tidier compendium.** Its sections start folded, each with its count, so the areas stay close at hand.

turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.name: v0.15.3
turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.body:
- **Premium yearly.** The Get Premium QR page now gives both plans: $4.99 a month, or $39.99 a year (save 33%). You pick on your phone. Already subscribed? Manage your plan there to switch between monthly and yearly.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/TuriusX/Quest-Compendium-Decky/compare/v0.15.2...v0.15.3

turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.name: v0.15.2
turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.body:
- **Sign in by email.** Under the link QR code, "Or email me a sign-in link": type your address, open the email on
  your phone or PC, confirm the code shown on the Deck, and the Deck signs in by itself. No Google account needed.
- **Premium from the Deck.** Settings shows your plan. "Get Premium" shows a QR code that opens Premium on your phone,
  where you sign in with the same account; Premium then shows up on the Deck by itself. It's also on the
  out-of-questions screen, in place of "About Premium".

turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.name: v0.15.1
turiusx/quest-compendium-decky.body:
- **Your questions and the countdown.** The status line shows "Pro 1 · Fast 3 · ⏱ 5:26:41", ticking every second, like
  the desktop app.

  here?, and Best gear for where I am (How do I beat this? in a fight). After an answer, two follow-ups. The rest are
  in the pull-down.

novasound6945/deckygram.name: Deckygram v0.7.7
novasound6945/deckygram.body:
### Changed / 변경

- Clip quality is one list now: frame and bitrate together, sixteen rows,
  each stating the rate the encoder will use and what a minute weighs at
  it. The two separate choices had a gap between them: the bitrate did not
  follow the frame, so 480p came out the same size as 800p, and a
  one-minute clip came out at 43 MB whatever was picked because the size
  limit was deciding (reported 2026-09-16: "all qualities and fps and
  bitrate produced the same file size"). The reference is 800p at
  12.8 Mbit/s, a touch above the most a Deck records, so that row means
  the recording as it is; the other three are Steam's own tiers, and each
  smaller frame gets the same four scaled by pixel count - 480p has 36 %
  of the pixels and gets 36 % of the rate. "As recorded" is gone as a
  choice: a setting that held it lands on the top row for its frame, and
  an older 800p figure stored with a smaller frame lands on the scaled row.
  클립 화질이 목록 하나가 됐습니다. 화면 크기와 비트레이트를 한 줄로
  고르며, 열여섯 줄 각각이 인코더가 쓸 값과 그 값으로 1분을 보낼 때
  무게를 적습니다. 따로 고르던 두 설정 사이에 빈틈이 있었습니다.
  비트레이트가 화면 크기를 따라가지 않아 480p가 800p와 같은 크기로
  나왔고, 1분 클립은 무엇을 골라도 크기 한도가 결정해 43 MB였습니다
  (2026-09-16 리포트: "화질, fps, 비트레이트를 바꿔도 같은 크기"). 기준은
  800p·12.8 Mbit/s로 덱 녹화 최대치보다 살짝 위라 그 줄이 곧 녹화본
  그대로이고, 나머지 셋은 스팀 자체 등급이며, 작은 화면은 같은 네 줄에
  화소 비율을 곱해 받습니다. 480p는 화소가 36%라 36%를 받습니다. "원본"
  선택지는 사라졌고, 저장돼 있던 "원본"은 그 화면의 최고 줄로, 작은
  화면과 함께 저장된 예전 800p 숫자는 비례한 줄로 옮겨집니다.

- A 60 fps recording sent at 30 fps keeps the bits each frame was given
  rather than the bits per second, so it comes out about half the size.
  Before, the ceiling stayed at the recording's whole rate and the halved
  frames simply got twice the bits each, which cannot add detail the
  frames never had.
  60fps 녹화를 30fps로 보내면 초당 비트가 아니라 프레임마다 받던 비트를
  유지해 파일이 절반쯤 됩니다. 전에는 상한이 녹화 전체 비트레이트에
  머물러 절반이 된 프레임이 각각 두 배의 비트를 받았는데, 그건 프레임에
  없던 디테일을 더해 주지 못합니다.

### Fixed / 수정

- Clip captions were hours off. Steam names a clip folder in UTC, and the
  caption printed those digits as they were, so a clip taken at 19:58 read
  16:58 - or, in Korea, one taken at 00:30 read 15:30 the day before. The
  folder time is now read as UTC and shown in the Deck's own zone.
  Screenshots were never affected; their captions come from the file's
  own time.
  클립 캡션의 시각이 몇 시간씩 어긋났습니다. 스팀은 클립 폴더 이름을
  UTC로 짓는데 캡션이 그 숫자를 그대로 찍어서, 19:58에 찍은 클립이
  16:58로, 한국에서는 00:30에 찍은 클립이 전날 15:30으로 나갔습니다. 이제
  폴더 시각을 UTC로 읽어 덱의 시간대로 표시합니다. 스크린샷은 파일 자체의
  시각을 쓰므로 원래 문제가 없었습니다.

- The queued-clips size shown in the panel never exceeds what the
  recordings weigh on disk, whatever row is picked; before, only "as
  recorded" was quoted that way.
  패널의 대기 클립 용량 예상치가 어떤 줄을 골라도 녹화본의 실제 크기를
  넘지 않습니다. 전에는 "원본"을 골랐을 때만 그렇게 견적했습니다.

### Thanks / 감사

- **@EslamBradwil**, for the size table across every setting and for
  spotting the clock.
  설정별 크기 표와 시각 문제를 짚어 주신 **@EslamBradwil**님, 이번에도
  고맙습니다.

novasound6945/deckygram.name: Deckygram v0.7.6
novasound6945/deckygram.body:
### Changed / 변경

- Clips are decoded on the GPU as well as encoded there. v0.7.5 put the
  hardware encoder first but still decoded in software, and on the Deck
  that decode was most of the cost: a 15-second 60 fps clip going to
  480p spent 8.4 CPU-seconds across nearly six threads in one burst.
  With the decode on the video block, the frame-rate drop done on GPU
  frames, and a software scale in between only when a smaller frame is
  asked for, the same clip spends 3.7 CPU-seconds on about one thread;
  at the recorded size, 1.5 CPU-seconds on half a thread. The output is
  identical - SSIM against the same reference agrees to six digits -
  and the encode still runs at about five times real time. Software
  decode into the same encoder stays as the fallback, and x264 behind it.
  클립을 인코딩뿐 아니라 디코딩도 GPU에서 합니다. v0.7.5는 하드웨어
  인코더를 1순위로 뒀지만 디코딩은 여전히 소프트웨어였고, 덱에서는 그
  디코딩이 비용의 대부분이었습니다. 15초짜리 60fps 클립을 480p로 보내는
  데 CPU 8.4초를 스레드 여섯 개 가까이에 한꺼번에 몰아 썼습니다. 디코딩을
  비디오 블록으로 옮기고, 프레임 수는 GPU 프레임에서 낮추고, 작은 화면을
  골랐을 때만 그 사이에 소프트웨어 크기 조정을 두니 같은 클립이 CPU
  3.7초를 스레드 하나 정도에서 씁니다. 녹화된 크기 그대로면 CPU 1.5초,
  스레드 반 개입니다. 결과물은 동일하고(같은 기준 대비 SSIM이 소수점 여섯
  자리까지 일치) 인코딩은 여전히 실시간의 약 5배 속도입니다. 같은 인코더로
  가는 소프트웨어 디코딩이 폴백으로 남고, 그 뒤에 x264가 있습니다.

### Verified on a Deck / 덱 실기 확인

- v0.7.5's fixes were run on a Deck against real recordings this time.
  A 60 fps 800p clip sent with 30 fps and 480p chosen arrives as H.264,
  768x480, 30 fps; with 800p chosen it arrives at 800p and 30 fps; with
  60 fps chosen it is sent untouched. A 30 fps recording is left alone
  unless a smaller frame is asked for. The x264 fallback was forced once
  and produced the same file.
  이번에는 v0.7.5의 수정을 덱에서 실제 녹화로 확인했습니다. 60fps 800p
  클립을 30fps·480p로 보내면 H.264 768x480 30fps로 도착하고, 800p를
  고르면 800p 30fps로, 60fps를 고르면 손대지 않고 그대로 보냅니다. 30fps
  녹화는 더 작은 화면을 고르지 않는 한 그대로 둡니다. x264 폴백도 한 번
  강제로 태워 같은 파일이 나오는 것을 확인했습니다.

novasound6945/deckygram.name: Deckygram v0.7.5
novasound6945/deckygram.body:
### Changed / 변경

- Clips are encoded on the GPU again, still as H.264. v0.7.4 moved the
  encode to the CPU for a small gain in picture (SSIM 0.9537 against
  0.9407 for the hardware encoder) and paid for it with three times the
  encode time - and on the Deck's APU the CPU and the GPU draw on the
  same power budget, so an encode running during play takes frames from
  the game. The gap is not visible at phone size; the frame drops are.
  The hardware H.264 encoder now goes first, the frame is still scaled
  in software, and x264 stays behind it as the fallback, capped at two
  threads so that even the fallback leaves the game most of the CPU.
  HEVC and the GPU scaler stay out.
  클립을 다시 GPU에서 인코딩합니다. 코덱은 그대로 H.264입니다. v0.7.4는
  약간의 화질(SSIM 0.9537, 하드웨어 인코더는 0.9407)을 위해 인코딩을
  CPU로 옮겼고, 그 대가로 인코딩 시간이 세 배가 됐습니다. 덱의 APU는 CPU와
  GPU가 전력 예산을 나눠 쓰므로, 플레이 중에 돌아가는 인코딩은 게임의
  프레임을 가져갑니다. 그 화질 차이는 휴대폰 화면에서 보이지 않지만 프레임
  저하는 보입니다. 이제 하드웨어 H.264 인코더가 1순위이고, 크기 조정은
  여전히 소프트웨어로 하며, x264는 폴백으로 남되 스레드를 2개로 제한해
  폴백이 돌아도 게임에 CPU를 남겨 둡니다. HEVC와 GPU 스케일러는 계속
  쓰지 않습니다.

- The README said H.265 and "~7 % CPU"; both described the encoder that
  left in v0.7.4. It now describes what actually runs.
  README에 H.265와 "CPU 약 7%"라고 적혀 있었는데, 둘 다 v0.7.4에서 빠진
  인코더 이야기였습니다. 지금 실제로 돌아가는 구성대로 고쳤습니다.

### Note / 참고

- The broken 480p output reported against v0.7.3 never reproduced here,
  and v0.7.4 removed both parts that could have caused it: the HEVC
  encoder and the GPU scaler. This release brings the GPU encoder back,
  as H.264, and keeps the scaler in software. If 480p comes out broken
  again, that places the fault in the encoder block, and the fix is to
  put x264 first - please report it.
  v0.7.3에서 보고된 480p 깨짐은 이쪽에서 재현되지 않았고, v0.7.4는 원인일
  수 있는 두 부품인 HEVC 인코더와 GPU 스케일러를 모두 뺐습니다. 이번
  릴리스는 GPU 인코더를 H.264로 되살리고 스케일러는 소프트웨어로 둡니다.
  480p가 다시 깨지면 원인은 인코더 블록이라는 뜻이고, 그때는 x264를
  1순위로 두면 됩니다. 알려 주세요.

novasound6945/deckygram.name: Deckygram v0.7.4
novasound6945/deckygram.body:
### Fixed / 수정

- Picking 30 fps did nothing to a 60 fps recording. The frame rate is
  set during the encode, and a clip small enough to send skipped the
  encode - the same gap that made the resolution cap do nothing.
  30fps를 골라도 60fps 녹화가 그대로 나갔습니다. 프레임 수는 인코딩할 때
  정해지는데, 전송 가능한 크기의 클립은 인코딩을 건너뛰었습니다. 해상도
  상한이 동작하지 않던 것과 같은 자리입니다.

### Changed / 변경

- Clips go out as H.264, the codec Steam records in, and the scaling is
  done in software. Both had been chosen for speed and both were
  costing picture. Measured on a Deck at 2.5 Mbit/s from one source,
  as SSIM against that source: libx264 0.9537, h264_vaapi 0.9407,
  hevc_vaapi 0.9345, and the previous first choice - HEVC with the GPU
  scaler - 0.9310. The files are within 5 % of each other in size.
  Encoding takes longer for it; a 48-second clip went from 5 to 15
  seconds.
  클립을 스팀이 녹화하는 코덱인 H.264로 내보내고, 크기 조정도
  소프트웨어로 합니다. 둘 다 속도를 위해 고른 것이었는데 둘 다 화질을 깎고
  있었습니다. 같은 원본 2.5 Mbit/s 기준 덱 실측 SSIM은 libx264 0.9537,
  h264_vaapi 0.9407, hevc_vaapi 0.9345, 기존 1순위였던 HEVC + GPU
  스케일러 0.9310입니다. 용량 차이는 5% 이내입니다. 대신 인코딩이
  길어집니다. 48초 클립 기준 5초에서 15초가 됐습니다.

### Thanks / 감사

- **@EslamBradwil** again, for catching both of these.
  이번에도 **@EslamBradwil**님이 두 가지를 모두 짚어 주셨습니다.

novasound6945/deckygram.name: Deckygram v0.7.3
novasound6945/deckygram.body:
### Fixed / 수정

- The resolution cap did nothing. A clip small enough to send skipped
  the encode, and the scale went with it, so 480p went out at the
  recorded size. Forcing the encode then hit a second problem: with the
  bitrate on "as recorded" the encode was aimed at whatever the size
  limit allowed - 26 Mbit/s for a short clip - so the smaller frame came
  out larger than the original and was thrown away for it. The encode is
  now capped at the source rate and the scaled file is the one sent.
  해상도 상한이 동작하지 않았습니다. 전송 가능한 크기의 클립은 인코딩을
  건너뛰는데 그때 크기 조정도 같이 건너뛰어서, 480p를 골라도 녹화된 크기
  그대로 나갔습니다. 인코딩을 강제하니 두 번째 문제가 드러났습니다.
  비트레이트가 '원본 그대로'면 용량 제한이 허용하는 값(짧은 클립은
  26 Mbit/s)을 목표로 잡아서, 작아진 화면이 원본보다 커지고 그 이유로
  버려졌습니다. 이제 원본 비트레이트를 넘지 않게 잡고, 크기를 조정한
  파일을 전송합니다.

### Changed / 변경

- The gallery list is five times quicker to open. It no longer walks
  every file in the recording folders to date them - the folder's own
  timestamp does - and reads each clip's length only for the rows on
  screen. Game names are resolved once per request instead of once per
  item. Measured on a Deck with 60 items: 124 ms to 25 ms.
  갤러리 목록이 5배 빠르게 열립니다. 날짜를 알아내려고 녹화 폴더의 모든
  파일을 훑지 않고 폴더 자체의 시각을 쓰며, 클립 길이는 화면에 보이는
  항목만 읽습니다. 게임 이름은 항목마다가 아니라 요청당 한 번 조회합니다.
  60개 기준 덱에서 124 ms → 25 ms.

### Thanks / 감사

- **@EslamBradwil** reported both of these and shared a build with their
  own fix for the gallery, which this release builds on. Thank you.
  두 문제 모두 **@EslamBradwil**님이 알려주셨고, 갤러리는 직접 고친 빌드를
  공유해 주셔서 그 방식을 가져왔습니다. 감사합니다.

elias02345/sonnenschein.name: Sonnenschein v0.2.9-test
elias02345/sonnenschein.body:
# Sonnenschein v0.2.9-test

> **Test build:** Please report Steam Deck, controller, and host-lifecycle
> results before a stable release is created.

## What changed


### Fixed

- The native **Stream with Sonnenschein** game-page control now uses the full
  proven MoonDeck anchor model: a zero-height anchor in Steam's header context,
  absolute native focus-group positioning, and TopCapsule visibility tracking.
  This fixes the v0.2.8 node being injected but clipped outside the visible
  Game Mode layout.
- Added explicit Game Mode diagnostics for route target discovery and the
  final anchor insertion point.

### Added

- The Decky panel can check GitHub Releases for a newer Sonnenschein test
  build and install it automatically, updating both the plugin and AppImage.
- The updater includes a masked, changeable sudo password field initialized
  to `deck`. The password exists only in memory for that update, is passed via
  an anonymous stdin pipe, and is never saved in settings, logs, environment
  variables, or command arguments.
- Update progress survives the intentional Decky Loader restart and is shown

elias02345/sonnenschein.body:
## Sonnenschein Client 0.2.1-test — Stream-Button funktioniert jetzt wirklich

### Behoben nach echtem Deck-Test

**Der Stream startete nicht.** Ursache: Unser eigener Easy-Mode-Code sondierte bei jedem frischen Stream-Start (jeder Decky-Start ist einer) einmal die komplette Hardware-Decoder-Fähigkeit — direkt gefolgt von der echten, ebenfalls vollständigen Decoder-Initialisierung des Streams selbst. Dieser doppelte GPU-Auf-/Abbau im selben Prozess, unmittelbar hintereinander, war auf dem PC nie aufgefallen (dort läuft der Client über mehrere Starts weiter), traf aber jeden einzelnen Deck-Start. Die Easy-Mode-Sondierung nutzt jetzt eine schlanke Variante ohne Decoder-Erstellung — die volle Sondierung bleibt exklusiv dem Diagnose-Befehl vorbehalten. Zusätzlich: **jeder Fehlschlag beim Stream-Start wird jetzt sichtbar angezeigt** statt lautlos die App zu beenden — sollte trotzdem mal etwas schiefgehen, siehst du jetzt genau warum.

**Der Button war zu groß und hat die Seite kaputt gemacht.** Er sitzt jetzt in nativer Button-Größe direkt neben Spielen/Installieren statt als eigene große Zeile darunter.

**Der Platzhalter „Sonnenschein Stream".** Das gemeinsame Shortcut wird jetzt vor jedem Start auf den echten Spieltitel umbenannt — Steams Start-Übergang zeigt „Portal" statt eines generischen Platzhalters.

### Neu: Verfügbarkeits-Anzeige

Kleiner Punkt am Button: **grün** = Host erreichbar und frei, **orange** = Host beschäftigt mit einem anderen Spiel, **rot** = Host nicht erreichbar. Aktualisiert sich alle 8 Sekunden.

### Steam Deck installieren/aktualisieren (Desktop-Modus, Konsole)

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Elias02345/sonnenschein/dev/decky-plugin/deck-install.sh | bash
```

| Gerät | Datei |
