| Windows | `SonnenscheinClientSetup-0.2.1-test.exe` |
| Steam Deck Client | `Sonnenschein_Client-0.2.1-test-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Steam Deck Plugin | per Install-Script (empfohlen) |

📖 [Steam-Deck-Anleitung](https://github.com/Elias02345/sonnenschein/blob/dev/docs/steam-deck.md)

⚠️ Das Layout-Wrapping des App-Panels (für die Button-Platzierung) ist auf echter Hardware noch nicht visuell bestätigt — falls die Spieleseite trotzdem seltsam aussieht, bitte melden.

artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.name: v0.4.1
artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.body:
## What's Changed (since v0.4.0)

Three additions on top of v0.4.0's trust-network feature, all aimed at keeping the receiver healthy when network state isn't immediately useful:

### Boot-time DNS race
- At Steam Deck boot, NetworkManager reports wifi as `active` before DNS is reachable, so `receiver.start()` could fail with `fetch failed` errors against YouTube's lounge API and take down the whole plugin (`Backend process ended before signaling READY`).
- Initial reconcile is now wrapped in try/catch — failure no longer kills the plugin.
- Network poll always runs reconcile (not just on change), so a failed initial start auto-retries every 10s until DNS comes up.

### SSDP rebind across trusted networks
- SSDP/DIAL multicast sockets are interface-specific. Switching networks while advertising left the socket on the old interface, so the phone couldn't see the receiver on the new one.
- New `boundNetworkUuid` tracks the interface the receiver bound to. If it differs from `currentNetwork.uuid` while advertising, reconcile stops + restarts so SSDP rebinds.

### Log hygiene
- Reconcile only logs on actual state change (not every 10s poll).
- `safeReconcile` suppresses repeated identical error messages and prints `Reconcile recovered after prior failure` on success after a previous failure.

## Full Changelog
https://github.com/artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1

artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.name: v0.5.0
artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.body:
## What's Changed

This is the v0.3.0 stable model (single `Receiver Enabled` toggle, persisted across reboots, default off) with the v0.4.0 install-on-top fix kept in. The trust-network feature from v0.4.x has been removed — it had unresolved boot-time race conditions where the receiver tried to start before DNS was reachable.

### Kept from v0.4.x

- `main.py` stages `bin/node` and `bin/yt-dlp` to `/tmp/youtube-cast-receiver` before exec. Plugin-folder binaries are never busy, so Decky's reinstall `extractall` can't hit Linux `ETXTBSY`. **Reinstall on top works without manual uninstall.**
- Process-group `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` via `os.killpg` with bounded waits and a 200ms grace so any `yt-dlp`/`nmcli` grandchildren are reaped before unload returns.
- Shutdown fail-safe: 1.5s hard exit, `receiver.stop()` raced against 1s timer.
- Stale-session timeout bumped 5 min → 30 min so paused tracks don't drop the cast session.

### Removed

- Trust-network feature, `backend/src/network.ts`, all `/api/network/*` routes
- Network polling, `nmcli` detection, reconcile state machine

### Restored

- Single `Receiver Enabled` toggle on the player page
- `/api/receiver/{enable,disable,status}` routes
- `receiver.enabled` persisted to datastore, default off at boot

## Full Changelog
https://github.com/artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.name: v0.4.0
artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.body:
## New Features

- **Trust this network** — A single toggle on the player page lets you mark the current Wi-Fi (or ethernet) connection as trusted. The receiver only advertises while connected to a trusted network, and automatically stops when you roam to an untrusted one. Roam back and it resumes within 10 seconds.
- Replaces the previous `Receiver Enabled` toggle. Trust list is keyed by connection name (SSID), stable across reconnects.

## Bug Fixes

- **Reinstall on top now bulletproof** — `main.py` stages `bin/node` and `bin/yt-dlp` to `/tmp/youtube-cast-receiver/` at startup and executes from there. The plugin folder's binaries become static files Decky can overwrite freely; `extractall` can't hit Linux `ETXTBSY` regardless of what children are running at unload time.
- **Stale-session timeout** bumped 5 min → 30 min. Pausing music briefly no longer drops the session.
- **Tighter unload** — extra `SIGKILL` to the process group plus 200ms grace after `wait` reaps orphaned `yt-dlp` / `nmcli` grandchildren before Decky's `rmtree` runs.
- **Reconcile serialized** — user toggle and network poll can no longer race two overlapping `receiver.start()`/`stop()` calls.
- All background timers tracked and cleared on shutdown.

## Full Changelog
https://github.com/artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.name: v0.3.0
artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.body:
## Bug Fixes

- **Install-on-top no longer hangs** — Decky's reinstall flow extracts the new ZIP over the existing plugin directory. If our Node process or its orphaned `yt-dlp` children still held `bin/node` or `bin/yt-dlp` open, Linux returned `ETXTBSY` and the extract hung at `Installing plugin...` indefinitely.
  - `main.py` now spawns Node in its own session/process group (`start_new_session=True`) and tears it down via `os.killpg`, killing yt-dlp orphans alongside Node
  - All `process.wait()` calls run in a thread executor with bounded `asyncio.wait_for` timeouts (2s SIGTERM, 3s SIGKILL safety) — no more event loop blocking
  - `server.ts` has a 1.5s hard-limit fail-safe and races `receiver.stop()` against a 1s timer so SSDP teardown stalls can't keep us alive

You can now reinstall the plugin on top of itself without a manual uninstall first.

## UI / Copy Refinements

- Player idle text mentions YouTube Music explicitly
- Subtitle line only renders when the track has an artist (no fallback prompt)
- Receiver toggle relabeled **Receiver Enabled** with the description removed
- Queue empty state mentions YouTube Music

## Full Changelog
https://github.com/artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver/compare/v0.2.9...v0.3.0

artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.name: v0.2.9
artistro08/youtube-cast-receiver.body:
## UI / Copy Refinements

- **Player idle text** now mentions YouTube Music explicitly: "Cast a video from YouTube Music or YouTube to start playing"
- **Receiver toggle** relabeled "Receiver Enabled" with the clearer description "Advertise your Steam Deck on the network for casting"

- NetworkManager for connection management
- Root permissions for network configuration

18798aa12/deckyproxy.name: v0.2.6 — SteamOS 筛选与更新兼容修复
18798aa12/deckyproxy.body:
v0.2.6 包含复杂筛选与 SteamOS Python 3.13 空匹配兼容修复，并解决开启 TUN 时检查更新失败的问题。

- 固定更新、镜像及 GitHub 发行 CDN 域名使用真实 DNS，避免虚拟 IP 被安全下载器拒绝；继续拒绝内网/保留地址。此改动覆盖插件更新链路。
- Decky 冻结后端默认 CA 为空时加载固定系统证书库；保留 HTTPS 证书链、主机名和发行签名验证，无系统信任时明确失败。
- 插件状态、更新器及健康确认统一读取安装包版本；个人订阅、规则、节点选择和设置保持在独立目录。

验证：483 项本地 Python 测试通过，覆盖率 89.49%；[Linux CI](https://github.com/18798aa12/DeckyProxy/actions/runs/39476513858) 的前后端、Python 3.13、真实内核组成员 API、隔离 TUN 启停、打包与脱敏全部通过。

Steam Deck Python 3.13.5 实机已完成更新后的配置校验、代理启动、节点和策略组读取、TUN 接口及专用路由、HTTPS 连网，以及开启 TUN 时插件内检查更新（签名验证成功）。个人配置文件与升级前逐字节一致。休眠、Wi-Fi 切换、UDP 等完整验收仍待补充。

安装包自带锁定内核和离线 GEO/ASN 数据，源码与许可证随同提供。SHA256SUMS、update.json 及 Ed25519 签名随包发布，不包含个人订阅链接、凭证或运行配置。

18798aa12/deckyproxy.name: v0.2.5 — 修复 SteamOS 筛选兼容与版本一致性
18798aa12/deckyproxy.body:
> 后续兼容修复：SteamOS Python 3.13 的筛选、TUN 下更新 DNS 与 Decky 系统证书问题已在 [v0.2.6](https://github.com/18798aa12/DeckyProxy/releases/tag/v0.2.6) 修复，建议直接使用最新版。

v0.2.5 修复 SteamOS Python 3.13 对空筛选结果 `(?!)` 的解析优化导致“节点筛选表达式过于复杂”的问题，包含 v0.2.4 的复杂筛选兼容改进。无需修改订阅中的表达式。

同时将更新器、状态显示与健康确认统一到安装包版本，避免重复更新提示或错误回退。更新保留个人配置，安装前停止代理。

验证：
- 478 项本地 Python 测试通过，后端覆盖率 89.43%；生产构建、Ruff、安装包/源码脱敏审计与更新签名验签通过。
- [Linux CI](https://github.com/18798aa12/DeckyProxy/actions/runs/39474875873) 全部通过，包括新增 Python 3.13 后端检查、真实内核筛选 API 与隔离 TUN 启停。
- Steam Deck Python 3.13.5 上已完成实际保存配置的预检、Decky 安装升级、节点/策略组读取、TUN 接口及路由、普通 HTTPS 与 GitHub API 联网检查；个人订阅及设置校验保持一致。休眠、Wi-Fi 切换、UDP 等完整验收仍待补充。

18798aa12/deckyproxy.name: v0.2.4 — 修复复杂节点筛选兼容性
18798aa12/deckyproxy.body:
> 后续兼容修复：SteamOS Python 3.13 的筛选、TUN 下更新 DNS 与 Decky 系统证书问题已在 [v0.2.6](https://github.com/18798aa12/DeckyProxy/releases/tag/v0.2.6) 修复，建议直接使用最新版。

v0.2.4 修复导入或启动订阅时，合法节点筛选被误报“过于复杂”的问题。嵌套前瞻、复合重复、长多分支与更多反引号分段会在限时隔离进程中计算，然后转为精确节点名称匹配，继续保留策略组和规则。

- 不再仅因表达式结构复杂而拒绝；语法、容量、处理失败和实际执行超时分别提示。
- 单个原始筛选支持最多 16 KiB UTF-8，保留 CPU、内存、总输出大小限制，避免卡住后端。仍有 Python/Mihomo 正则扩展及 Unicode 语义兼容范围，详见 README。
- 更新包校验要求包含完整筛选运行模块。更新保留个人订阅、规则和设置；先停止代理，再从插件“检查更新”安装。
- 本地 466 项 Python 测试与 80 项前端测试通过，后端覆盖率 89.38%，类型检查、Ruff、生产构建、真实内核组成员 API 校验、安装包与源码脱敏审计及更新清单签名验签通过。

Linux CI 已通过前后端、打包脱敏、真实内核筛选 API 和隔离网络/挂载空间的 TUN 启停及清理检查：[验证记录](https://github.com/18798aa12/DeckyProxy/actions/runs/39472529418)。

安装包自带 Linux amd64-v1 Mihomo 内核和离线 GEO/ASN 数据。源码及许可证随同发布。此版本尚未在 Steam Deck 真机完成更新后的验收。

18798aa12/deckyproxy.name: v0.2.3 - TUN 修复与折叠策略组
18798aa12/deckyproxy.body:
修复开启 TUN 后误报“路由未建立”、内核自动停止且策略组消失的问题，并默认折叠策略组与节点列表。

- 兼容 iproute2 的字符串路由表编号，并使用数字输出检查专用路由表及规则冲突。
- 对路由 JSON 和优先级做边界检查；错误接口、错误表号和缺失路由仍会拒绝启动。
- 增加真实 Linux 内核的隔离网络命名空间 TUN 启停、策略组及专用路由清理检查。
- 策略组与节点默认折叠；点击或按 A 展开总列表，再展开需要的策略组选择节点和测速。轮询保留展开状态，切换配置或停止代理后重新折叠。
- 保留本地 YAML 导入、原始策略组/规则与 B 键修复。升级前停止代理；个人配置保留，无需重新导入 YAML。

验证：前后端测试、类型与静态检查、Linux 真实内核/规则/TUN 检查、安装包与源码附件脱敏及签名校验。Linux 隔离检查不等同于 Steam Deck 上的 DNS、UDP、休眠或更新全流程验收。

v1k0d3n/monoink.name: monoink v0.1.2
v1k0d3n/monoink.body:
## What's new in v0.1.2

A fix release for installing and updating.

### Fixed
- **ZIP updates no longer stall.** Updating with *Install Plugin from ZIP
  File* while monoink was running could stop part-way, leaving Decky's
  install dialog spinning. monoink now runs a private copy of its program,
  so Decky can always replace the plugin's files during an update.

### Updating from v0.1.1
Update **once using Install Plugin from URL** (the link below). A ZIP update
from v0.1.1 can still stall, because v0.1.1 itself has the old behavior;
from v0.1.2 onward, either method works.

If a link install seems to hang for a minute or two at the start, leave it
running: Decky first reports the install to its own plugin-store server and
waits for it even when that server is slow.

### Documentation
- The README's status line no longer names a specific version; see the
  Releases page for the latest.
- The install guide and privacy page cover the above.

## Install or update

1. In Gaming Mode, open Quick Access (**⋯**) → **Decky** → ⚙ **Settings**, and turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Decky → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from URL**:
   `https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/releases/latest/download/monoink.zip`
3. Or download **monoink-v0.1.2.zip** below and use **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

Updating keeps your settings. Full guide: [docs/install.md](https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/blob/v0.1.2/docs/install.md)


## What's Changed
* README: make the status line version-agnostic by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/22
* Fix ZIP updates stalling while the plugin is running by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/23
* Release v0.1.2 by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/24


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2

v1k0d3n/monoink.name: monoink v0.1.1
v1k0d3n/monoink.body:
## What's new in v0.1.1

### Dark mode
White on black for every screen. Photos and cover art keep their normal
tones. Turn it on under **Screens → Dark mode**.

### Screens
- **Clock: year progress.** "Day 280 of 365 · Week 41" with a progress bar
  under the date (toggle under *Clock & weather*). (#4)
- **Game: session time.** How long you've been playing appears on the Game
  screen and the dashboard while a game runs, updating every minute. A new
  **Session timer** layout shows it as a large clock (*Screens → Game screen
  layout*). (#2)
- **Game: controller indicator.** A gamepad icon appears next to the title
  while a controller is connected, within seconds of turning it on or off.
  Works with Steam Controllers on the wireless puck and with USB and
  Bluetooth pads. (#3)
- **Performance: RAM history.** Memory joins CPU and GPU on the 30-minute
  graph, with a legend that matches what's drawn. (#5)
- **Performance: history survives restarts.** The graph no longer starts
  empty after a plugin update, Decky restart or reboot, and gaps (such as
  sleep) show as breaks instead of joined lines. (#6)
- **Calendar: week starts on your region's day.** Automatic uses your
  system's region setting (Sunday in the US, Monday in most of Europe,
  Saturday in much of the Middle East), from the official Unicode CLDR
  data; you can also pick Monday, Sunday or Saturday. Nothing is looked up
  online. (#8)
- **Photo frame: fill the screen.** Crop photos to fill the whole display
  instead of showing them whole with bars. (#10)

### Privacy and transparency
- New **[privacy page](https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/blob/main/docs/privacy.md)**:
  everything monoink reads, stores and contacts, what it never does, and
  commands to verify it yourself.
- The service log is now readable only by your user account (it contains
  your display's Bluetooth address).
- Every network request now identifies itself as monoink.

### Smaller improvements and fixes
- On an idle machine, the CPU and GPU lines on the Performance graph no
  longer disappear into the graph's border.
- A new game's session reads "Just started" instead of "0m".
- The dashboard's game column no longer overflows into the system stats.
- New **[screen gallery](https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/blob/main/docs/screens.md)**
  showing every screen in light and dark mode.

### Upgrading
Install the new version the same way as before. Your settings are kept. A
"Week starts on Sunday" choice is kept; otherwise the calendar switches to
Automatic.

## Install or update

1. In Gaming Mode, open Quick Access (**⋯**) → **Decky** → ⚙ **Settings**, and turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Decky → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from URL**:
   `https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/releases/latest/download/monoink.zip`
3. Or download **monoink-v0.1.1.zip** below and use **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

Updating keeps your settings. Full guide: [docs/install.md](https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/blob/v0.1.1/docs/install.md)


## What's Changed
* Clock screen: show year progress (day and week of the year) by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/13
* Photo frame: add a fill-screen option by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/14
* Performance screen: add RAM to the 30-minute history graph by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/15
* Keep performance history across restarts by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/16
* Game screen: show when a game controller is connected by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/17
* Privacy: full accounting page, input-devices comparison, private log by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/18
* Game screen: session time and a session-timer layout by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/19
* Calendar: start the week on the day customary for your region by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/20
* Release v0.1.1 by @v1k0d3n in https://github.com/v1k0d3n/monoink/pull/21

codevski/decky-ftpd.name: v0.1.4
codevski/decky-ftpd.body:
### Added
- Username/password authentication, on by default with credentials `deck` / `deck` (editable in Settings).
- Anonymous (no-password) mode as an opt-in toggle, gated by a confirmation prompt.
- Login row on the main panel showing the active username (or "anonymous").

### Changed
- Root directory is now locked to `/`. Navigate to subdirectories from your FTP client. This sidesteps a "no access" bug seen when the configured root resolved through a symlink (notably `/run/media` for the SD card).
- Settings modal: removed the Root directory field; added Username, Password, and Anonymous access controls.
- Quick Paths panel removed from the main screen.
- Settings moved from a bottom button to a gear icon in the panel title bar. The Options section is gone; the QAM panel is now action-only.
- Login and Sharing rows merged into a single line (`<user> · /`) to tighten the FTP Server section.

### Migration
- Existing installations with a custom `root_dir` setting will start serving `/` after upgrade. Authentication is on by default, so existing users automatically gain credential protection.

rayekkk/spotideck.body:
### Fixed

- The local player stays off after a console restart or Decky reload, including existing installations that previously saved an enabled player. SpotiDeck no longer starts Soloist or selects the handheld's Spotify Connect receiver just because the plugin is installed and configured.
- Spotify status reads begin when the plugin panel is opened. Opening the panel does not start the local player or transfer playback from another device.

### Added

- **Start player on this handheld** on the main page starts and selects the local receiver on request. The regular Play button continues to control the currently selected Spotify device.

### Changed

- Saved credentials, Soloist pairing and player choice are preserved. After a manual start, music continues when QAM closes; after a console restart or Decky reload, start the local player again when needed.
- Updated setup instructions and player status guidance to explain manual startup.

### Internal

- Added regression tests for saved configurations, explicit startup, Decky reloads and keeping remote Play separate from local player startup.
- Verified on Legion Go 2 that the player stays off after Decky reload and panel opening, starts from the new button, and stays off after another reload. Full console reboot was not part of this live check.

### Install

Download `SpotiDeck-1.1.1.zip`, then in Decky: gear icon, Developer, **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

### Added

- Spotify Flatpak is available as an alternative local player in Settings. Play/pause, skipping, seeking, volume and game audio balance remain accessible from the same QAM interface.
- Open or stop the Spotify app directly from the plugin. Use the desktop app to manage audio quality and downloads; SpotiDeck's search, library and queue still require an internet connection.

### Changed

- Soloist remains the default and recommended player, with an explanation of its lower memory and power use beside the player selector. Explicit player choices survive restarts, and switching engines preserves the Soloist key and pairing.
- Switching from Flatpak back to Soloist closes the Spotify app to release its resources. Closing QAM alone keeps music playing.
- The Decky plugin menu now uses SpotiDeck's own handheld/music icon instead of the Spotify logo.

### Fixed

- Returning to SpotiDeck after selecting another playback device starts an enabled Soloist player when needed and waits for it to become ready. An explicitly stopped player stays stopped, and device selection does not start music automatically.
- Recover a Soloist process left behind by a Decky reload after verifying that it belongs to this plugin's private session, so it no longer blocks the new player from starting.

### Internal

- Verify the Flatpak media interface and local audio before linking its Spotify Connect device. Unconfirmed playback commands are not repeated through the Web API.
- Added regression coverage for player selection, saved preferences, process ownership, desktop playback and command failures. Validation passed 358 backend tests on Linux, 76 frontend tests, type checking and the production build.

### Install

Download `SpotiDeck-1.1.0.zip`, then in Decky: gear icon, Developer, **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

vindeckyy/slipstream.name: v0.24.0
vindeckyy/slipstream.body:
# Slipstream 0.24.0

Slipstream 0.24.0 brings the streaming host to Windows, alongside web console polish and
hardening across the Linux host paths.

## Supported downloads

- Linux x86_64 host archive
- Steam Deck client Flatpak
- Steam Deck Decky plugin zip
- Android clients continue on the rolling `v0.23.0-public` release

## Windows host (new)

A Windows PC can now be the streaming host. Build `slipstream-host` and `slipstream-tray` on
Windows (MSVC or GNU toolchain); the Linux, Android, and Steam Deck clients connect to it the
same way they connect to a Linux host. See the [Windows host guide](https://vindeckyy.github.io/slipstream/docs/windows-host).

- **Capture:** Windows Graphics Capture with DXGI fallback (`SLIPSTREAM_CAPTURE_METHOD` selects
  `auto`, `wgc`, or `dxgi`); the pointer is embedded in the frame.
- **Encode:** NVIDIA NVENC over D3D11 when the driver answers, with the honest codec list from the
  driver probe; openh264 H.264 software fallback otherwise.
- **Display:** Mirror a monitor by default, or plug a RustDesk indirect display when that driver
  is installed.
- **Audio:** WASAPI loopback capture with resample/remap to 48 kHz.
- **Input:** `SendInput` keyboard/mouse/pen injection with native Unicode text; host cursor hides
  during sessions. (A virtual gamepad is not wired up yet.)
- **Clipboard:** Text, HTML, RTF, and PNG in both directions.
- **Service & tray:** Run headless under the Service Control Manager (`sc create slipstream-host`),
  with a system-tray icon for service state, console deep links, and pairing approvals.
- **QoS:** MMCSS and qWAVE cover the low-latency profile.

AMD AMF and Intel Quick Sync are not encode backends on Windows; requesting them fails loudly
instead of silently substituting.

## Web console

- Library empty state redesigned as an intentional dashed affordance.
- Getting Started and pairing PIN presentation refined.
- Design tokens, shell density, and chart palette reworked with light/dark parity.

## Host hardening

- Cursor, frame-queue, and video paths hardened (TV-only cursor visibility, queue occupancy
  reservation, defensive cropping of unaligned frames on older drivers).
- Settings: shared guidance, dependency-aware configuration, safer saves.
- Clippy 1.96 hygiene across the workspace.

## Operations

- Release artifacts include SHA-256 checksums, third-party notices, SBOM, and build provenance
  attestations.
- The repository scans full Git history for secrets and validates first-party links, generated
  API files, packaging metadata, and pinned GitHub Actions.

See the [installation guide](https://vindeckyy.github.io/slipstream/docs/install) and
[security policy](https://github.com/vindeckyy/slipstream/security/policy) before exposing a host
outside a trusted LAN.

ch1mpleo/decky-dns-unblock.name: DNS Unblock v0.2.0
ch1mpleo/decky-dns-unblock.body:
Reliability release: Automatic provider selection with DNS + HTTPS checks, safer restore,
honest diagnostics, and clearer status.

### Features

- **Provider Automatic** (default on new installs): try Cloudflare → Google → Quad9 (then plain
  backups in Auto mode). Saved 0.1.0 providers (e.g. Cloudflare) are **not** remapped on upgrade.
- Selection verifies **Steam DNS and HTTPS** (SNI/Host) before committing a provider. DNS-only
  success can stay applied with “Steam unverified”; full failure falls back to network DNS.
- Status shows the active provider and transport (e.g. `Active · Google · Encrypted`).
- Diagnostics columns: **Network / Provider / Deck / HTTPS** against the active or configured
  resolver (not a fixed Cloudflare DoH probe). Sticky results clear when mode/provider/device changes.

### Fixes

- Restore marker cleared only after a successful restore; unload retries restore before stopping
  dnsproxy; startup restores before killing a leftover proxy the link may still need.
- Generation guards discard stale apply/diagnostics work after reconnect or settings changes.
- Two-failure hysteresis before replacing an established provider; 60 s health reuse on panel open.
- Probe dnsproxy on ports 15353–15355 for selection/diagnostics without touching live link DNS.
- Plain mode tests each server independently and applies only verified addresses.
- Auto mode still keeps a plain provider IP as link backup behind dnsproxy.

### Tests / CI

- Plugin lifecycle tests for Automatic failover, fallback, diagnostics cancel, shutdown restore.
- Release workflow runs the same TypeScript check as CI before packaging.

### Field notes

- VNPT / Viettel behaviour from 0.1.0 still applies as a baseline.
- **FPT is not claimed fixed** without affected-user Steam confirmation on that ISP.
  Compare Automatic vs Cloudflare vs Google on the same link (see `docs/field-test.md`).

ch1mpleo/decky-dns-unblock.name: DNS Unblock v0.1.0
ch1mpleo/decky-dns-unblock.body:
First release.

### Features

- Quick Access panel: on/off toggle, Mode (Auto / Encrypted only / Plain only), Provider (Cloudflare, Google,
  Quad9, Custom), live status with Wi-Fi, link DNS and the server in use, toasts for Paused / Fallback / Error.
- Encrypted DNS through a bundled, checksum-pinned AdGuard dnsproxy v0.86.0 on `127.0.0.2:53`, using IP-address
  DoH upstreams so nothing is looked up through the ISP's DNS.
- Safe fallback chain: encrypted -> plain public DNS -> the network's own DNS. Each step is verified by resolving
  `store.steampowered.com` before the Wi-Fi link is changed.
- Diagnostics: Steam domains checked against the network's DNS, Cloudflare DoH and the Deck's resolver, with a
  plain-language summary.

### Network handling

- Event-driven (`nmcli monitor`), no polling: re-applies after Wi-Fi off/on, sleep/wake and network switches,
  including Steam's delete-and-recreate of Wi-Fi profiles.
- Waits for NetworkManager's internet check after connecting (up to 10 s; ~6 s on a 4G hotspot) before applying.
- Captive portals: pauses and restores the network's DNS so the login page loads, resumes after login.
- dnsproxy is restarted after every reconnect: its pooled HTTPS connections from the previous network are dead and
  its cache would hide that (found switching from home Wi-Fi to a phone hotspot).
- dnsproxy crash -> restart and re-apply; 3 crashes -> plain DNS until the next connection or settings change.
- The resolver drifting to the backup server after a proxy hiccup is corrected when the panel is opened.

### Safety

- Runtime-only changes (`nmcli device modify` / `reapply`): saved Wi-Fi profiles are never edited, a reconnect or
  reboot always restores normal DNS.
- Crash cleanup on start (leftover DNS and dnsproxy), full restore on disable, unload and uninstall.
- IPv6-disabled profiles fall back to IPv4-only DNS settings.

### Verified

- VNPT home fiber (ISP DNS answers NXDOMAIN for Steam): Active - Encrypted, Steam resolves.
- Viettel 4G phone hotspot (same NXDOMAIN block): Active - Encrypted after the ~6 s internet check, Steam resolves.
- Wi-Fi off/on, sleep/wake, home <-> hotspot switching, mode/provider changes, killing dnsproxy.

xxjsonderuloxx/omfg-deck.body:
## What's new in v0.1.3

### Workarounds section
New **Workarounds** panel in the plugin UI with two toggles that get prepended to the generated launch option string:

**Disable vSync** (`MESA_VK_WSI_PRESENT_MODE=immediate`)
Recommended for all frame generation use. Prevents Mesa's compositor vsync from interfering with the layer's frame insertion timing. Without this, the display sync interval fights the layer's inserted presents, causing stutter.

**Disable vkbasalt** (`DISABLE_VKBASALT=1`)
Enable if you see black screens or visual artifacts. vkbasalt post-processing can conflict with frame generation layers by processing the inserted frames.

When active, the launch option shown in the Usage panel and copied by the clipboard button automatically includes the enabled workarounds at the front:
```
MESA_VK_WSI_PRESENT_MODE=immediate DISABLE_VKBASALT=1 ENABLE_OMFG_RUST=1 OMFG_HOT_CONFIG_PATH=... %command%
```

### Shared omfg.env store
Refactored the `~/.config/omfg/omfg.env` file to be a proper multi-key store. The global layer disable flag and workaround flags now coexist without clobbering each other.

### Tests
197 passing tests · 100% backend coverage

xxjsonderuloxx/omfg-deck.body:
## OMFG Deck v0.1.0

Decky Loader plugin for the [OMFG (Open Multi Frame Generation)](https://github.com/xXJSONDeruloXx/omfg) Vulkan layer on Steam Deck.

### Installation
Install via Decky Loader → Developer → Install from ZIP, or wait for store listing.

### Features
- One-click install — downloads latest OMFG layer from GitHub releases
- Live config editing — all 25 OMFG knobs exposed with sliders/dropdowns/toggles
- Hot-reload — changes to `~/.config/omfg/omfg-live.toml` apply in ~250 ms, no game restart
- Context-aware UI — Reprojection, Optical Flow, Multi/Adaptive, BFI sections appear only for relevant modes
- Per-slider reset (B button snaps to default)
- Reset to Defaults button (backs up current config to `.toml.bak`)
- Launch option clipboard button
- Plugin self-update checker

### Quick Start
1. Install the plugin
2. Press **Install OMFG** in the plugin panel
3. Add to each game's Steam **Launch Options**:
```
ENABLE_OMFG_RUST=1 OMFG_HOT_CONFIG_PATH=/home/deck/.config/omfg/omfg-live.toml %command%
```

### Layer Modes Supported

alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.body:
## Void Deck 1.0.1

A fix for 1.0.0.

- **Settings are kept again.** In 1.0.0 every restart brought back the default settings: theme, Home screen, notification style, screensaver and weather city were all forgotten. Your choices now survive Steam and Decky restarts as intended.

**Update:** if you're on 1.0.0, open the Void Deck panel and press *Update to v1.0.1*. On older versions: Decky → ⚙ → Developer → *Install Plugin from URL*, and paste the link to `VoidDeck-v1.0.1.zip` below.

alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.name: v1.0.0
alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.body:
## Void Deck 1.0

Void Deck now covers the whole Steam Deck experience, from Home to the screensaver, and it is polished enough to call 1.0.

**Notifications, restyled.** Achievements unlock as a dot that stretches into a pill with the trophy inside, then folds back into the corner. Friend notifications (in game, online) use the same pill with the friend's avatar and a status dot. A panel toggle brings back Steam's own style.

**A screensaver of widgets.** Steam's slideshow of your games is replaced with a large dot-matrix clock, the date, the battery as a row of dots and the weather for a city you pick in the panel (powered by Open-Meteo). It follows Steam's 12/24-hour setting, and there is a button to preview it.

**Updates from the panel.** When a new version is released, the Void Deck panel shows *Update available*: one press and Decky installs it. This is the last time you need to install by URL.

**Also new**

- Your settings are kept across restarts.
- The light theme now inverts the whole interface, so Steam's own white titles and icons no longer disappear on the light background.
- A new plugin icon: a V drawn in dots.
- The reset to defaults button is gone: with so few settings it wasn't needed.

Thanks to **@endoflineservice** for keeping settings across restarts.

**Install / update:** Decky → ⚙ → Developer → *Install Plugin from URL*, and paste the link to `VoidDeck-v1.0.0.zip` below. It replaces the previous version.

alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.name: v0.2.2
alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.body:
## Void Deck 0.2.2 — lighter and easier on the battery

A performance release. Nothing changes visually.

- **Cheaper Home animation.** The light sweep across the dot grid is now handled by the GPU instead of being redrawn every frame, and it rests between passes. On my Deck it went from about 21% to 7% of a CPU core.
- **Paused while you play.** The Home animation stops whenever a game is running, so it never competes with the game in the background.
- **No more background process.** Void Deck no longer ships an unused Python backend, so Decky doesn't start (or have to kill) an extra process, and restarts are faster.
- **Half the download.** The release zip dropped from 227 KB to 120 KB.

**Install / update:** Decky → ⚙ → Developer → *Install Plugin from URL*, and paste the link to `VoidDeck-v0.2.2.zip` below. It replaces the previous version.

alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.name: v0.2.1
alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.body:
## What's new in Void Deck 0.2.1

**English and Spanish.** The whole plugin interface is now available in English and Spanish, with a language selector in the Void Deck panel. English is the default.

**Steam Settings, restyled.** The Settings page (System, Internet, Display…) now follows the Void Deck look: monospaced page list with a dot marking the current page, ruled setting rows and dot-matrix sliders.

**A living Home screen.** A band of light now sweeps slowly across the dot grid behind the featured game. The dots never move, they only light up.

**More panel options:** reset to defaults, a version entry with a link to the release notes, and guidance when no games are installed.

**Fixes**

- Opening Quick Access or the main menu while a game is running no longer covers the game with a black background.
- The status bar shown in Quick Access during a game now matches the panel instead of Steam's blue.
- Long game titles on Home scale down across four sizes, and the last row of the dot-matrix font is no longer clipped.
- Turning off the Home screen while you're on it now takes you to the Library.

Thanks to **@endoflineservice** for the English localization, the Steam Settings styling and the Home title refinements.

**Install / update:** Decky → ⚙ → Developer → *Install Plugin from URL*, and paste the link to `VoidDeck-v0.2.1.zip` below. It replaces the previous version.

alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.name: v0.2.0
alejandrotenorioc/voiddeck.body:
## What's new in Void Deck 0.2.0

**Game details, restyled.** The page you land on when you open a game now speaks the Void Deck language:

- The header art fills the whole screen, with the Play bar right above the button hints. Scroll down to reveal the Activity / Your Stuff / Community / Game Info tabs.
- The green Play button is now a white pill with the (A) glyph. Install, Update, Stop and every other state keep working exactly as before — only the look changes.
- Last played, playtime and required space are shown in dot-matrix numbers.
- Pure black background (no more blurred copy of the header tinting the page) and flat dark sections.

**Dot dissolve transition.** Leaving the Home screen, the next screen appears through a grid of growing dots. It's also faster: about 0.6 s instead of Steam's ~1 s.

**Smaller fixes**

- Home tabs trimmed to Home, Library and Friends.
- The focus ring around the selected Quick Access tab is no longer clipped.

**Install / update:** Decky → ⚙ → Developer → *Install Plugin from URL*, and paste the link to `VoidDeck-v0.2.0.zip` below. It replaces the previous version.

d0minatorx/rogcontrol.name: ROG Control v1.0.2.7
d0minatorx/rogcontrol.body:
> **Manual installation required for this update.** Download `Rog-Control-V1.0.2.7.zip`, extract it, open a terminal from your desktop (not from ROG Control), enter `Rog-Control-V1.0.2.7/rogcontrol`, and run `bash install.sh`. Keep your normal user account; do not run the whole installer with sudo. The older app updater can kill its own installer when it stops the tray service, so the app's update button cannot reliably install this fix. Your profiles and settings are preserved by the installer.




### Changes
- Decky: GPU clock ceiling, live CPU/GPU temperatures and fan speeds, GPU sleep status, and active-profile feedback.

- Plugin installation supports root-owned Decky directories and refuses unsafe symbolic-link or unrelated plugin destinations.
- Manual app installation restarts a previously running app after the library is replaced.
- Shared CPU planning, fan-curve handling, service queries, and boost detection reduce duplicated code. Removed unused GTK assets and obsolete helpers.

- Refreshes CPU and GPU temperatures and fan speeds approximately once per second.
- Shows the installed plugin version and presents a clearer hardware readout.
- Removes the saved GPU ceiling display line while retaining the ceiling control.

jedwards1230/decky-wake-dispatch.name: v0.2.0
jedwards1230/decky-wake-dispatch.body:
## wake-dispatch v0.2.0

This release significantly expands wake-dispatch with network scanning, mDNS hostname resolution, an improved Steam-native UI, in-app update checks, and smarter home-network automation — plus several reliability fixes.

---

## Features

### Network Scan & Device Discovery
The plugin can now scan your local network and discover devices automatically. Found devices can be added directly from scan results, saving you from manually entering MAC addresses. mDNS names are resolved where available, so devices appear with friendly hostnames rather than bare IP addresses. You can also look up devices by IP address or hostname.

### In-App Update Check
A new update checker notifies you when a new version of wake-dispatch is available, so you no longer need to check manually.

### Improved Home-Network Automation
The home-network gate now matches against your router's MAC address for more reliable network detection. Automation also correctly resumes cooldown timers after a wake attempt, preventing repeated spurious packets.

### Redesigned Panel UI
The Quick Access panel has been refreshed with a Steam-native layout. The device editor is more compact, and the scan and update workflows are integrated directly into the panel.

---

## Bug Fixes

### Clean Unload & Backend Hardening
Plugin teardown is now handled cleanly on unload, preventing stale state or lingering processes between sessions. Several backend edge cases were also hardened against unexpected input.

---

## Improvements

- Panel layout and device editor now feel at home alongside other Steam Deck Quick Access menus.
- Network scan results feed directly into the add-device workflow, reducing friction when setting up new entries.

## Commits

- feat(panel): Steam-native layout, shorter editor, scan and update UI (#11) (a3861ec)
- feat(scripts): install a release on a device over CDP (#20) (7db9e3a)
- feat(automation): match the router's MAC in the home-network gate, resume cooldown (#21) (1ea1a76)
- feat: network scan, mDNS names and find by IP or hostname (#10) (2e8b8ad)
- feat: update check (#8) (7ba6275)
- fix: clean unload + backend hardening (#9) (aa1223f)
- chore: drop a template TODO from decky.pyi (#7) (7d5215d)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jedwards1230/decky-wake-dispatch/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0

60plus/deckycache.name: DeckyCache 0.4.8
60plus/deckycache.body:
# DeckyCache 0.4.8

Choose whether cache covers entire selected drives or specific folders. Installation and update writes no longer allocate new cache blocks, and the final **Other cached data** tile explains occupancy outside the game list.

## Compatibility

**SteamOS Stable only.** Beta, Preview and Main are not supported.

| Requirement | This release |
| --- | --- |
| Tested SteamOS PC | 3.8.28, build 20260922.1, NVIDIA x86-64 |
| Required kernel | `6.18.50-valve2-1-neptune-618-gc7289a96b14d` |
| Library filesystem | Separate ext4 data partitions |
| Tested Decky Loader | 3.2.10 |

The kernel bundle is unchanged from 0.4.7. No kernel rebuild or on-device compilation is required.

## Changes

- **Cache scope:** choose **Entire selected drives** or **Selected folders**. Add Steam libraries or browse for folders across enabled drives.
- **Write-around:** copying, installation and Steam update writes go to the original HDD without allocating new cache blocks. Cached overlaps remain coherent.
- **Other cached data:** always the last tile, using the disk-and-rocket icon. It accounts for blocks outside the current game list without counting Small fragments twice.
- **Folder controls:** added spacing between selected folders and the Add folder action.
- **Preservation:** changing scope does not remount libraries or clear existing cache. Compatible built-in plugin updates retain the mounted cache and tracking IDs.

## What the scope choice means

Folder mode controls read admission, not whether a game is running. Reading selected files for copying, unpacking or verification can still populate cache.
Some direct or asynchronous reads cannot be assigned to a directory and bypass cache in folder mode.
The engine has 32 class slots per volume, shared by game tracking and selected folder roots. A new folder is refused if no required slot remains.

Previously cached data is retained. A large Other cached data tile can include data saved by older versions.
Use **Clear cache** if you want to discard all cached copies; the games on the HDD and the prepared SSD filesystem remain intact.

## Install or update

Download the attached **DeckyCache plugin ZIP**, not the source-code archive.
Enable Developer mode in Decky settings and use **Install Plugin from ZIP File** or **Install Plugin from URL**.

For an existing installation with the current updater, close games and finish Steam downloads, then use **Check for updates** in DeckyCache.
Confirm Decky's installer; the plugin reloads automatically.
Cache preservation requires the compatible built-in updater. The old updater in 0.4.5 or earlier and manual ZIP replacement can rebuild cache once.

## Validation

A native Decky update to the development build preserved occupied cache bytes, the library mount and all 31 installed Steam game entries.
Folder selection applied online without remounting or clearing cache. Isolated ext4 checks covered write admission, selected/excluded reads, cache hits, overwrites and atomic replacement.

After a normal PC restart, a 90-second MOUSE loading/gameplay observation measured **1.05 GiB from cache and 69 MiB from HDD**.
Approximately **94% of the measured storage-read bytes came from cache**, with matching physical NVMe reads and zero cache errors.
This confirms retained cache and real NVMe reads for that sample. It is not a loading-time benchmark or a measurement of RAM reads.

A real Steam download/update was not run for this release; file-update coherence was checked with controlled writes.

60plus/deckycache.body:
# DeckyCache 0.4.7

Non-Steam games added to Steam can now appear in **Cached games**, using the names and artwork already set in Steam, including artwork from SteamGridDB.

## Compatibility

**SteamOS Stable only.** Beta, Preview and Main are not supported.

| Requirement | This release |
| --- | --- |
| Tested SteamOS PC | 3.8.28, build 20260922.1, NVIDIA x86-64 |
| Required kernel | `6.18.50-valve2-1-neptune-618-gc7289a96b14d` |
| Library filesystem | Separate ext4 data partitions |
| Tested Decky Loader | 3.2.10 |

The kernel bundle is unchanged from 0.4.6. No kernel rebuild or on-device compilation is required.

## Changes

- Detects non-Steam shortcuts whose executable is inside a selected library partition.
- Uses the shortcut's game folder for Open CAS attribution, alongside regular Steam installations.
- Reuses custom Steam artwork for both Steam games and shortcuts, with alternate image and standard-cover fallbacks.
- Preserves existing cache data, folder tracking and Steam library mounts during a compatible built-in update.

## What appears in Cached games

A shortcut appears only after its folder has attributed cached data. Entries below **16 MiB** are under **Small fragments**.
Simply launching a game does not guarantee a new entry: Linux may serve those reads from RAM.
Previously unclassified data is not counted retroactively; subsequent storage I/O can attribute it without clearing cache.

Tracking remains limited to 32 distinct installation folders per cached volume.
Shortcuts that open an external launcher without exposing the game's executable path are not attributed.
All folders on the selected partition still use the block cache, including data not assigned to a game.

## Install or update

Download the attached **DeckyCache plugin ZIP**, not the source-code archive.
Enable Developer mode in Decky settings and install through **Install Plugin from ZIP File** or **Install Plugin from URL**.

For an existing installation with the current updater, close games and finish Steam downloads, then use **Check for updates** in DeckyCache.
Confirm Decky's installer. The plugin reloads automatically.

Cache preservation requires the compatible built-in updater. Updating through the old updater in 0.4.5 or earlier, or replacing the ZIP manually, can still rebuild cache once.
Original games remain on the HDD.

## Validation

A native Decky update to the development build preserved cache occupancy, all existing tracking IDs and all 31 installed Steam game entries.
Five real non-Steam shortcuts were detected. Blood's existing custom Steam artwork loaded successfully.

A controlled 1 MiB read of a Blood game file was served entirely from NVMe and attributed to Blood, with no original-HDD read.
This was a diagnostic read, not a gameplay benchmark. Existing Steam game-update coherence behavior is unchanged.

Shortcut parsing and path-selection checks, updater/lifecycle checks and TypeScript typecheck/build passed.

60plus/deckycache.name: DeckyCache 0.4.6
60plus/deckycache.body:
# DeckyCache 0.4.6

The built-in updater now keeps cached data and Steam library mounts connected while Decky replaces the plugin.
This fixes cache rebuilding and installed games disappearing from Steam after a plugin update.

## Compatibility

**SteamOS Stable only.** Beta, Preview and Main are not supported.

| Requirement | This release |
| --- | --- |
| Tested SteamOS PC | 3.8.28, build 20260922.1, NVIDIA x86-64 |
| Required kernel | `6.18.50-valve2-1-neptune-618-gc7289a96b14d` |
| Library filesystem | Separate ext4 data partitions |
| Tested Decky Loader | 3.2.10 |

## Changes

- The storage worker and Open CAS binaries have an independent runtime outside the directory replaced by Decky.
- Compatible updates keep the same mounted cache devices, cached blocks, selected drives and master switch state.
- The worker adopts the new code between operations without stopping the storage service or unmounting libraries.
- Writes continue through Open CAS, so changes to original files remain coherent with cached data.
- Cancelling the installer keeps caching unchanged. If an incomplete installation leaves the plugin absent, the worker returns libraries to direct HDD access after a grace period.
- An update that changes the active cache engine or cannot accept the cache handoff is refused before storage is changed.

## Install or update

Download the attached **DeckyCache plugin ZIP**, not the source-code archive.
Enable Developer mode in Decky settings and install through **Install Plugin from ZIP File** or **Install Plugin from URL**.

For later compatible updates, close games and finish Steam downloads, then use **Check for updates** inside DeckyCache.
Confirm Decky's installer. The plugin reloads automatically and retains your cache switch state.

**Preservation requires the new updater on both sides.** Updating from 0.4.5 or older through its old updater can still rebuild cache once.
Manual ZIP replacement does not use the preservation handoff.
If Steam lost the installed-game list after an earlier update, re-add the existing library in Steam Storage; do not format the HDD or reinstall the games.

## Validation

A native Decky installation from one development build to the next preserved the mounted library and all 31 installed-game entries throughout the operation.
Cache occupancy remained populated, and reading GRID after the update increased cache hits from 2 to 21.
The storage worker adopted the new runtime without a PC restart.

A disposable file on the selected library was written, overwritten and atomically replaced.
Each version matched both the cached filesystem read and a direct read from the original HDD.
This is a storage-coherence check, not an end-to-end Steam game download/update test.

Focused updater/lifecycle checks and TypeScript typecheck/build passed.

60plus/deckycache.name: DeckyCache 0.4.5
60plus/deckycache.body:
# DeckyCache 0.4.5

DeckyCache adds a master switch and a GitHub updater that selects releases for the running kernel.

## Compatibility

**SteamOS Stable only.** Beta, Preview and Main are not supported.

| Requirement | This release |
| --- | --- |
| Tested SteamOS PC | 3.8.28, build 20260922.1, NVIDIA x86-64 |
| Required kernel | `6.18.50-valve2-1-neptune-618-gc7289a96b14d` |
| Library filesystem | Separate ext4 data partitions |
| Tested Decky Loader | 3.2.10 |

## Changes

- **Enable DeckyCache** turns caching on or bypasses reads to the HDD while retaining valid cached blocks and drive selections.
- Switching OFF and ON keeps cached game entries. Writes while OFF invalidate affected blocks, so Steam updates do not leave stale cached data.
- **Check for updates** finds a newer stable GitHub release with modules for exactly the running kernel.
- The updater verifies the ZIP and bundled modules, then opens Decky's installer. Decky reloads the plugin automatically.
- The panel and updater remain available if no cache module matches the kernel.
- Extra spacing separates the master switch from the update button.

Original games stay on the HDD. There is no kernel rebuild, pinning or full-game copy.

## Install or update

Download the attached **DeckyCache plugin ZIP**, not GitHub's source-code archives.
In Decky settings, enable **General > Developer mode**, then use **Developer > Install Plugin from ZIP File**
or **Install Plugin from URL**.

If the installed version already has the updater, close games and finish Steam downloads, then choose
**Check for updates > Update to 0.4.5** and confirm Decky's installer.
Reopen the plugin and enable caching when ready. Update preparation returns libraries to direct HDD access,
so cache stays off after installation or a cancelled installer and may refill when enabled again.
A normal OFF/ON toggle preserves valid blocks.

The ZIP, `SHA256SUMS` and `deckycache-update.json` are attached. The JSON file lets the plugin verify kernel compatibility.

## Validation

The development build was installed through Decky's native installer without a PC restart.
On the test PC, the OFF/ON switch preserved GRID's 136 MiB of attributed cached data and its mounted library;
the owner confirmed that the game remained listed. GitHub checks succeeded from Decky's embedded Python.
The final runtime matches that build, with only release version metadata changed.

TypeScript typecheck/build and focused updater, recovery and lifecycle checks passed.
An end-to-end Steam game download/update remains unverified; earlier storage checks covered writes and atomic replacement.

60plus/deckycache.name: DeckyCache 0.4.4
60plus/deckycache.body:
# DeckyCache 0.4.4

## Compatibility

**Tested SteamOS: 3.8.28, build 20260922.1 (NVIDIA PC).**

This ZIP includes Open CAS 26.09.0.1102.release modules for exactly:

```text
6.18.50-valve2-1-neptune-618-gc7289a96b14d
```

Supported library sources are ext4 data partitions on separate, non-system drives.
The kernel is not rebuilt or replaced. A different kernel needs a matching bundle.

SSD/NVMe block caching for SteamOS PC using Open CAS. Games stay on the original HDD,
and writethrough keeps game writes and updates on that drive.

- Simple cache-drive format/reuse controls and independent switches for library partitions.
- Persistent cache across clean restarts.
- Cached games with Steam artwork, names and partial cache sizes.
- Small fragments collapsed separately, compact information dialogs and section dividers.
- Clear all cache without formatting the NVMe or deleting games.
- Shutdown ordering for the tested NVIDIA SteamOS setup.
- Illustrated installation and setup guide.

## Install

Download **DeckyCache-0.4.4.zip** from this release.

Enable **Decky Loader settings → General → Developer mode**.
Then open **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File → Browse** and select the ZIP,
or paste the attached ZIP's direct download link into **Install Plugin from URL**.
If the link requires signing in, install the downloaded file.

Choose the attached plugin ZIP, not the automatically generated source-code archives.

A selected partition is cached as a whole. No pinning, folder filtering or per-game clear is included.
Game sizes are partial attribution. A clean shutdown is required for cache reuse;
invalid state causes a cold rebuild.

GRID and DiRT 3 ran on the test PC. Normal restart preserved cached data;
GRID produced attributed cache hits and physical NVMe reads after reboot.
Storage-level update coherence was checked on disposable images.
An end-to-end Steam download/update remains unverified.

The plugin runtime matches the tested 0.4.4-dev build; this release changes the version metadata,
packaging and documentation.

capraaudio/capralink.name: CapraLink 0.3.1
capraaudio/capralink.body:
0.3.0 was never released: 0.3.1 is the first release with these features, and it also includes fixes from an outside security and reliability review.

## What's new

- **Push-to-talk.** Pick a button for each connection and choose *Hold to talk* (with a short 200 ms tail so word endings aren't cut) or *Press to toggle*. It works while a game has focus, and a short chirp tells you when you start and stop talking. On the Steam Deck the back grips (L4, L5, R4, R5) work directly, with no Steam Input mapping needed. Windows uses a listen-only method that doesn't take the key away from your game. On a Mac, CapraLink asks for the Input Monitoring permission. If the button's keyboard or controller is unplugged, or keys can't be read for a moment, talking stops at once until the next press.
- **Music Mode/Hi-Fi.** A new Hi-Fi switch next to Music Mode streams lossless 24-bit audio (about 2.3 Mbit/s each way). Lost packets are re-sent instead of being covered up (never more than were sent, so a misbehaving computer can't use resends to flood the network). If the network can't keep up, it falls back to Music Mode by itself and tries Hi-Fi again after a clean minute. Both computers need 0.3.1 for Music Mode/Hi-Fi; with an older version it simply stays in Music Mode.
- **Volume and mute.** Send and Receive volume sliders (0–150%) and a Mute button, remembered for each connection. Changes apply instantly, without reconnecting, and fade smoothly instead of clicking.
- **Delay readout.** The window shows how much delay each direction has, e.g. "You hear them: 45 ms · They hear you: 60 ms".
- **One-click updates.** From this version on, "New version available!" comes with an **Update now** button that downloads, checks and installs the update, then restarts CapraLink. (Linux .deb/.rpm installs, and Mac releases that change the audio drivers, still link to the download page.)
- **Steam Deck Game Mode plugin.** A Decky Loader plugin puts CapraLink in the Quick Access Menu: connection status, Connect/Disconnect, Music Mode, Music Mode/Hi-Fi, Mute, volume, push-to-talk and the delay readout. Download `CapraLink-Decky-0.3.1.zip` below and install it from Decky's Developer settings (Install Plugin from ZIP File).
- **Command-line control.** `capralink --status`, `--connect`, `--disconnect`, `--music`, `--hifi`, `--mute`, `--volume`, `--ptt` and `--ptt-set` let scripts control a running CapraLink.
- **Accessibility.** The whole window works with the keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space, Esc closes menus), every control has a screen-reader label, status changes are announced, "reduce motion" is respected, and text contrast is improved.

## Fixed

- **Pairing is more reliable.** Pairing, or connecting again right after a refused connection, could occasionally fail with a dropped connection (seen mostly on Windows).
- **Mac permissions no longer reset with every update.** CapraLink is now signed with its own stable certificate, so macOS remembers the microphone and Input Monitoring permissions across updates.
- **Safer Mac installer.** The installer keeps its temporary files in the private folder macOS gives each install, instead of a shared location.
- **Disconnect always works while a connection is starting.** Disconnecting while the other computer's connection was still opening your audio devices no longer leaves the two computers connected.
- **Settings changed while connecting take effect.** Picking another microphone, speaker, channel count or bitrate while a connection is starting no longer gets lost.
- **Music Mode rides out longer Wi-Fi dropouts.** Wi-Fi stalls longer than half a second are now measured too, so the buffer grows to cover them (up to 1 second), and when it shrinks again it drains smoothly instead of skipping audio.
- **Changing a setting never undoes another one.** The window and the tray menu now send only the setting you changed.
- **Clean sound on low-rate headsets.** Playback on devices below 48 kHz (e.g. 16 kHz Bluetooth headsets) no longer has harsh artifacts.
- **Less CPU on high-sample-rate devices.** Devices running at 96 kHz and above use 2–8× less processing time.
- **Quit is always quick.** Quit no longer waits while the engine is still starting, and it still stops the engine then (unless it runs in the background).
- **A wrong address can't hold up connecting.** Something on the network that answers in place of the other computer, but never finishes connecting, is given up after 5 seconds so the right address is tried.
- **Automatic reconnects keep trying.** If the audio has to be rebuilt and the first reconnect fails, CapraLink keeps retrying (when auto-reconnect is on) instead of staying disconnected.

## Good to know

- **Mac:** because of the new signature, macOS asks for the microphone permission (and Input Monitoring, if you use push-to-talk) one more time after installing 0.3.1. If CapraLink is already listed there, remove it with **−** and allow it again.
- **Windows:** the installer isn't code-signed. If Windows' Smart App Control is on, it may block the installer.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/CapraAudio/CapraLink/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.1

vettv-studios/deck-live.body:
- Go Live can now use a protected gst-launch runner on systems with GStreamer but without PyGObject, including SteamOS configurations where the required GStreamer elements are present.
- The runner receives the pipeline over stdin and disables Linux ptrace access before exec, keeping stream keys unreadable through process arguments. Streaming still fails closed if process privacy controls are unavailable.
- Health statistics are unavailable when using the gst-launch runner; Go Live status and reconnect behavior remain available.

SteamOS hardware testing remains outstanding. See the README for runtime/plugin requirements and installation instructions.

### Install / update
In Desktop Mode, run:
```
curl -L https://github.com/VetTV-Studios/deck-live/raw/main/install.sh | sh
```
Or install the ZIP below through Decky Developer settings.

vettv-studios/deck-live.name: Deck Live 1.0.2
vettv-studios/deck-live.body:
**Security fix. Updating is recommended for everyone.**

- **Stream key protection:** on systems without PyGObject (`python3-gobject`), Deck Live used a fallback that could make your stream key visible to other programs running on the same device. Deck Live now refuses to stream in that case and tells you how to fix it: install `python3-gobject`, or update Bazzite/SteamOS, then reload Decky.
- **Private settings:** the settings file that holds your stream keys is now private to your account (mode 0600) from the moment it's created.
- **Redacted logs:** stream keys and stream URLs are removed from logs and error messages.

If you use YouTube or Twitch on a device that was missing PyGObject, consider resetting your stream key on the platform as a precaution.

### Install / update (no developer mode)
In Desktop Mode, open Konsole and run:
```
curl -L https://github.com/VetTV-Studios/deck-live/raw/main/install.sh | sh
```
**Requires your sudo password.** The installer writes to `~/homebrew/plugins`, which is owned by root.
- **SteamOS (Steam Deck):** the `deck` user has no password by default. If you've never set one, open **Konsole** in Desktop Mode and run `passwd` first, then run the installer.
- **Bazzite:** use your normal account password.

Alternatively, download `Deck-Live-1.0.2.zip` and use Decky → Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP.

Tested on Legion Go / Bazzite. SteamOS is untested.

vettv-studios/deck-live.name: Deck Live 1.0.1
vettv-studios/deck-live.body:
- New `install.sh`: one-line installer and updater (`curl -L …/install.sh | sh`) that needs no Decky developer mode. It downloads the latest release, swaps the plugin folder atomically, and restarts plugin_loader. It works with stock tools (curl, unzip or a python3 fallback, systemctl).
- New `uninstall.sh` (`PURGE=1` also removes settings and stream keys).
- Releases now also carry an unversioned `deck-live.zip` asset for a stable `latest/download` URL.
- No plugin code changes.


### Install / update (no developer mode)
In Desktop Mode, open Konsole and run:
```
curl -L https://github.com/VetTV-Studios/deck-live/raw/main/install.sh | sh
```
**Requires your sudo password.** The installer writes to `~/homebrew/plugins`, which is owned by root.
- **SteamOS (Steam Deck):** the `deck` user has no password by default. If you've never set one, open **Konsole** in Desktop Mode and run `passwd` first, then run the installer.
- **Bazzite:** use your normal account password.

Alternatively, download `Deck-Live-1.0.1.zip` and use Decky → Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP.

Tested on Legion Go / Bazzite. SteamOS is untested.

justinca92/minimi-town.name: Minimi Town 0.2.2
justinca92/minimi-town.body: - New 100h and 150h upgrades, so every tier changes the building. kuchazefira-hub/gyroparallax-decky-plugi.name: GyroParallax-v.1.0.2
kuchazefira-hub/gyroparallax-decky-plugi.body:
Баг: после выхода из спящего режима экран начинает мерцать и "бегать". Тестовые исправления внесены в версию 1.0.2.

Что известно:
Это не какой-то один конкретный баг в самом плагине, что точно такая же проблема (мерцание, «троение» картинки, диагональный «сдвиг» после пробуждения) — известный, широко задокументированный класс багов на уровне SteamOS/Chromium, никак не привязанный к конкретным играм или плагинам:
SteamOS сам по себе имеет открытые issue про чёрный экран / «радужные» артефакты / мерцание после сна — не связанные с каким-либо конкретным приложением.
Chromium на Linux (а интерфейс Steam как раз работает на CEF — Chromium Embedded Framework) имеет отдельный, тоже хорошо задокументированный баг: GPU-компоузитор браузера после выхода из сна «просыпается» со старыми/повреждёнными текстурами для тех элементов, которые активно анимировались в момент засыпания.
Плагин как раз постоянно двигает (transform) фон/средний план/передний план/лого каждый кадр, пока включён гироскоп — то есть он один из немногих, кто непрерывно «дёргает» GPU-слои поверх интерфейса Steam. Это отлично объясняет и «троение» (наложение нескольких устаревших закомпонованных кадров), и «диагональное движение» (смещение по X и Y одновременно). 

Какие правки и дополнения были реализованы: (защитное, best-effort решение)
Так как сам баг — на уровне браузера/ОС и не чинится снаружи, я добавил механизм обнаружения пробуждения + принудительного сброса GPU-слоёв:
Цикл анимации теперь замечает аномально большой разрыв между кадрами (>1.5с — невозможно при обычной работе, но типично сразу после сна) и в этот момент принудительно заставляет браузер "сбросить" закомпонованные слои для всех анимируемых элементов (фон/лого/средний-передний план/фоновая картинка/превью), вместо повторного использования потенциально испорченного состояния GPU.
Дополнительные сигналы «подстраховки»: document.visibilitychange и SteamClient.System.RegisterForOnResumeFromSuspend.
Фильтр сглаживания и автоцентровка сбрасываются «с нуля» при обнаруженном пробуждении.
Добавлена строка отладки «Восстановлений после сна» (при включённом Debug) — чтобы тестеры могли проверить, действительно ли срабатывает защита вокруг реальных засыпаний.
На бэкенде: чтение гироскопа (hidraw) теперь само восстанавливается, если устройство пропадает/переинициализируется вокруг сна, вместо необратимой остановки до перезапуска плагина.

lopesleo/discord-lite.name: Discord Lite v1.2.0 - PKCE OAuth2 Security Update
lopesleo/discord-lite.body:
## 🔒 Security & Authentication Overhaul (PKCE)

This release introduces a critical security update by implementing **PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)**, eliminating the need for a client secret and aligning with modern OAuth2 standards for public applications.

### 🛡️ Security Improvements
* **PKCE Implementation:** Transitioned the OAuth2 flow to use Proof Key for Code Exchange. This standard is significantly more secure for installed apps (mobile/desktop).
* **No More Client Secret:** Completely removed `CLIENT_SECRET` from the source code/binary. The application now functions strictly as a public client.

### 🛠️ Technical Enhancements
* **Optimized OAuth2 Flow:** Authorization now utilizes code challenge/verifier instead of hardcoded credentials.
* **Enhanced Logging:** Added comprehensive and descriptive error messages during the authentication process to aid debugging.
* **Deployment Script:** Introduced `deploy.ps1` for automated builds.
    * Supports automatic deployment.
    * Adds support for remote installation directly to the Steam Deck.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
* **ZIP Structure:** Fixed an issue where files were not in the root of the archive, ensuring correct installation.
* **Credential Cleanup:** Patched potential credential leaks by removing legacy implementation details.

### 📦 Compatibility
* **Discord API:** Fully compatible with the latest secure public app guidelines.
* **Steam Deck:** Improved installation reliability and script execution.

---

### ⚠️ Migration Notes / Breaking Changes
**For existing users:**
1.  Install the new version normally.
2.  **Action Required:** You must **re-authenticate** with Discord upon first launch. The move to PKCE requires a fresh authorization token.


------

------

## 🔒 Melhorias de Segurança e Autenticação (PKCE)

Esta versão traz uma atualização crítica de segurança com a implementação do **PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)**, eliminando a necessidade de *client secrets* e adequando o plugin aos padrões modernos do Discord para aplicativos públicos.

### 🛡️ Segurança
* **Implementação PKCE:** A autenticação OAuth2 agora utiliza o padrão PKCE, que é muito mais seguro para aplicações instaladas (desktop/mobile).
* **Remoção do Client Secret:** O `CLIENT_SECRET` foi totalmente removido do código-fonte. O plugin agora opera como uma aplicação pública legítima.

### 🛠️ Melhorias Técnicas
* **Novo Fluxo OAuth2:** O processo de autorização agora usa *code challenge/verifier*, eliminando credenciais *hardcoded*.
* **Logs Melhorados:** Mensagens de erro mais descritivas e logs detalhados durante a autenticação.
* **Script de Deploy:** Adicionado o `deploy.ps1` para automação.
    * Suporte a deploy automático.
    * Suporte a instalação remota diretamente no Steam Deck.

### 🐛 Correções de Bugs
* **Estrutura do ZIP:** Corrigido um problema onde os arquivos não ficavam na raiz do arquivo compactado, o que impedia a instalação correta.
* **Limpeza de Credenciais:** Resolvidos potenciais vazamentos de credenciais no código antigo.

### 📦 Compatibilidade
* **Discord API:** Compatível com as práticas de segurança mais recentes para Apps Públicos.
* **Steam Deck:** Deploy simplificado e mais confiável.

---

### ⚠️ Notas de Migração
**Para usuários existentes:**
1.  Instale a nova versão normalmente.
2.  **Ação Necessária:** Será preciso **reautenticar** com o Discord. A melhoria de segurança exige um novo token de autorização.

jinzhongjia/decky-tools.name: v0.1.2
jinzhongjia/decky-tools.body:
## 改进：系统监控开销大幅降低
在 Steam Deck OLED 上实测（每秒采样一次，新旧版本交替运行对比）：
- 监控进程 CPU 占用降低约 32%（面板关闭约 713 → 485 µs/s，面板打开约 708 → 483 µs/s），读文件的系统调用从每秒约 20 次降到 6–7 次。
- 面板关闭时，插件的 Python 进程不再有任何定时唤醒（82 → 0 µs/s）；面板打开时其开销降低约 66%（1376 → 467 µs/s）。

具体改动：
- Steam Deck 等 AMD APU 上，CPU / GPU 的频率、温度、占用和 APU 功耗改为一次读取 SMU 指标获得，取代 ACPI 温度区与十余个单独的文件读取。CPU 温度改用 SMU 给出的核心温度，与旧数据源相差约 1–2 °C。
- 充放电状态改为由内核事件驱动：插拔电源后 1 秒内更新，不再每秒查询交流适配器。电量与充放电功率仍每秒读取，保持准确。
- 监控进程以低优先级运行，被唤醒时不会抢占游戏线程，每秒一次的唤醒可与其他定时器合并以省电。

otisabiburada/decky-screen-mirror.body:
## Screen Mirror PiP 0.5.0 (beta)

Mirror your **iPhone's screen** into a small window **over your game** in Gaming Mode, with the iPhone's built-in
Screen Mirroring (AirPlay). Sound plays from the Deck. No setup and no extra app: the AirPlay receiver comes with the plugin.

### Highlights
- **Window over any game**, any corner and size; phone-shaped, or fill a wide window. Opens and closes by itself.
- **Mirror volume**: just the iPhone's sound; game sound untouched.
- **Approved phones only** (optional): a new iPhone types a PIN once; a notification shows the PIN.
- **Rename** the Deck, **quality** presets (1080p / 720p / 540p), **60 fps**, **low delay** mode.
- **Recovers by itself** after sleep, Wi-Fi changes and receiver crashes.
- **Check setup** and **Save problem report** built in.

### Install
Decky settings > Developer mode on > **Developer** > **Install Plugin from URL**:
`Or download `screen-mirror-pip-v0.5.0.zip` below and use **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.
Then on the iPhone: Control Center > Screen Mirroring > **Steam Deck**.

### Known limits
- About 0.1-0.3 s of delay: great for watching, not for playing iPhone games through the Deck.
- Same Wi-Fi; guest networks with client isolation block AirPlay discovery.
- Copy-protected video (e.g. Netflix) shows black, as on any AirPlay receiver.
- Uses undocumented Steam internals for the overlay; a Steam update can break it.

### Status
Beta. Mirroring is confirmed on a Steam Deck (SteamOS 3.8) with an iPhone; newer options (PIN, 60 fps, low delay)
are tested in a SteamOS-like environment.
Problems: More > Help > **Save problem report** and attach the file to an issue.

### Licenses
Plugin code: BSD-3-Clause. Bundled receiver: UxPlay (GPL-3.0), FFmpeg AAC/ALAC decoders, GStreamer plugins and
libplist (LGPL-2.1+). Their complete sources are attached below as `screen-mirror-pip-v0.5.0-third-party-sources.tar`.

Not affiliated with Apple. AirPlay and iPhone are trademarks of Apple Inc.

koffcheck/potato-deals.body:
## What's changed

### 🐛 Bug fixes
- **Steam Beta UI**: Added `SteamClient.Browser?.OpenURL` fallback so links open correctly in the new Beta UI (fixes #1)
- **Loading stuck forever**: `sync_wishlist` now has a 120 s frontend timeout — the spinner can no longer get permanently stuck

### ⚡ Performance fixes
- **First-open hang (2+ min)**: Removed blocking network calls from the `get_bootstrap` startup path — plugin opens instantly even on slow networks
- **Decky event loop blocking**: Backend now runs in a thread pool (`asyncio.to_thread`) instead of blocking the event loop directly
- **Double network round-trip on sync**: `sync_wishlist` no longer calls `get_bootstrap` a second time — eliminates up to 90 s of extra work after every wishlist refresh
- **Sales tab blocking**: Removed HEAD-request loop + page-fetch loop from `get_sales_events` (was adding up to 95 s of blocking per call)
- **Wishlist auto-mode**: Removed 6th duplicate HTTP request in auto-mode without API key

### 📦 Installation
Download `potato-deals-v3.1.15.zip` and install via **Decky Loader → Settings → Install Plugin from ZIP**.

# Decky EnvTest - Release Notes

## Version 1.0b

 - Initial Release 🚀

### Overview

Decky EnvTest is a debugging tool for Decky that logs game-specific details from Decky's SteamClient.Apps and extracts Heroic configuration data. This first release provides essential logging and data extraction capabilities, making it easier to analyze game environment details within Decky.

### Features

- ✅ **Game Data Logging** – Retrieves and logs detailed information about installed Steam games.
- ✅ **Heroic Data Retrieval** – Fetches and filters configuration details from Heroic.
- ✅ **Clean Data Display** – Removes unnecessary fields and presents a structured, readable format.
- ✅ **Export JSON Data** – Save logged game data as a JSON file for offline inspection.
- ✅ **Decky Integration** – Works seamlessly within Decky UI with minimal setup.

### Installation

1. **Install ZIP or from URL in Developer Settings** from the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/wowitsjack/deckyloader-envtest/releases).
2. **Let the install finish**.
3. **Restart Decky** and access the plugin via the UI.

### Usage

1. Open the **Decky EnvTest** plugin from Decky.
2. Select a game and click **DEBUG: Log Game Data** to fetch Steam data.
3. Click **Pull Heroic Data** to retrieve Heroic configurations (if applicable).
4. Use **Export JSON** to download the log data.

### Known Issues

- 🔹 Some non-Steam games may not appear in the logged data.
- 🔹 Heroic data may be unavailable if the game is not configured in Heroic.

### Future Improvements

- 📌 Support for additional game platforms.
- 📌 More filtering and search capabilities.
- 📌 UI enhancements for better readability.

### Acknowledgements

- Thanks to the **Decky Team** for their great plugin platform.

hrhnick/decky-romsync.name: ROM Sync 1.9.0
hrhnick/decky-romsync.body:
Turns a ROM folder into Steam shortcuts with artwork and per-system
collections. Runs inside Game Mode, uses Valve's own React components, and
never touches `shortcuts.vdf`.

## Installing

ROM Sync is not in the Decky plugin store yet, so install is manual:

1. Install [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz) if you do not have it.
2. QAM → **Decky** → gear icon → **General** → turn on **Developer Mode**.
3. Download the `ROM-Sync-*.zip` attached below, onto the Deck itself.
4. Decky settings → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from ZIP File**, and pick
   the archive.

Full instructions, including a Desktop Mode fallback, are in the
[README](https://github.com/hrhnick/decky-romsync#installing).

## What is in the archive

The seven files that run on device — `plugin.json`, `package.json`, the four
Python modules and the compiled `dist/index.js` — inside a single `ROM Sync/`
folder. TypeScript sources and build config are not included; build them with
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run build`.

## Notes

- Everything defers to the next Sync. Toggling a system, excluding a ROM or
  changing a core takes effect then, not immediately — removing a shortcut
  discards its Steam playtime and cannot be undone, so a mis-tap costs nothing.
- Shortcuts already imported by Steam ROM Manager are adopted rather than
  duplicated.
- Artwork needs a SteamGridDB key, set on the Settings page. Without one the
  sync still runs; art is filled in on a later sync once a key is present.

feelsrat/decky-task-manager.name: Decky Task Manager v0.1.20
feelsrat/decky-task-manager.body:
## New UI
- Compact tab bar with badges for running plugins and plugins with problems
- **Overview:** health summary, CPU/RAM tiles with recent history, live/snapshot freshness, a needs-attention list and top plugins that jump straight to details or logs, plus a Refresh button when live monitoring is off
- **Plugins:** grouped into running, idle and disabled. Select one to see current vs peak CPU/RAM and Disable/Enable, Stop and Logs buttons
- **Logs:** plugins ranked by severity. Select one to see known problems, the most frequent error lines and how fast the log is growing
- Confirmation dialogs before disabling, stopping, clearing all logs, starting a fresh capture or installing an update
- Buttons are native Steam buttons laid out for D-pad navigation, so they work with the physical controls
- Problems already showing when you open the panel no longer pop up as alerts; several new ones are combined into one

## Fixes
- **Security:** update checks and downloads now verify HTTPS certificates (verification was previously turned off while installing as root)
- Plugins that stop running no longer stay listed as active with old CPU/RAM values
- Log scanning matches exact plugin folder/file names, so one plugin no longer picks up (or clears) another plugin's logs
- A failed update check is no longer cached for 24 hours
- Enabling/disabling a plugin writes Decky's loader.json atomically and keeps its ownership

## Performance
- Live monitoring reads the plugin list once per sample instead of five times, and scans the log folder once per pass
