# Armada LSFG v0.1.2

## 🇫🇷 Français

### Nouveautés et corrections

- Ajout de la prise en charge de plusieurs bibliothèques Steam.
- Les jeux installés sur une carte microSD ou dans une bibliothèque Steam secondaire sont maintenant détectés.
- Lecture des bibliothèques Steam déclarées dans `libraryfolders.vdf`.
- Les bibliothèques amovibles non montées sont ignorées proprement.
- Gestion des manifests Steam pouvant rester temporairement en double après le déplacement d'un jeu entre deux bibliothèques.
- La bibliothèque Steam principale continue de fonctionner comme auparavant.

### Documentation

- Ajout d'un guide de mise à jour pour les utilisateurs ayant déjà une ancienne version d'Armada LSFG.
- Ajout d'une procédure de désinstallation.
- Documentation de la conservation des configurations et des sauvegardes lors d'une mise à jour.

### Important

- Armada LSFG ne modifie pas les Steam Launch Options.
- Cette release n'ajoute pas la prise en charge des jeux Linux natifs par LSFG-VK.

---

## 🇬🇧 English

### Changes and fixes

- Added support for multiple Steam libraries.
- Games installed on a microSD card or in a secondary Steam library can now be detected.
- Steam libraries are discovered from `libraryfolders.vdf`.
- Unmounted removable libraries are safely ignored.
- Handles duplicate Steam manifests that may temporarily remain after moving a game between libraries.
- The primary Steam library continues to work as before.

### Documentation

- Added update instructions for users who already have an older Armada LSFG version installed.
- Added an uninstall procedure.
- Documented configuration preservation and backups during updates.

### Important

- Armada LSFG does not modify Steam Launch Options.
- This release does not add LSFG-VK support for native Linux games.

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.2.0
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Links installed plugins to the repo they came from, so checking for updates no
longer means typing a repo for each one by hand.

The official store builds every plugin from a submodule in its plugin database,
and that database records which repo each plugin comes from. Bazaar now reads
that index and matches it against the folder a plugin is installed under, which
resolves every plugin currently in the store. Anything the store has never
carried falls back to the files the plugin itself ships.

- **Find repos for your unlinked plugins** appears in the panel whenever
  something is unlinked. One press links everything it can work out, and leaves
  the rest alone.
- **Links say where they came from.** One matched against the store's database
  is taken as fact. One worked out from a plugin's own files is marked
  *detected*, because those can still name the repo a plugin was forked from
  rather than the one it is maintained in today — worth a glance, and one press
  to correct.
- **An automatic link reports updates immediately**, comparing the version on
  disk against the latest release instead of waiting for you to mark which
  release you are on. Any older link with no release recorded benefits too.
- **Plugins hosted outside GitHub are skipped** rather than guessed at, and a
  branch the store builds from is not mistaken for the branch releases are
  tagged on.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/compare/v1.1.2...v1.2.0

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.1.2
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Fixes 1.0.9 being treated as newer than 1.0.10.

Releases were taken in the order GitHub returned them, which is the order they
were created rather than which version is highest. A plugin sitting on 1.0.9
could be reported as up to date with 1.0.10 already published, and the release
picker could offer an older release at the top of the list.

- **Releases are now ordered by version**, so the latest release is the highest
  one — 1.0.10 after 1.0.9, and a pre-release before the release it leads to.
- **An update is only offered when it is actually newer.** A release cut for an
  older line no longer shows up as an update waiting to be installed.
- Tags that carry no version number at all still fall back to publish date.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/compare/v1.1.1...v1.1.2

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.1.1
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Fixes a branch showing up empty when its releases are pre-releases.

Picking a branch hid pre-releases before it ever considered the branch, so a
branch that ships previews — a `testing` or `beta` branch, which is most of the
reason to pin one in the first place — looked like it had no releases at all,
and the dialog blamed the branch for it.

- **Pre-releases are now counted per branch**, and the dialog says how many it is
  hiding and why instead of claiming nothing was tagged from the branch.
- **"Include pre-releases" is in the Add and Source dialogs**, next to the branch
  picker where the question actually comes up. It is the same setting as the one
  in Settings, so update checks follow it too.
- Flipping it is instant — every release is fetched once and narrowed on the
  Deck, so neither the toggle nor the branch picker spends a GitHub request.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/compare/v1.1.0...v1.1.1

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.1.0
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Plugins can now follow a single branch of their repo instead of every release.

- **Pick a branch when adding or re-pointing a plugin.** The Add and Source
  dialogs list the repo's branches, with the default branch first. Only releases
  whose tag was cut from the chosen branch are offered — and every later update
  check stays on that branch, so a plugin set to `beta` never offers a `main`
  release and the other way round.
- **Any branch** is still the default, so plugins tracked before this update
  keep considering every release until you narrow them down.
- The panel row and the plugin's Source line now show which branch is being
  followed, as `owner/repo@branch`.

Note that GitHub only records the branch a tag was *cut from*. A release tagged
straight from a commit has no branch attached and shows up only under **Any
branch**.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.0.0
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
First release.

Decky Bazaar lists **every** plugin installed on your Deck — store-sourced or
not — and keeps the ones that never went through the official store updated
from their GitHub releases.

- **Add a plugin from GitHub** by owner and repo rather than a URL. Paste a full
  URL into either field and it splits itself across both.
- **Finds the release zip for you**, newest first, and reads the plugin's real
  name and version out of the zip before installing, so it lands under the name
  Decky expects instead of a guess from the file name.
- **Installs through decky-loader itself** — the same confirmation prompt,
  unzip, remote binary download, permission fixup and hot reload the official
  store uses. A zip is only accepted if it looks like a real plugin package, so
  source archives and multi-plugin zips are refused with an explanation rather
  than installed into a broken state.
- **Tracks versions and offers updates.** One button re-checks every tracked
  plugin against GitHub, and rows with an update waiting sort to the top.
- **Adopts plugins you already have.** Link an installed plugin to a repo and
  mark the release you are on, without reinstalling it.
- **Optional GitHub token** to lift the 60-requests-per-hour anonymous rate
  limit and reach private repos. It is stored in
  `~/homebrew/settings/decky-bazaar/bazaar.json`, chmod'd to `600`.

## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/commits/v1.0.0

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: egpu-switch 0.3.4: final release (security fixes, discontinued)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
**This is the last release of egpu-switch.** The project continues as
**[Yby eGPU](https://github.com/TiPSilva/yby-egpu)**, which provides GPU switching
and safe eject without depending on all-ways-egpu, plus a desktop app and
additional controls. Its installer removes egpu-switch from Decky. Update
to 0.3.4 if you still use egpu-switch, then migrate to Yby eGPU.

### Security fixes

- **High: a user-writable file was executed as root.** The plugin runs as root
  and executed `all-ways-egpu` from `~/bin` (and from any user's
  `/home/*/bin`) every few seconds. Any program running as a user could
  replace that file and gain root without a password. The plugin, and the
  shutdown hook in `extras/`, now only run all-ways-egpu when the file and
  every folder above it belong to root and nobody else can write to them.
  If yours is in `~/bin`, the panel shows a command to install it
  for the whole system.
- **Medium: root followed a link when saving settings.** `settings.json`
  lives in a folder the user owns; replacing it with a link made root
  overwrite arbitrary system files, and the settings screen could read any
  JSON file. Settings are now read and written without following links,
  through a temporary file, and only the two known options are kept.
- **Low: fixed file names in `/tmp`.** The shutdown hook wrote its errors to
  predictable files in `/tmp` as root. It no longer uses `/tmp`.
- **Low: Deep rescan could pick a bridge in another PCI domain.** On
  machines with more than one PCI domain it could reset the wrong bridge. It
  now matches the domain too.

These issues were identified during the review for the Yby eGPU release.

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: eGPU Switch v0.3.3 (stable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
First stable release since v0.1.0, with everything learned from real hardware testing on an AyaNeo (AMD Ryzen 7840U) and an ROG Ally X folded in.

## Highlights since v0.1.0

- Safe eject flow: unloads NVIDIA modules and removes the eGPU from the PCI bus before you disconnect the Thunderbolt cable, instead of only switching boot VGA.
- Deep Rescan option for cases where a plain PCI rescan does not bring the eGPU back after reconnecting.
- Automatic HDMI audio rebind after a rescan re-adds the eGPU, gated on actual ELD health instead of a fixed sleep.
- Connection diagnostics panel: connection type (Thunderbolt or PCIe), link speed and width, Thunderbolt controller and peripheral names, and boot/sleep freeze fix status.
- Friendly GPU and Thunderbolt controller names parsed from machine-readable lspci and boltctl output, picking the authorized peripheral instead of just the first one listed.
- Settings persistence for the auto-eject and deep rescan toggles.
- Documented fix for AMD platforms that freeze on boot or sleep/wake with the eGPU connected (thunderbolt.host_reset=0 kernel argument).
- Standalone shutdown-eject hook, distributed separately from the plugin, for systems that freeze on shutdown/reboot with the eGPU still attached.
- Dependency-free self-check test suite covering the pure parsing and decision functions.

## Installation

Download `egpu-switch.zip` below and install via Decky Loader: Settings -> Developer -> Install Plugin from ZIP File. Requires `all-ways-egpu` to be installed and configured first (see README).

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: v0.3.3 (dev, unstable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
Unstable dev-branch build, not the recommended release for most users (use [v0.1.0](https://github.com/TiPSilva/egpu-switch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) for that). Published specifically so testers on different hardware can try recent fixes and new options.

## Changed since v0.3.2

- **Fixed a real audio bug**: eject the eGPU, then click Switch to eGPU directly (without a manual Rescan first) could bring video back on the TV with no audio, and restarting the display manager didn't help. The plugin used to decide whether to repair audio based on whether a rescan had been "needed" for the video side, which is the wrong signal: automatic Thunderbolt hotplug can re-add the eGPU (video and audio both) before you press anything, so the video side already looked fine while the audio codec was still broken from that same re-enumeration. It now checks the ALSA card's own ELD state directly and repairs audio whenever it's actually broken, regardless of what triggered the reconnect. Confirmed fixed on hardware, and it's cheap: when audio is already fine, the check is a couple of instant file reads with no added delay.
- **New doc**: if the whole system hangs on boot with the eGPU already connected, or on wake from sleep with it active, see the README section on `thunderbolt.host_reset=0`. Confirmed on hardware (AMD Ryzen 7840U) to fix both outright, not just work around them. Includes the `rpm-ostree kargs` commands for Bazzite/SteamOS-style atomic systems.

## Install

Same as the stable release: Desktop Mode → download the zip below → Game Mode → Decky Developer Mode → Install Plugin from ZIP File.

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: v0.3.2 (dev, unstable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
Unstable dev-branch build, not the recommended release for most users (use [v0.1.0](https://github.com/TiPSilva/egpu-switch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) for that). Published specifically so testers on different hardware can try recent fixes and new options.

## Changed since v0.3.1

- **Data loss guard**: nothing previously checked for mounted storage before detaching PCI devices. Some NVIDIA boards expose their own USB-C controller as a sibling function, and Deep rescan removes an entire parent bridge, so an enclosure carrying an NVMe or a USB storage controller next to the GPU was one eject away from losing it mid-write. Eject and Deep rescan now refuse upfront (before the display manager is even touched) when mounted storage sits behind the target.
- **Concurrency fix**: `rescan_pci` now takes the same operation lock as every other action. It had grown from a single, safe sysfs write into an operation that can remove a PCI bridge, reauthorize a Thunderbolt tunnel and rebind a driver, while still running unserialized, so closing and reopening the QAM mid-operation could let two mutating calls run at once. Confirmed on hardware after the fix: a real concurrent request was caught and rejected, and a retry right after ran cleanly.
- **Lock rejections are now logged**, naming which action was rejected, instead of being silently swallowed.
- **Frontend polling now pauses during an operation**, instead of hammering `all-ways-egpu status` as root every 5 seconds while a multi-minute operation is racing that same state.
- **`_unload` now restarts the display manager** if a Decky-initiated reload lands mid-operation, instead of leaving the session stopped with no code left running to bring it back.
- **Thunderbolt tunnel reauthorization fix**: the experimental logic added to work around a reported reconnect issue had an anchored regex that could never match `boltctl list`'s actual output (a silent no-op), and it authorized every unauthorized device it found rather than only ones the user had previously approved. Both fixed.
- **Audio rebind now waits for a real display connection** (a DRM connector reporting "connected") instead of a blind timed sleep, so it can only ever land later than the timing already validated on hardware, never earlier.
- Added `tests/selfcheck.py`, a dependency-free self-check for the three pieces of logic where being wrong is expensive: the storage guard, the Thunderbolt authorization parser, and the `all-ways-egpu status` parsing everything else reads from.
- Packaging: committed the `pnpm-lock.yaml` the plugin store's build requires, and added the `publish` metadata block to `plugin.json`.

## Install

Same as the stable release: Desktop Mode → download the zip below → Game Mode → Decky Developer Mode → Install Plugin from ZIP File.

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: v0.3.1 (dev, unstable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
Unstable dev-branch build, not the recommended release for most users (use [v0.1.0](https://github.com/TiPSilva/egpu-switch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) for that). Published specifically so testers on different hardware can try recent fixes and new options.

## Changed since v0.3.0

- **Fixed the Deep rescan safety check.** Tester logs (Strix Halo / CachyOS Handheld) showed that after an eject, the system can automatically re-add the eGPU as a broken, half-initialized device: it exists on the PCI bus but is not actually usable (no working `boot_vga`, the same `bridge window ... can't assign; no space` allocation issue). The previous check saw "device exists" and skipped the deep path exactly when it was needed, which also made **Switch to eGPU** give up without doing anything. Deep rescan now triggers whenever `all-ways-egpu` does not report the eGPU as connected and no driver is bound to it, covering both "missing from the bus" and "re-added broken".
- With that fix, the expected recovery flow after a disconnect (or after waking from sleep with the eGPU previously ejected) is: **Rescan for eGPU**, then **Switch to eGPU**, all without leaving Game Mode and without rebooting. Log lines to look for in `journalctl -u plugin_loader | grep -i "deep rescan"`: `remove bridge ... ok=True` (deep path ran), `eGPU connected and functional, skipping bridge removal` (nothing to fix), or `functions still driver-bound (...), skipping bridge removal` (safety stop).

## Install

Same as the stable release: Desktop Mode → download the zip below → Game Mode → Decky Developer Mode → Install Plugin from ZIP File.

enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.name: v0.6.11
enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.body:
# v0.6.11 — remove the current version from the version card

The card at the top of the panel shows the HelixSR version in use. It now also tells you where that version is installed, and lets you remove it right there.

## What changed

- **The path note**: the folder the active version lives in. The backend always knew it, the panel never showed it.
- **"Remove this version"** right under that note (danger tone, two-tap confirm — the same armed state as the *Remove* in the Version list). Removing the version you are using switches the plugin to another one.

Everything else is unchanged.

## Updating from 0.6.10

Use the panel's **Update to v0.6.11** button and confirm Decky's install popup, or install `helixsr-muse-plugin-v0.6.11.zip` from Decky's developer settings (Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File).

## Checks

52 backend tests and 23 UI checks. Not yet run on a Steam Deck.

enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.name: v0.6.10
enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.body:
# v0.6.10 — the version in use gets its own card

Which HelixSR version the panel is working with was easy to miss: its details were mixed into the step header and the inventory list.

## What changed

- **The version in use has its own card at the very top**: the release tag (`v2.0.0` — the header only showed the DLL stamp, so the release and the built DLL were indistinguishable), the network state as a chip, and a line with the DLL version, the size on disk, the bundled Scaler version and whether frame generation is built.
- The step card moved below it and no longer repeats the version line.
- **A divider** separates the state from the *Last action* card, so the log output is clearly apart from the version and the step.

Everything else is unchanged.

## Updating from 0.6.9

Use the panel's **Update to v0.6.10** button and confirm Decky's install popup, or install `helixsr-muse-plugin-v0.6.10.zip` from Decky's developer settings (Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File).

## Checks

52 backend tests and 23 UI checks. Not yet run on a Steam Deck.

enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.name: v0.6.9
enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.body:
# v0.6.9 — drop the sticky header again

0.6.8 made the header stick to the top of the panel, so the step and its action would stay visible while scrolling a long game list. It does not behave inside the Decky panel, so it is gone again: the header sits at the top of the panel and scrolls with the list like everything else.

Everything else from 0.6.8 is unchanged: the game list can be searched and filtered, a game the last *Verify installs* found damaged gets a *Needs repair* chip and **Repair** as its main action, the anti-cheat rule is stated on the card, the *Extra game folder* field is behind a button, and the release picker shows only the versions you do not have.

## Updating from 0.6.8

Use the panel's **Update to v0.6.9** button and confirm Decky's install popup, or install `helixsr-muse-plugin-v0.6.9.zip` from Decky's developer settings (Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File).

## Checks

52 backend tests and 23 UI checks. Not yet run on a Steam Deck.

enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.name: v0.6.8
enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.body:
# v0.6.8 — find the games you need

The second UI pass: the game list can be filtered, a game that needs attention says so, and the header stays in sight.

## What changed

- **The game list can be searched and filtered**: a search field (name or folder) and a status filter — All / Installed / Not installed / Needs repair. The header line says how many are shown.
- **A broken game stands out**: a game the last *Verify installs* found damaged gets a **Needs repair** chip, the reason (a Steam update replaced the drop-ins) and **Repair** as its main action. Until now the verify result was only a number in the list header.
- **The anti-cheat rule is on the card**: "Anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat) — only the FSR drop-in is used here."
- **The header sticks to the top** of the panel, so the step and its action stay visible while you scroll a long game list.
- **Smaller things**: the *Extra game folder* field is behind an *Add a game folder* button, the header offers *Re-scan games* at the last step, and the release picker now shows only the releases you do not have yet (the ones you have are in the list below with their details and Use/Remove), so a release is no longer listed twice.

## Updating from 0.6.7

Use the panel's **Update to v0.6.8** button and confirm Decky's install popup, or install `helixsr-muse-plugin-v0.6.8.zip` from Decky's developer settings (Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File).

## Checks

52 backend tests and 23 UI checks (5 new). The sticky header and the new focus order are worth a look on a Steam Deck. Not yet run on a Steam Deck.

enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.name: v0.6.7
enzodiloreto/helixsr-decky-plugin-muse.body:
# v0.6.7 — a panel that explains itself

The plugin did not say where you were in the flow: it started straight into the sections, so the order (download → build → scan → install) had to be known. The game cards had up to ten buttons each, and the result of your last action sat in a section at the bottom of the panel.

## What changed

- **A header on top**: the active version and its network state, "Step 2 of 4 — Build the network" with a one-line hint, and the one button that moves the flow forward (download the picked release / build the network (+ FG) / scan the games). A running download or build shows its progress and its cancel button there.
- **A "Last action" card** right under the header with the result of what you just did (the Output section at the bottom is gone).
- **Fewer buttons per game**: the way picker and the primary action (Install / Update / Switch to …) stay visible, the rest (Remove, Repair, FG, Roll back, Settings, Log) is behind a **More** button — three to five focus stops per game instead of up to ten.
- **Destructive actions look destructive**: Remove, Remove old versions and Factory reset use the danger tone.
- **Clearer wording**: the way picker's first entry is "Automatic" (it was called "Recommended", the same word the state chip used), and the chip says what the game gets: "Auto: Scaler", "Auto: FSR drop-in", "✓ Scaler 2.0.0", "→ FSR drop-in".
- **The scan says what it left out**: "14 games · 3 installed · 12/12 verified · 27 not compatible (not listed)".

## Updating from 0.6.6

Use the panel's **Update to v0.6.7** button and confirm Decky's install popup, or install `helixsr-muse-plugin-v0.6.7.zip` from Decky's developer settings (Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File).

## Checks

52 backend tests and 18 UI checks. The new header and the "More" button change the focus order, so a look on a Steam Deck is worth it. Not yet run on a Steam Deck.

lozazamastro/now-playing.name: Version 2.5.0
lozazamastro/now-playing.body:
Less waiting, fewer silent starts. Now Playing 2.5.0 improves Spotify audio recovery and gets you back to your Spotify and YouTube Music libraries sooner.

## Improvements

- Spotify Home and Library reuse previously loaded content for a faster return to your music.
- YouTube Music remembers Home, Search, music details and Library content between plugin restarts.
- Large libraries become available progressively while the rest loads in the background. Play All and Shuffle still use the complete collection.
- Spotify reconnects to the current default audio output if the previous device changes or becomes unavailable.

## Fixes

- Fixed silent Spotify starts after an audio-device change, where playback appeared active but no sound reached the audio output.
- Fixed old library results reappearing after a refresh, disconnect or account change.

lozazamastro/now-playing.name: Version 2.4.0
lozazamastro/now-playing.body:
**Important**
**Please disconnect and reconnect to Spotify after the update.**

This update makes Spotify playback more independent and resilient, extends surround sound to Spotify, and smooths out source changes across the entire plugin.

## What’s new

- **Spotify surround upmix** now supports 5.1 and 7.1 output with the same per-speaker controls available for local music and YouTube Music.

## Improvements

- Spotify playback services now recover automatically after startup and authenticate in the background when the saved account can be reused.
- YouTube Music skips unavailable tracks instead of leaving playback stuck.
- Surround settings now update Spotify’s integrated mixer live, without stopping, reloading or losing the position of the current track.
- The LFE channel uses a restrained 120 Hz low-pass mix with additional headroom, preventing bass from being redistributed excessively across the main speakers.
- Stereo and surround playback now share consistent headroom, avoiding sudden volume jumps when Spotify upmix is enabled or disabled.
- Source ownership is stricter, so Spotify no longer takes control while local music or YouTube Music is selected.
- Runtime checks now guard Spotify API polling, helper ownership, source isolation and live surround updates.

## Fixes

- Fixed Spotify occasionally failing to start until **Restart plugin services** was pressed.
- Fixed Spotify taking over playback controls while another source was active.
- Fixed broken YouTube Music items blocking the rest of the queue.

lozazamastro/now-playing.name: Version 2.3.0
lozazamastro/now-playing.body: - ThemeDeck now reacts reliably to every Now Playing source. ThemeDeck stays silent only while a track is playing and resumes immediately when it is paused, stopped or no longer available.

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker 1.1.0
failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This release brings the Status and Logs tabs over from my other project, CheevoDeck, offering more info on each freeze mitigation event. Also ports the system over where this plugin now checks for updates, allowing you to install updates easily through the desktop updater or link copy method.

## New

- The main section now becomes the Status tab, showing your protection status, as well as basic status such as how many QAM freezes were prevented and how many QAM freezes were recovered from.

- A Logs tab has been added that shows you the last 200 mitigation/recovery events, along with basic logging info.

- Stormbreaker now checks GitHub for a new release twice a day. When an update is available, you will be notified once with a toast, the new update message will show in-app, and download options will appear.

That's all for today. Since this is pretty stable, there shouldn't be many updates after this point unless a SteamOS update breaks it. In that case, I will be sure to release one. It's unlikely though since Stormbreaker looks at symptoms of a problem, not the source.

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker 1.0.1
failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This is a small patch release with a variety of fixes that came from review of the same code from my other project, CheevoDeck. Everything still works the same, but it is more stable now.

## Fixes

- Stormbreaker and Automatic Recovery now only run in Game Mode, so they won't unnecessarily run in Desktop Mode. It makes sense because the QAM freeze issue can only occur in Game Mode anyway.
- Fixed a problem where Automatic Recovery failed to restart Steam's interface while a game with a non-Latin name was running.
- Fixed a problem at startup where Stormbreaker stays off for a whole session if Steam's menus weren't ready when the plugin loaded.
- Fixed an issue where reloading the plugin at the wrong time would leave CheevoDeck thinking Stormbreaker was still running after it was gone, so neither plugin would break a storm until Steam restarted.
- Settings and recovery logs are now saved in a way that can't be pointed at another file on your system.

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker 1.0.0
failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This is the first release of Stormbreaker, ported from my other project, [CheevoDeck](https://github.com/FAILINATOR5000/decky-cheevodeck).

Stormbreaker is a Decky Loader plugin for SteamOS platforms that both prevents and recovers you from a rare SteamOS bug related to the Quick Access Menu (QAM), where in rare cases upon opening, it gets stuck and becomes unresponsive. While rare, it is devastating as controls also become unresponsive, so usually it results in hard resetting the device, losing game progress in the process.

woodsi3/forza-dualsense-decky.name: Decky Forza DualSense Haptics v1.0.0
woodsi3/forza-dualsense-decky.body:
## Forza DualSense Haptics v1.0.0

The first stable release of Forza DualSense Haptics for Decky Loader.

This plugin converts Forza UDP telemetry into meaningful DualSense adaptive-trigger and haptic feedback natively in Game Mode on SteamOS.

### Manual Install Instructions:

1. Download the latest release ZIP.
2. Extract the `forza-dualsense-haptics` folder into:
   `~/homebrew/plugins/`
3. Restart Decky Loader (or safer, reboot the Steam Deck).
4. Enable UDP telemetry in Forza and configure it to send telemetry to your Steam Deck on IP 127.0.0.1, Port 5300.
5. Launch the game and enjoy.

The plugin will automatically create its settings on first launch.

Further detail on manual Decky plugin installation can be found [here](https://wiki.deckbrew.xyz/en/user-guide/settings).

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.4.0
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## ✨ Features

- use the shared Steam notification style with the NVIDIA icon (moi952)

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- support Main driver staging and guard EFI shutdown migration (60plus)
  Omit empty Arch pin arguments and recognize Valve's complete Main finalizer
  loop before inserting the driver repair hook.
  Arm a verified runtime systemd override before staging on the affected Main
  implementation. Keep EFI mounts in a private namespace during shutdown,
  preserve custom overrides, and let the guard expire automatically at reboot.
  Validate with 109 Python tests, namespace probes, frontend checks, and a real
  Main 610-to-615 Decky update and reboot on a 5 GiB read-only root. Record the
  hardware scope and remaining unrelated preparation warnings.
- migrate legacy builds and collect only unpinned driver caches (60plus)

## 🔧 Chores

- add the 0.4.0 what's new entry (moi952)
- reset version to 0.3.0 for the 0.4.0 release (moi952)
- use upstream decky-ui-kit 0.6.1 without local patch (60plus)
- prepare SteamOS adaptation for upstream (60plus)
- v0.4.0-standalone.9 (60plus)

## 📦 Other

- Merge pull request #2 from 60plus/pr/steamos-ab-upstream (moi952)
  Support SteamOS A/B driver updates without requiring an 8 GiB root
- Restore plugin self-updates and retain upstream README structure (60plus)
- Adapt plugin to standalone SteamOS A/B driver updates (60plus)

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.3.0
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## ✨ Features

- build NVIDIA driver versions Arch hasn't packaged yet (moi952)
  Adds a separate build path (bin/steamos-nvidia-build.sh +
  custom_build.py) that clones Arch's packaging repos, bumps pkgver,
  and builds under a throwaway user in the existing overlay chroot.
  Builds are cached under /home/.steamos-nvidia-custom-builds, and
  pin_pkg checks that cache before hitting the network.
  The version dropdown merges Arch, cached, and not-yet-built
  versions into one sorted list, checks buildability before enabling
  Install, and chains build -> install on a single click.
- adopt decky-plugin-toolkit for settings & self-update (moi952)
  Replace the plugin's own update-check code with the shared
  decky-plugin-toolkit, and add a Settings view (gear button) for it,
  like decky-quick-tab already does. Driver settings stay on the main
  panel. Also fixes the What's New banner width and bumps to 0.3.0.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- use pnpm version --message and --no-git-checks (moi952)
  pnpm's version command no longer accepts the -m shorthand, and -- -m
  doesn't work either (pnpm forwards the literal -- to npm, which then
  rejects it as an extra positional argument). --message is the long
  form that works.
  --no-git-checks skips pnpm's own working-tree-clean check, which was
  tripping on the changelog step's untracked artifact/ dir before this
  step ran. Same fix already used in decky-proton-launch and
  decky-quick-tab.

## 📦 Other

- Add github download and stars indicators (moi952)
- Add Ko-fi username to FUNDING.yml (moi952)
  Added Ko-fi username for funding support.

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.2.2
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- harden curl retries and warn on undersized rootfs before install (moi952)
  set -e was silently killing the curl retry loops on any transient
  failure. Also warn upfront if rootfs looks under 8GiB, and drop the
  inaccurate "10-20 min" build estimate.

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.2.1
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- include bin/ in packaged plugin zip and harden version list fallback (moi952)
  - release.yml and build.yml never copied bin/steamos-nvidia-update.sh
    into the packaged zip, so installing from a GitHub release (including
    via the new self-update button) left the script missing entirely —
    breaking both the version dropdown and driver installs.
  - index.tsx now derives the collapsed version list from the detailed
    one whenever list_driver_versions() comes back empty, so a single
    failing/missing script can't fully blank the picker again.

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.2.0
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## ✨ Features

- add self-update system and fix channel-scoped update detection (moi952)
  - Fix: the driver update badge/toast always compared against Arch's
    plain stable repo, ignoring the user's chosen NVIDIA channel
    (recommended/NFB/beta). Now scoped via computeChannelLatest.
  - Add a top banner and a collapsible panel section that check GitHub
    releases for a newer plugin build and install it in one click via
    Decky Loader's own installer (utilities/install_plugin), the same
    mechanism the Decky plugin store itself uses.

Fix: remove a hardcoded home-LAN IP address that leaked into the Ollama translate-URL fallback (main.py, bin/capture_dynamic.py, scripts/run_translate.sh), and genericize a dev-server hostname mentioned in a few comments.

No functional/behavioral changes for cloud engine users;

Users of Ollama should create a file named translate_url.txt in the plugin data directory with the server URL as http://host:port/translate, or set the PLAYTRANSLATE_TRANSLATE_URL environment variable before launching Steam. If neither is set, http://127.0.0.1:8787/translate is used by default.
See d91c9f6.

neatsorg/livetranslate-decky.name: Release v0.1.0
neatsorg/livetranslate-decky.body:
## LiveTranslator-kun v0.1.0(日本語)

Gamescope/PipeWire経由で画面をキャプチャし、OCRで文字を認識して、翻訳結果をリアルタイムでオーバーレイ表示するDecky Loaderプラグインです。Steam Deckでのゲーム字幕翻訳を主な用途として作られています。

### 機能

- 文章の移動・スクロールにも追随するリアルタイム自動翻訳
- 特定の字幕エリアに限定した矩形キャプチャモード
- 一時停止中に任意の箇所だけを翻訳する画面タップ翻訳
- 既定はオンデバイスOCR(Chrome Screen AI)、TesseractOCRはレガシーのフォールバックとして利用可能
- 複数の翻訳エンジンに対応: Ollama(ローカル)、Gemini AI、Google翻訳、Google Cloud Translate、DeepL
- ゲームパッド・キーボード・Steam Deck本体に割り当て可能なキーバインド

インストール・セットアップ・使い方は[README](../../blob/main/README.ja.md)をご覧ください。

### 既知の問題

非Deck環境での注意点(入力デバイスの権限、gamescopeのネスト実行、オーバーレイのフォーカスに関する不具合)は[非Deck Linux環境での利用](../../blob/main/README.ja.md#非deck-linux環境での利用)を参照してください。

---

## LiveTranslator-kun v0.1.0

A Decky Loader plugin that captures the screen through Gamescope/PipeWire,recognizes text with OCR, and overlays a live translation - built for gamesubtitles on Steam Deck.

### Features

- Real-time auto-translation that tracks moving/scrolling text
- Region capture mode for a single fixed subtitle area
- Screen-tap translation for one-off lines while paused
- On-device OCR (Chrome Screen AI) by default, TesseractOCR available as a legacy fallback
- Multiple translation engines: Ollama (local), Gemini AI, Google Translate, Google Cloud Translate, DeepL
- Configurable keybindings (gamepad, keyboard, or Steam Deck's own controls)

See the [README](../../blob/main/README.md) for installation, setup, and
usage instructions.

### Known issues

See [Running on a non-Deck Linux host](../../blob/main/README.md#running-on-a-non-deck-linux-host) for caveats on non-Deck setups (input permissions, nested gamescope, an overlay-focus bug).

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.1-beta.3 — Free DLC and the base game
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Free DLC now tells you when it needs the base game.** Spotted on *Dying Light: The Beast — Discharge Weapon Pack* (€4.99, free right now): Steam only hands a free DLC to owners of the game it belongs to.

## What's new
- 🧩 FSG reads the game a DLC belongs to and checks whether it is in your library. If it isn't, the card says **"Needs <game> in your library"**, the add button is disabled, and a second button opens the base game on Steam.
- 🤖 Auto-add skips those DLCs instead of retrying them and failing.
- 💬 If you claim one anyway, the message explains it: *this DLC is free, but Steam only gives it to owners of <game>*.

## Also in this 0.4.1 line
- 🟢🔴 Steam session light at the top of the list, with a button to open the Steam Store when it is red (beta.2).
- 🔁 A redirect from Steam is no longer reported as a failure; clearer messages and a better log line when a claim really fails (beta.1).

## How to update
Options → **Beta versions** on, then **Check for updates** → **Update**, at the bottom of the panel.
From a stable version without the beta option: Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → **Developer mode**, then ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL** with the link below.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.1-beta.2 — Steam session light
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**You can now see, at a glance, whether FSG can talk to your Steam account.**

## What's new
- 🟢🔴 **Session light** at the top of the free games list: green when FSG finds your Steam session in Steam's own browser, red when it doesn't, grey before the first check. It is refreshed every time you open the panel.
- 🛒 **"Open the Steam Store" button** appears when the light is red, so you can sign in right where FSG reads the session, then come back and claim.

## Also in this 0.4.1 line (from beta.1)
- 🔁 A redirect from Steam is no longer reported as a failure: FSG always checks your licence list afterwards, and says **Added to your library** whenever the game landed there.
- 💬 Clearer messages when a claim really fails (sign-in needed, redirect, HTTP error, not confirmed yet), each with what to do next, and the HTTP status plus redirect target written to `~/homebrew/logs/FSG`.

## How to update
Options → **Beta versions** on, then **Check for updates** → **Update**, at the bottom of the panel.
From a stable version without the beta option: Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → **Developer mode**, then ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL** with the link below.

**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.1-beta.1 — A redirect is no longer a failure
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Fixes the "Steam refused the request (HTTP 302)" message** reported on r/deckyloader.

## What changed
- 🔁 **A redirect is not a failure.** Steam often answers the claim request with a redirect instead of a body, and a redirect says nothing about the result. FSG now always checks your licence list afterwards — if the game landed in your library, you get **Added to your library**, whatever HTTP status came back.
- 💬 **Clearer messages** when the claim really fails, each with what to do next:
  - *Steam sent the request to its login page* → open the Steam Store on the console and make sure you are signed in.
  - *Steam answered with a redirect / HTTP xxx and the game is still missing* → open the Store once and try again, or claim the game from its Steam page.
  - *Steam took the request but the game is not in your library yet* → wait a few seconds and refresh.
- 🧾 **Better log line**: the HTTP status and the redirect target are written to `~/homebrew/logs/FSG`, so a failure can be diagnosed.

## How to update
Options → **Beta versions** on, then **Check for updates** → **Update**, at the bottom of the panel.
From a stable version without the beta option, install by URL: Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → **Developer mode**, then ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL** with the link below.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.0 — Statistics, stick navigation, visible updates
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Statistics, smoother stick navigation and easier-to-spot updates.** Everything tested through 11 betas on a Legion Go 2, where FSG has already added two 100%-off games on its own.

## What's new
- 📊 **Statistics view**: press **See the statistics** to open a dedicated view inside the panel, with a way back (B button works too).
  - **Value claimed**: the normal price of every game FSG added for you, in total and game by game.
  - **Your Steam library**: number of items and estimated value (priced items vs. items at €0: demos, free-to-play…).
  - Computed **only** when you press **Recalculate the statistics**: nothing runs in the background on your console.
- 🔄 **Updates are easier to spot**: the update button now sits under **Check for updates**, at the bottom of the panel, and every check shows a notification (up to date / update found / GitHub unreachable).
- 🗂️ **Clearer panel order**: free games to keep, Refresh, Options, upcoming promos, statistics, updates.

## Fixes
- 🕹️ **Stick navigation**: moving up with the stick now scrolls the panel all the way to the top (the logo and game cards are focusable, and the panel follows Steam's gamepad focus).
- ↩️ After an update, the panel closes and reloads on the new version instead of staying on the old code.

## How to update

### From v0.2.0 or later (built-in updates)
1. Open FSG in the Decky menu and press **Check for updates** (bottom of the panel).
2. Press **Update to 0.4.0** (in v0.2.0 to v0.3.1, it shows up in the **Update available** section at the top of the panel).
3. Decky shows its confirmation window, checks the zip's checksum and reloads the plugin.

Beta users get this version too.

### From v0.1.0 (no built-in updates): reinstall by hand, once
v0.1.0 can't update itself. If your panel has no **Check for updates** button, install v0.4.0 over it:
1. Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Decky → ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL**, paste this link and confirm:
   ```
   https://github.com/koua29/decky-fsg/releases/latest/download/FSG.zip
   ```
   Or download `FSG.zip` below and use **Install plugin from ZIP file**.
3. From then on, new versions show up right in the panel.

Settings and history are kept either way.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — a SteamOS console with Decky Loader. Install by URL or from the ZIP file (developer mode).

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.0-beta.11 — Stick scrolling (real cause)
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**The right cause, this time.** Steam moves a *virtual* focus: the target item never receives a browser focus event.

## Fixes
- 🕹️ The scrolling added in beta 9 never started, because it was hooked to the browser's `focus` event — which Steam does not fire when navigating with a controller. It is now hooked to **`onGamepadFocus`**, the event actually fired. The logo, game cards and statistics lines therefore bring the panel to them.

## How to update
From beta 10, with the **Beta versions** option on: *Updates* section, at the bottom of the panel.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.3.0
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
# GFG Extreme 3.3.0

**GFG Extreme 3.3.0 combines the stable GFG Extreme 3.2.2 with GSF Kedavra 1.5.0.**

## What improved

- **Clearer detail during fast, reliably reconstructed motion.** Kedavra now reduces its existing motion blur only where source samples and neighbouring motion vectors agree.
- **Conservative reconstruction elsewhere.** Uncertain motion and conflicting image regions retain the previous handling.
- **No extra GPU passes or image buffers.** The change reuses existing texture samples in the reconstruction shader.
- **The familiar 3.2.2 application remains.** This release preserves its interface, settings, generation modes, per-game profiles, Autopilot/Governor controls, graphics filters, HUD, diagnostics and engine recovery mechanisms.

There is no new collection of quality sliders to configure. The earlier experimental colour-range clamp is not included.

## Validation and measured results

In a reproducible synthetic fast-pan test at 1280×800, the new engine improved generated-frame PSNR by **3.68–4.20 dB** and reduced mean absolute RGB error by approximately **80%**. These are software Vulkan measurements for that test scene, not a promise of the same improvement in every game.

The engine passed its normal and low-source-FPS software suites. GFG CI passed backend tests, control-system simulations, frontend build/smoke checks, the Gamescope build and runtime library checks. The published installer was also checked for ZIP integrity and a matching SHA256 checksum.

## Known limitations

Block-shaped artifacts during complex camera turns below 30 source FPS remain an open limitation. This release's main demonstrated improvement is fast-motion sharpness, rather than a general solution to ghosting, occlusion or low-FPS artifacts.

This release does not claim hardware validation of Steam Deck GPU performance, power use, physical display pacing or input-to-photon latency. Software test results must not be interpreted as device measurements.

## Installation and rollback

1. Download `GFG-Extreme-v3_3_0.zip`; use `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to verify the download.
2. Install it through **Decky Loader → Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP**.
3. Open GFG Setup, update/install the engine and reboot when prompted.
4. Confirm that Setup reports the installed runtime matching the plugin before testing.

Retain the official 3.2.2 installer and a settings backup. To return to 3.2.2, restore the stock engine through Setup and reboot, then install the 3.2.2 plugin and its engine.

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.2.2 - Stable
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
# GFG Extreme 3.2.2

A simpler Dash and a lighter plugin, on the same GSF Kedavra engine as 3.2.1. Press **Update
engine** when the panel asks and reboot.

## 90 FPS everywhere in SteamOS Gaming Mode

GSF Kedavra runs at the Gamescope presentation layer, after application rendering or video decoding. No game-engine hooks, emulator modifications or streaming-server integration are required. The same frame-generation path covers native Steam/Proton games, emulators (shadPS4, RPCS3, PCSX2, Dolphin, Cemu, PPSSPP, DuckStation and others), and remote-play clients (Xbox Remote Play / Greenlight, PlayStation Remote Play / Chiaki, Moonlight) launched through **SteamOS Gaming Mode**.

On the Steam Deck OLED 90 Hz display, a stable 30 FPS source can reach up to **90 FPS output** at ×3: one original frame and two motion-reconstructed frames per source interval. This increases presentation cadence, not the source game's native simulation rate; streaming and interpolation latency still apply.

## Dash
- The **Mode** tiles switch generation too: tap a mode to play with it, tap the selected mode
  again to turn frame generation off (no mode is highlighted while it is off). Tap any mode to
  turn it back on.
- The separate Frame generation card is gone; the mode picks the multiplier.

## Lighter plugin
GFG's own loop runs once a second next to the game. It now does less work each second:

| Per second, in a game | 3.2.1 → 3.2.2 |
|---|---|
| Power sensor reads (TDP caps, APU draw) | 17 → 6 |
| Battery and charger scans | 1 → 0.5 |
| Telemetry file writes | 1 → 1/30 |
| hwmon folder scans | 1 → 1/60 |
| Engine mount check while the panel is open | every 5 s → once per boot |

Every feature works as before: the plugin's 39 control scenarios (Autopilot, Governor, Power
Split, GPU clock, dock, battery, menus) give identical results.

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.2.1
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
# GFG Extreme 3.2.1

Cleaner camera turns, steadier thin lines, smoother recovery after a game hitch, a simpler Dash
and a system profile for games. **Update engine** in Setup and reboot after installing.

## Picture
- **Fast camera turns.** The motion search also checks where each block's content comes from
  and where it goes, so walls, pillars and sky follow the camera as one surface.
- **Frame edges.** Blocks at the edge of the frame keep the motion of the image next to them on
  fast turns.
- **Thin straight lines.** Fences, wires, window frames and crosshair-like detail stay steady
  during slow pans.
- **Scene cuts.** A real cut shows the last real frame until the new scene arrives; fast turns
  and slow pans stay generated.
- **HUD.** HUD rows at the screen edges stay in place.

Engine test scenes (PSNR against the true frame, higher is better; line flicker, lower is better):

| Scene | 3.2.0 → 3.2.1 |
|---|---|
| Camera turn, 32 px per frame | 32.5 → 33.1 dB |
| Camera turn, 64 px per frame | 27.1 → 28.1 dB |
| Camera turn, 96 px per frame | 23.9 → 24.8 dB |
| Dark grainy turn | 35.3 → 35.7 dB |
| Fast pan | +2.0 … 2.6 dB |
| Thin lines, slow pan ×3 | 21.0 → 28.4 dB, flicker 34.8 → 12.7 |
| Thin lines, slow pan ×2 | 19.3 → 27.2 dB, flicker 38.6 → 14.1 |

## Frame delivery
- After a late game frame the engine catches up once and settles, without alternating faster and
  slower refreshes.
- The base FPS cap releases exactly one game frame per slot.

Scheduler simulator, tracking error P95:

| Case | 3.2.0 → 3.2.1 |
|---|---|
| Game hitch of 155 ms | 7.4 → 1.2 ms |
| Game hitch of 300 ms | 7.1 → 0.5 ms |
| ×3, game under its cap | 4.3 → 3.6 ms |
| ×3, game holding its cap | 1.0 → 0.6 ms |

Average latency changes by 0–3 ms; the extra analysis costs well under 0.1 ms per game frame.

## Dash
The Frame generation card has a single **Off** button. The mode (Autopilot, Battery, Balanced,
Quality) chooses the multiplier; tap Off to play a game without generation, tap it again to
bring generation back.

## System profile
Installed with the engine and removed with it: runtime kernel settings for memory (zram swap,
huge pages, earlier reclaim), the CPU scheduler and storage. Every value is saved first and
written back on **Remove**. **Setup → Save report to Desktop** shows how many were applied.

cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful.name: Colorful 1.0.0
cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful.body:
This is the first release of Colorful, a Decky plugin that gives each of your TabMaster console tabs a colored panel with the console's artwork, in the style of the COLORFUL theme by Viking.

When a game is selected, the panel shows its playtime, when you last played it, your latest save, and your RetroAchievements progress for emulated games or your Steam achievements for native ones. With nothing selected, it shows the tab's total playtime and your three most played games.

To install it, open the Decky settings, turn on Developer mode, then use **Install Plugin from URL** with this address:

```
https://github.com/cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful/releases/latest/download/Colorful.zip
```

You need EmuDeck and TabMaster set up first. The README explains every step.

raindropx/decky-llm-translator.name: Decky LLM Translator v0.3.0
raindropx/decky-llm-translator.body:
## What's new

- Added 18 plugin-interface languages: Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Vietnamese, Filipino, Malay, North Korean, French, German, Polish, Indonesian, Min Nan, Italian, Thai, Finnish, toki pona, and Esperanto.
- Added Steam/system-language following for recognized locales, while keeping every language manually selectable when Steam does not expose it as a preferred language.
- Added English fallback for missing or newly introduced translation strings so incomplete locale updates never leave blank UI text.
- Reviewed and refined the Japanese, Korean, Thai, Russian, French, German, Min Nan, and toki pona translations.
- Improved settings persistence, custom-language handling, dependency download verification, OCR worker timeout recovery, and Steam screenshot path handling.
- Modernized the release build and packaging pipeline.

## Validation

- 26 frontend tests passed.
- 47 Python tests passed; 1 environment-dependent test skipped.
- TypeScript check and production build passed.
- Release ZIP manifest and required-file validation passed.
- Plugin ZIP SHA-256: `fd665e0df0bbab4594625e7af60bd43288f806acdb789e86cdd35edd9b1f1668`.
- Dependency archive SHA-256: `bc8c2a9d81e200c7056d131c581279a78b380b6876f5afdf3eee85a19efa27e5` (matches `package.json`).

## Installation note

The plugin ZIP uses the `remote_binary` entry in `package.json` to download the matching OCR/runtime dependency archive during installation, so it is not a fully offline installer.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Raindropx/Decky-LLM-Translator/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0

woovs-cg/caretcontrol.name: Caret Control 0.7.0
woovs-cg/caretcontrol.body:
Added support for external controllers through Linux evdev.

- Supports shoulder buttons and four-direction right-stick input.
- Tested with 8BitDo Ultimate 2.4G in Bluetooth D-input and USB XInput modes.
- Preserves built-in Steam Deck controls, hold-to-repeat, hot-plugging, and keyboard navigation suppression.

woovs-cg/caretcontrol.name: Caret Control v0.6.0
woovs-cg/caretcontrol.body:
Move the text caret on Steam Deck without leaving the on-screen keyboard.

### Features

- Move left and right with **L1** and **R1**.
- Move in all four directions with the **right stick**.
- Hold a bumper or the stick to repeat movement.
- Activates only while Steam's on-screen keyboard and its text target are active.
- Uses Steam's built-in keyboard arrow actions for reliable Game Mode support.
- Suppresses conflicting Gamepad UI navigation while caret controls are active.

### Installation

Install `CaretControl-0.6.0.zip` through Decky Loader's developer menu.

### Known limitation

In Firefox's address bar in Desktop Mode, Steam's native on-screen keyboard input path may display control characters as squares. Firefox in Game Mode is unaffected.

- Add **TF card game library** mode alongside system installation.
- Pair with [Smart TF Card Allocator](https://github.com/mydanyi/smart-tf-allocator) to divide one card between Android app storage and a Linux game library.
- Format only the Linux reserve partition as ext4 while preserving Android storage. Existing Armada libraries can be mounted and reconnected to Steam.
- Support recovery after interrupted setup and retrying game-library registration.
- Fix horizontal shifts during controller navigation and add companion-app download links to both READMEs.

Download **armada-installer-0.2.0.zip** below for Decky Loader.

**Back up first:** allocation in the Android app erases the whole card; formatting in the Linux plugin erases only the confirmed Linux reserve partition.

## 简体中文

- 新增 **TF卡游戏库** 模式，与系统安装入口并列。
- 配合[智能TF卡分配器](https://github.com/mydanyi/smart-tf-allocator)，让一张卡分别用于 Android 应用存储和 Linux 游戏库。
- 仅将 Linux 保留分区格式化为 ext4，保留 Android 存储；已有 Armada 游戏库可挂载并重新接入 Steam。
- 支持中断后的继续设置，以及重试游戏库接入。
- 修复手柄导航时界面横向偏移，并在中英文主页补充安卓配套工具下载入口。

下载下方 **armada-installer-0.2.0.zip**，通过 Decky Loader 安装。

**请先备份：** 安卓应用重新分配会清空整张卡；Linux 插件格式化仅清空已确认的 Linux 保留分区。

mydanyi/armada-installer.name: Armada Installer v0.1.0
mydanyi/armada-installer.body:
# Armada Installer v0.1.0

## English

The first stable release of Armada Installer, a Decky plugin for [ArmadaOS](https://github.com/armada-os/armada).

- Install Armada onto the internal storage from the SD-card installer environment.
- Works before Steam sign-in; no Steam account or game library is required.
- Supports fresh and occupied layouts with an explicit review and confirmation step.
- Supports English and Simplified Chinese interfaces, including controller navigation.
- Writes to the selected disk only after the user confirms the destructive operation.

Download the complete [`armada-installer-0.1.0.zip`](https://github.com/mydanyi/armada-installer/releases/download/v0.1.0/armada-installer-0.1.0.zip) and install it through Decky's developer settings. Verify the download with [`SHA256SUMS.txt`](https://github.com/mydanyi/armada-installer/releases/download/v0.1.0/SHA256SUMS.txt).

This plugin is for ArmadaOS. See the [ArmadaOS project](https://github.com/armada-os/armada) for system images, device support and system documentation.

## 简体中文

Armada Installer 首个正式发布版，面向 [ArmadaOS](https://github.com/armada-os/armada) 的 Decky 安装插件。

- 从 SD 卡安装环境把 Armada 安装到内部存储。
- Steam 登录前即可使用，不需要 Steam 账号或游戏库。
- 支持全新布局和已有布局，并提供明确的方案查看与确认步骤。
- 支持英文和简体中文界面，以及手柄操作。
- 只有用户确认清除操作后，才会写入选定的磁盘。

请下载完整的 [`armada-installer-0.1.0.zip`](https://github.com/mydanyi/armada-installer/releases/download/v0.1.0/armada-installer-0.1.0.zip)，通过 Decky 的开发者设置安装，并使用 [`SHA256SUMS.txt`](https://github.com/mydanyi/armada-installer/releases/download/v0.1.0/SHA256SUMS.txt) 校验文件。

此插件仅用于 ArmadaOS。系统镜像、设备支持和系统文档请参考 [ArmadaOS 主项目](https://github.com/armada-os/armada)。

## License / 许可证

danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games.name: v1.7.13
danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games.body:
**Steam shortcuts list**

- **Check saved games** is now **Load Steam Shortcuts**, and says what it does
  before you press it: it shows the shortcuts currently in Steam, and only
  updates when the Steam client restarts.
- The list is sorted alphabetically. It used to arrive in whatever order Steam
  had written `shortcuts.vdf`, which is no order at all to look through.
- Thirty entries was a hard cut-off, with the rest simply unreachable. The list
  now opens at twenty and a **Show 20 more** row extends it, so nothing is out
  of reach and the panel still opens short. Pressing it moves the D-pad onto
  the first row it revealed, rather than dropping the selection twenty rows
  down the panel with the row that was pressed.
- A **Search** field appears once there are twelve or more shortcuts, matching
  on the name and the path — the fastest way to answer "is my game in here?"
  without scrolling past a hundred rows.
- The **Show the list** toggle no longer sits flush against the button above it
  or the first entry below it.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games/compare/v1.7.10...v1.7.13

danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games.name: v1.7.10
danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games.body:
**Browse tabs**

- The selected tab now wears the inverted white surface permanently, and gamepad
  focus and hover use the accent colour instead. Selection and focus were
  previously the same paint, so a focused tab and a selected one were
  indistinguishable.
- The bar marking the selected tab runs the full width of the button rather than
  60% of it.

**Options**

- Removed the **Paste key** button. The on-screen keyboard's own paste key now
  lands in the field correctly, so the button had nothing left to do. Every
  fallback route behind it went with it — the clipboard API, `execCommand`, and
  the backend's `wl-paste`/`xclip`/`xsel` read, which had been shelling out as
  root.
- Reworded the restart and artwork settings, and said *shortcuts* where the
  thing being added is as often an application as a game.
- Spacing and indentation: descriptions are indented under the control they
  belong to, the **SteamGridDB API key** field is set off from the toggle above
  it, and **Rescan applications** no longer sits flush against the row above it.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-add-non-steam-games/compare/v1.7.9...v1.7.10

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 1.2.0
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
# Sharp Filter Selector 1.2.0

[Español](#español) · [English](#english)

## Español

### Novedades

- **SGSR en SteamOS:** Nitidez del QAM pasa de FSR `2` a SGSR `5` cuando el Gamescope activo es compatible. El puente comprueba cada ~750 ms más la respuesta X11; no modifica Gamescope de forma atómica.
- **Detección corregida:** se resuelve el bloqueo de `/proc/PID/exe` mediante la ruta absoluta observada y validada del proceso, sin elegir otro ejecutable del PATH ni conceder root al plugin.
- **QAM y controles:** conserva el modo de escalado elegido en SteamOS moderno; los overrides NIS/FSR son excluyentes y la interfaz muestra el estado SGSR.
- **Compatibilidad conservada:** los 12 métodos Ubuntu/UGM, la ruta SteamOS antigua, la lógica HDR y la nitidez 0–5 siguen intactos.

Para usar SGSR, deja **Use NIS** y **Use FSR** apagados y selecciona **Nitidez** en el QAM de Steam. Con entrada HDR, Gamescope conserva su fallback FSR; una salida HDR con juego SDR no oculta por sí sola FSR.

### Instalación

Descarga el ZIP y su archivo `.sha256` en la misma carpeta:

```bash
sha256sum -c sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip.sha256
unzip sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip
cd sharp-filter-selector
./install.sh
```

Recarga el plugin desde Decky o reinicia Steam/Gaming para cargarlo. Se conservan tus selecciones. El ZIP es para instalar; las fuentes completas y las pruebas están en el repositorio.

### Validación y organización

- **48 pruebas aprobadas:** 41 Python y 7 frontend, incluida una matriz de 90 casos de filtro/escalado/override. Tipos, build e instalador también comprobados.
- El mantenedor confirmó funcionamiento en SteamOS 3.9.5 / Gamescope 3.16.30.1 el 24-10-2026. No se atribuye una captura GPU independiente ni una matriz física HDR completa.
- Repositorio reorganizado: README breves en ambos idiomas, dos guías técnicas y documentación centrada en el plugin. ZIP simplificado, sin expedientes de tienda ni documentos administrativos.
- **Misma versión y runtime:** esta limpieza cambia documentación y empaquetado, no el plugin validado. El tag original `v1.2.0` permanece intacto; el paquete documental se genera desde el [commit de limpieza](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/tree/f20d02fe91bcd1abbda1042b26df67110ef2209c).

[Guía en español](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/README_ES.md) · [Compatibilidad y comparación con 1.1.0](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md#español) · [Desarrollo](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#español)

## English

### Changes

- **SGSR on SteamOS:** QAM Sharp is promoted from FSR `2` to SGSR `5` when the active Gamescope supports it. Checks run every ~750 ms plus X11 response time; this is not an atomic Gamescope modification.
- **Detection fixed:** restricted `/proc/PID/exe` access is handled using the process's validated observed absolute executable, without substituting PATH or granting root to the plugin.
- **QAM and controls:** preserve the selected scaler on modern SteamOS; NIS/FSR overrides are exclusive and the UI shows SGSR status.
- **Compatibility preserved:** twelve Ubuntu/UGM methods, legacy SteamOS, application-HDR policy and 0–5 sharpening remain unchanged.

To use SGSR, leave **Use NIS** and **Use FSR** off and choose **Sharp** in Steam's QAM. HDR input retains Gamescope's FSR fallback; HDR output with an SDR game does not itself hide FSR.

### Installation

Download the ZIP and `.sha256` file into the same directory:

```bash
sha256sum -c sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip.sha256
unzip sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip
cd sharp-filter-selector
./install.sh
```

Reload the plugin through Decky or restart Steam/Gaming Mode to load it. Existing selections are retained. The ZIP is for installation; complete sources and tests remain in the repository.

### Validation and organization

- **48 tests passed:** 41 Python and 7 frontend tests, including 90 filter/scaler/override cases. Types, build and installer checks also pass.
- The maintainer confirmed operation on SteamOS 3.9.5 / Gamescope 3.16.30.1 on 2026-10-24. This is not an independent GPU trace or a complete physical HDR matrix.
- Repository reorganized: concise English/Spanish READMEs, two technical guides and plugin-focused documentation. The ZIP is simplified, without store-submission or administrative documents.
- **Same version and runtime:** this cleanup changes documentation/packaging, not the validated plugin. The original `v1.2.0` tag remains unchanged; the documentation package is generated from the [cleanup commit](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/tree/f20d02fe91bcd1abbda1042b26df67110ef2209c).

[English guide](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/README.md) · [Compatibility and 1.1.0 comparison](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [Development](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 1.1.0
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
## Sharp Filter Selector 1.1.0

This release fixes HDR-aware control visibility without changing Gamescope's filter, scaler or sharpening behavior.

### What changed

- **Display HDR no longer hides FSR.** An SDR game on an HDR output keeps both explicit FSR and NIS controls available.
- FSR visibility now follows fresh, unambiguous application feedback from `GAMESCOPE_COLOR_APP_WANTS_HDR_FEEDBACK`.
- Missing, invalid or conflicting application feedback fails open: both controls remain available on SGSR-capable Gamescope builds.
- A failed frontend refresh clears stale HDR gating so a previous HDR game cannot hide FSR for the next game.
- NIS availability, SGSR/FSR/NIS selectors, the 0–5 sharpening mapping and QAM scaling ownership are unchanged.

### Validation

- Physical Ubuntu 26.04 Gaming Mode test with Gamescope 3.16.30, NVIDIA RTX 2060, 4K HDR output and QAM transitions.
- Confirmed: SDR application input on an HDR output retains FSR and NIS; application HDR feedback—not display HDR mode—controls FSR visibility.
- Automated coverage for SDR, HDR, missing, invalid and conflicting feedback, stale-state transitions, both sharpening backends and invalid sharpness rejection.
- TypeScript type-check, Rollup build, Python syntax and **5/5 tests** passed.

### Installation

Download `sharp-filter-selector-v1.1.0.zip`, extract it and run:

```bash
cd sharp-filter-selector
./install.sh
```

The accompanying `.sha256` file verifies the archive. The plugin does not install or patch Gamescope.

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 1.0.0
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
## Sharp Filter Selector 1.0.0

This release packages the runtime validated on Ubuntu 26.04 Gaming Mode with
Gamescope 3.16.30, NVIDIA RTX 2060, multi-Xwayland, 4K and VRR.

### Highlights

- Native SGSR detection from the Gamescope process that owns the active session.
- Explicit FSR and NIS overrides with shared 0–5 sharpening.
- Correct distinction between SDR SGSR, HDR-input FSR fallback and HDR output.
- QAM scaler/filter synchronization across Gamescope Xwayland roots.
- QAM scaling modes remain owned by Steam; filter selection no longer overwrites them.
- Portable installer and uninstaller included in the ZIP.

### Installation

1. Download and extract `sharp-filter-selector-v1.0.0.zip`.
2. Enter the extracted `sharp-filter-selector` directory.
3. Run `./install.sh`.
4. Reload Decky Loader or restart Steam/Gaming Mode.

The default destination is `~/homebrew/plugins/sharp-filter-selector/`.

### Integrity

```text
7869023cec0c393874f00a84ea9e0ca1dafe5d41a44d9331d04789aa73a37123  sharp-filter-selector-v1.0.0.zip
```

The SteamOS compatibility path is retained, but this 1.0.0 release's final
acceptance was performed on the Ubuntu/Gamescope environment described above.

See `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` and `README_ES.md` for full details.

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 0.3.4
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
## Sharp Filter Selector 0.3.4

Validated release for Ubuntu and SteamOS with the modern Decky Loader API.

### Highlights

- NIS switching is confirmed working on both **Ubuntu** and **SteamOS / Steam Deck**.
- SteamOS now discovers and targets Gamescope's multiple Xwayland roots instead of assuming a single display.
- SteamOS performs an explicit **LINEAR → NIS** transition before applying the final NIS state.
- Ubuntu/Linux keeps its isolated, validated compatibility path based on `GAMESCOPE_SHARP_FILTER`.
- Frontend migrated to Decky's supported public packages: `@decky/api`, `@decky/ui` and `@decky/rollup`.
- Keeps the plugin's own **0–5 NIS sharpness slider**, mapped to Gamescope's full sharpening range.
- Adds Xwayland server/filter diagnostics and FSR feedback verification.
- Source frontend is now TypeScript/React with Rollup.

### Packaging

The release keeps the exact runtime frontend and backend validated by the maintainer. Build checks compile the modern TypeScript frontend separately without replacing the tested runtime in the release archive.

The plugin does **not** replace or patch Gamescope.

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 0.3.1
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
## Sharp Filter Selector 0.3.1

SteamOS/Game Mode compatibility test release.

### Fixes

- Keeps NIS enforced if Steam/QAM re-applies FSR after the plugin changes the scaler.
- Applies both modern and legacy Gamescope selectors plus AUTO scaler state.
- Uses Gamescope's FSR feedback property to detect an active FSR override.
- Adds in-plugin verification so the Quick Access Menu reports whether NIS was actually confirmed.
- Keeps the existing 0-5 sharpness control unchanged.

### Test request

On Steam Deck / SteamOS, enable scaling below native resolution, turn on **Use NIS**, and watch both MangoHud and the status line in Sharp Filter Selector.

The desired result is:
- MangoHud reports NIS.
- The plugin reports **NIS verified active**.

If SteamOS still wins the filter state, the plugin should instead report that SteamOS is still forcing FSR while automatic retry remains active.

Nothing else changed — same backend, same host API, same pairing. If you're already on

nico8324/couchlink.name: v0.4.0 — StreamLink is now CouchLink
nico8324/couchlink.body:
**StreamLink is now CouchLink.** The old name clashed with the unrelated
[streamlink](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink) project, and the plugin's Python package
(`py_modules/streamlink`) shadowed that project's import name.

### Upgrading — read this

Decky treats this as a **new plugin**, not an update:

1. Remove **StreamLink** on *both* devices (Decky → gear → StreamLink → uninstall).
2. Install [`CouchLink.zip`](https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink/releases/latest/download/CouchLink.zip) on both.
3. **Pair again** from the Deck. An old host and a new client can't discover each other — the `/ping`
   identity string changed with the name.

### Also in this release

* The update check finally works. Every release up to 0.3.0 shipped with the feed URL pointing at a
  placeholder repo, so the plugin never saw a new version.
* Store listing image is the project's own rather than the plugin template's banner.
* `LICENSE` keeps the plugin template's original copyright, as the Decky store requires.

Nothing else changed: same wake/sleep/auto-sleep behaviour, same host API, same
[known limitations](https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink#known-limitations-read-this) (S5 wake still
doesn't work on the Steam Machine — use Sleep).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

nico8324/couchlink.name: v0.3.0 — approve-on-host pairing, away mode, stream stats
nico8324/couchlink.body:
Install on **both** devices: Decky → gear → General → Developer mode → Developer → **Install Plugin from Zip** → `StreamLink.zip`.
Then pair once from the Deck (*Pair host…* → *Find hosts on this network* → **Allow** on the host's screen).

### New

* **Approve-on-host pairing** — discover the host, tap it, press **Allow** on the host's own screen. No typing a token (manual entry kept as a fallback).
* **"Leaving home" mode** — keep the host awake for streaming over the internet, and restore your sleep settings when you're back.
* **Stream session stats** — fps, bitrate, ping and slow stages parsed from Steam's `SessionStats`, shown on both panels.
* **Update check** against a configurable JSON feed; the Deck warns when host and Deck versions differ.

### Changed / fixed

* The host is matched in Steam's device list by its hostname (learned at pairing) instead of a fixed name.
* The client tolerates non-JSON replies from the host API.

### Known limitations

Wake from a full power-off (S5) does **not** work on the Steam Machine — a firmware limitation
([SteamOS#2735](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/SteamOS/issues/2735)). Use **Sleep**. Wake also only works on your
own LAN; use *Leaving home* before you go out. Details in the [README](https://github.com/Nico8324/StreamLink#known-limitations-read-this).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Nico8324/StreamLink/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0

steve133t/decky-wake-on-controller.name: v1.0.24
steve133t/decky-wake-on-controller.body:
**Wake your Steam Deck from sleep by pressing the home button on any Bluetooth controller** — Xbox, DualSense, Switch Pro, 8BitDo, and more. Just like an Xbox or PlayStation console.

### Install (manual sideload)

Requires [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz). On the Deck: **Steam → Power → Switch to Desktop**, open **Konsole**, set a password with `passwd` if you haven't, then run:

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/steve133t/decky-wake-on-controller/releases/latest/download/wake-on-controller.zip \
  -o /tmp/wake-on-controller.zip && \
sudo unzip -o /tmp/wake-on-controller.zip -d /home/deck/homebrew/plugins/ && \
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

Return to Gaming Mode → open **Wake on Controller** in Quick Access (⚡) → toggle **Enable BT Wake** on.

### Setup
1. Pair your controller in Steam's Bluetooth settings
2. Enable BT Wake in the plugin
3. Put the Deck to sleep, press the controller's home button — it wakes and reconnects

See the [README](https://github.com/steve133t/decky-wake-on-controller#readme) for full details and troubleshooting.

koua29/savewaypoint.name: v0.2.0 — Sync your non-Steam saves to your own GitHub
koua29/savewaypoint.body:
First stable release. SaveWaypoint finds the game saves nothing else is backing up — emulators, GOG/itch titles, anything you added to Steam as a non-Steam shortcut — and syncs them to a **private repo on your own GitHub account**. No server of ours, no subscription, and because every backup is a commit, your version history comes free.

### What it does

- **Finds saves on its own.** Known emulator locations, plus a scan of Proton prefixes. Each entry is rated by what is actually in the folder: 🟢 detected (a `SaveGames` folder or `.sav` files are there), 🟡 probable, 🔴 nothing saved yet.
- **Leaves Steam games alone.** Steam Cloud already syncs them and a second writer racing it helps nobody, so they are filtered out — switchable, for the games Cloud does not cover.
- **Signs in from your phone.** GitHub device flow: the Deck shows a short code, you approve it on your phone. No keyboard, no browser on the handheld.
- **Test before you trust it.** Checks a save can be archived *and* written back, without uploading anything.
- **Restore any earlier backup** from the commit history.
- **Updates itself**, on a stable or beta channel.

### Getting started

1. Create a GitHub OAuth App and tick **Enable Device Flow** (see the README).
2. Paste its Client ID, press **Connect GitHub**, approve on your phone.
3. **Manage saves…**, switch on what you want, then **Back up now**.

### Known limitation

Backing up is proven on a Steam Deck and the archives were verified to hold real save data. **Restoring has not yet been exercised on a device.** The code path is tested, but before you rely on it, do a dry run: back up a save, then restore the copy you just made.

### Install

Download `SaveWaypoint.zip` below, then on the Deck in Desktop mode:

```bash
unzip -o SaveWaypoint.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```
